podman run --rm -d --name litellm-local \
  -p 4000:4000 \
  -v $(pwd)/config/local_dev.yaml:/app/config.yaml:Z \
  -v $(pwd)/hooks:/app/litellm_hooks:Z \
  -e STORE_MODEL_IN_DB=true \
  -e LITELLM_MASTER_KEY=sk-05132025 \
  registry.adeoaiengine.ecouncil.ae/openinnovationai/platform/mlops/mlops-serving/litellm-src:jya0-v1.96.2 \
  --config /app/config.yaml --port 4000

# Wait for startup, then verify
curl -s http://localhost:4000/health/liveliness
curl -s http://localhost:4000/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-05132025"

# Verify the fix is baked into the image
podman exec litellm-local grep -c "skip_in_memory" \
  /app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/common_utils/user_api_key_cache.py
# Expected: 10

podman exec litellm-local grep -c "skip_in_memory" \
  /app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/auth/handle_jwt.py
# Expected: 3

# Clean up
podman rm -f litellm-local

Alternatively, use the Makefile target for interactive testing (with --detailed_debug):

make litellm-local-docker

Or run from the local venv (no Docker, faster iteration):

make litellm-local-run

docs.title: Step 2: Push the Image to Harbor
docs.text:
# Login to Harbor (one-time per session)
make login

# Push the tagged image
make litellm-src-push

Or build and push in one step:

make litellm-src-build-push

docs.title: Step 3: Deploy to the Cluster
docs.text:
The deployment manifest (deploy/base/gateway) already references the correct image tag. If the tag in the manifest matches what you pushed, you only need a rollout restart to pull the new image:

# Verify the manifest image tag matches what you pushed
kubectl get deploy litellm-proxy -n adeo-litellm \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}'
# Expected: .../litellm-src:jya0-v1.96.2

# Trigger a rolling restart (maxUnavailable: 0, so one pod at a time)
kubectl rollout restart deploy/litellm-proxy -n adeo-litellm

# Wait for the rollout to complete
kubectl rollout status deploy/litellm-proxy -n adeo-litellm --timeout=300s

# Verify both new pods are running
kubectl get pods -n adeo-litellm -l app=litellm-proxy

# Verify the fix is in the deployed pods
NEW_POD=$(kubectl get pods -n adeo-litellm -l app=litellm-proxy \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
kubectl exec -n adeo-litellm $NEW_POD -- grep -c "skip_in_memory" \
  /app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/common_utils/user_api_key_cache.py
# Expected: 10

If the manifest image tag needs updating (e.g. new branch), edit deploy/base/gateway and apply:

kubectl apply -k deploy/overlays/prod

docs.title: Step 4: Verify the Fix in the Cluster
docs.text:
Port-forward to individual pods for multi-pod testing:

# Get the new pod names
POD1=$(kubectl get pods -n adeo-litellm -l app=litellm-proxy \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}')
POD2=$(kubectl get pods -n adeo-litellm -l app=litellm-proxy \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[1].metadata.name}')

# Port-forward to each pod on separate local ports
kubectl -n adeo-litellm port-forward pod/$POD1 4001:4000 &
kubectl -n adeo-litellm port-forward pod/$POD2 4002:4000 &

# Run the multi-pod test loop (see Phase 2 Multi-Pod Test Plan above)

Alternatively, test against the cluster ingress:

curl -sk https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/health/liveliness
curl -sk https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/models \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-05132025"

docs.title: Quick Reference: All Makefile Targets
docs.text: Target Description make litellm-src-build Build the LiteLLM source image from the repo root Dockerfile make litellm-src-push Push the image to Harbor (requires make login first) make litellm-src-build-push Build then push in one step make litellm-local-run Run from local venv (no Docker, fastest iteration) make litellm-local-docker Run the built Docker image locally (interactive, with debug) make litellm-local-stop Stop a locally-running Docker container make login Login to the Harbor registry make deploy Apply the k8s manifests to the cluster

docs.title: Same-Origin Client Distribution — Design Plan
docs.text:
Status: design, single plan of record. This folder describes serving cc-switch-cli and its install chain from the OICM gateway, so a locked-down developer machine whose only reachable host is litellm.ecouncil.ae can go from bare OS to a configured coding agent with one command and zero external network access.

The previous design (uv + Python + litellm[cli] + the lite CLI) is superseded and archived in history/lite-cli-PLAN.md. It is kept for context only; nothing below depends on it.

Everything here is designed against the current source tree (jya0-v1.102.0) and reuses existing upstream components wherever they exist.

docs.title: The one-paragraph design
docs.text: /install serves a generated bash script. It downloads the cc-switch static binary from the gateway mirror, prompts for the user's gateway virtual key and validates it against /v1/models, asks which harness(es) to configure, then uses cc-switch to register our gateway as a provider and write each chosen harness's native config file. No uv, no Python, no wheelhouse, no lite CLI, no login step — the user already holds their key.

docs.title: Why cc-switch over the lite CLI
docs.text:
• Harness coverage. cc-switch writes native config for 7 harnesses (claude, codex, gemini, open-code, hermes, open-claw, pi). lite only ever configured claude and codex; opencode/pi got an ephemeral env var, never a real opencode.json.
  • One static binary. No Python runtime, no uv bootstrap, no wheelhouse, no managed-CPython mirror. The mirror shrinks from ~1 GB to ~35 MB.
  • It already solved the hard part. cc-switch is a maintained provider-config engine with per-harness adapters, backup/restore, and idempotent-ish reconcile. We adopt it instead of hand-building the same in lite.

docs.title: The decisions that shape it
docs.text:
1. Everything under /install. One prefix for the user and the firewall. Public reads (the script, the manifest, the cc-switch archives) and the admin write surface (/install/admin/*) all nest under it.
  2. The bootstrap template is baked into the gateway image. RustFS holds versioned binaries + the manifest, never the shell developers pipe into sh. Store compromise then cannot become arbitrary code execution on developer machines (see security.md).
  3. The manifest is the client's integrity source of truth. Admin sync verifies upstream's checksums.txt at ingest and records the verified hash in the manifest; the client checks downloads against the manifest only.
  4. cc-switch releases are immutable + versioned. A cc-switch/<version>/<file> object, once published with a given sha256, is never overwritten with different bytes. The manifest publishes with a generation/ETag so concurrent admin syncs cannot clobber each other.
  5. One command is both install and resync. Re-running /install re-validates the key and re-syncs the provider's model list. Harness model lists are not live-read; reconciliation is explicit.
  6. Harness configure is per-harness, not one loop. claude/codex/gemini are switch-mode (field flags); open-code/pi/hermes/open-claw are additive (raw --config). See installer-script.md.
  7. First release certifies claude, codex, open-code. gemini/hermes/ open-claw/pi are added after their config semantics are E2E-tested against our gateway; we do not advertise untested harnesses.
  8. /install is the authoritative update channel. cc-switch's own update command points at public GitHub and is not used here.
  9. No upstream contribution. Proprietary, jya0- branches only. The drop-detection tests matter because we maintain the fork ourselves.
  10. No harness mirroring. cc-switch writes a harness's config; it never installs the harness. Users install Claude Code / OpenCode through their own channels.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: Developer machines inside the firewall can reach litellm.ecouncil.ae (443) and nothing else. The upstream cc-switch install flow assumes unrestricted egress (GitHub releases). We mirror the binaries and serve the whole chain same-origin.

docs.title: Reading order
docs.text:
• architecture.md — the slice, the route map, the flow
  • installer-script.md — the four steps + the generator contract
  • mirror-content.md — bucket layout + manifest schema 5
  • security.md — threat model, trust split, credential state
  • admin-sync.md — the operator's sync loop
  • platform-matrix.md — the four supported targets
  • deployment.md — env vars + rollout
  • rollout.md — pilot + GA
  • open-questions.md — deferred extensions

docs.title: Admin Sync API
docs.text: The admin must be able to fill and repair the artifact store from a machine with internet access. This doc defines the REST surface for that: push, upsert, or delete artifacts idempotently, over the gateway, with no kubectl, no mc, and no direct object-storage access.

docs.title: Why the API, not direct RustFS access (Conflict A resolution)
docs.text:
The alternative was to have the admin point mc / the S3 API straight at RustFS. Rejected: that desyncs the manifest from the objects, because the manifest's shape, the hash-on-write check, and the "publish only if every referenced object exists" invariant are logic that RustFS does not provide. Two writers (the admin's mc and any future tooling) would each have to reimplement that logic, and would drift.

So the admin talks to the slice, and the slice talks to RustFS. One place enforces the invariants. The gateway is the only thing with RustFS credentials; the admin only ever holds the LiteLLM master key.

docs.title: Why on the gateway
docs.text: The slice already runs inside the app, so the admin API is a second router in the same module. It reuses the admin-auth pattern OICM already uses: dependencies=[Depends(user_api_key_auth)] plus a _require_admin check against LitellmUserRoles.PROXY_ADMIN — see litellm/proxy/oicm_routes.py (_require_admin) for the precedent. The gateway's master key authenticates as a proxy admin, so the admin's existing bearer token works with no new credential type.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
All under /install/admin/v1/*, admin-only. Nested under /install per decision 1, but kept on its own sub-path so the ingress can restrict writes by network range without touching public reads.

Method Path Purpose GET /install/admin/v1/manifest Read the current manifest (admin view, includes hashes) PUT /install/admin/v1/artifact/{path} Upsert one artifact; body = raw bytes; idempotent PUT /install/admin/v1/manifest Upsert the manifest atomically; idempotent DELETE /install/admin/v1/artifact/{path} Delete one artifact; idempotent GET /install/admin/v1/inventory List stored objects + sizes + hashes

PUT semantics are upsert: writing the same bytes twice is a no-op and succeeds. The slice computes the sha256 on write (streaming into RustFS) and compares; if the stored object already matches, it returns 200 with "unchanged": true and writes nothing. That is what makes re-running the sync idempotent.

docs.title: Request/response shape
docs.text:
PUT /install/admin/v1/artifact/{path} takes the raw bytes as the body (Content-Type: application/octet-stream), not multipart, so a plain curl --data-binary @file works and the slice streams to RustFS without buffering the whole artifact in memory (the Python artifacts are tens of MB).

Always send the explicit header. curl defaults a --data-binary body to Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded, which sends auth down Starlette's form parser (request.form()); the form parser consumes the ASGI stream, and the handler's request.body() then fails with RuntimeError: Stream consumed (an opaque 500). With application/octet-stream, auth pre-reads and caches the body and the handler reads it from cache.

// 200 response
{"path": "cc-switch/5.11.1/cc-switch-cli-linux-x64-musl.tar.gz", "sha256": "...", "size": 8960000, "unchanged": false}

The manifest PUT validates the JSON against the schema in mirror-content.md and verifies every referenced object exists in the bucket with a matching hash. A manifest that points at a missing or mismatched object is rejected 409. This keeps the invariant that the manifest never lies about the store.

docs.title: Immutability + manifest compare-and-swap
docs.text:
• Immutable artifacts. A cc-switch/<version>/<file> object, once published with a given sha256, is never overwritten with different bytes. The slice enforces this: a PUT whose bytes hash differently from the existing object at that path is rejected 409. A new build gets a new version path, so "same path, different content" cannot happen.
  • Manifest compare-and-swap. The manifest PUT takes the current manifest's ETag as an If-Match precondition. Two concurrent admin syncs cannot silently clobber each other: the second PUT fails 412 and must re-read, re-merge, and retry. This replaces "last write wins" for the manifest, which could drop a concurrently-published artifact reference.

docs.title: Idempotent sync flow for the admin
docs.text:
KEY="$LITELLM_MASTER_KEY"                     # from the Secret, never in a file
BASE=https://litellm.ecouncil.ae

# 1. push every artifact (upsert; unchanged ones cost one hash, no write)
for f in $(find ./mirror -type f ! -name manifest.json); do
  rel="${f#./mirror/}"
  curl -fsS -X PUT "$BASE/install/admin/v1/artifact/$rel" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
    --data-binary "@$f"
done

# 2. publish the manifest last, atomically
curl -fsS -X PUT "$BASE/install/admin/v1/manifest" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @./mirror/manifest.json

# 3. verify
curl -fsS "$BASE/install/admin/v1/inventory" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"

Properties:

  • Order-independent for artifacts, manifest last. Artifacts can be pushed in any order and re-pushed freely; only the manifest publish is the commit-point, and it refuses to publish unless everything it references is present and hashes match.
  • Resumable. A dropped connection mid-upload leaves the store consistent (the object either landed fully or not at all); re-running the loop re-uploads only what changed.
  • Deletion is explicit. Removing an object is a DELETE; the manifest must be re-published afterward or the delete is rejected while the manifest still references it.
  • No partial state visible to users. Public reads proxy from the same bucket; because writes are atomic per object, a user never sees a half-written artifact.

docs.title: Concurrency
docs.text: Artifacts are immutable and content-addressed by version+path, so two admins pushing the same version push the same bytes — no conflict. The manifest is guarded by the compare-and-swap precondition above, so a concurrent publish cannot silently drop another sync's references. The one interleaving still worth guarding is "A publishes a manifest, B deletes an object A's manifest references" — the delete route re-checks the current manifest and rejects the delete with 409 if it is still referenced. Resolve by publishing a manifest that drops the object, then deleting.

docs.title: Security notes
docs.text:
• Admin-only via _require_admin (the oicm_routes.py precedent), which rejects anything that is not PROXY_ADMIN with 403.
  • Path parameters are validated: no .., no absolute paths, no escaping the mirror prefix. The handler normalizes the key against the bucket prefix and rejects anything that escapes it, so the write API cannot touch other buckets (notably not litellm-logs).
  • The write surface is separate from the public read surface (/install/admin/* vs the rest of /install/*), so an ingress rule can restrict it to an admin network range.
  • Size limits: a per-request body cap (reject 413 above it) so a runaway client cannot fill the bucket in one request.

docs.title: Architecture (v5 — gateway slice, cc-switch configurator)
docs.text:
Revision 5. The installed client is cc-switch-cli (a single static Rust binary), not the lite Python CLI. The end user already holds an admin-issued gateway key, so there is no lite login step and no uv/Python/ wheelhouse mirror tier. The mirror carries only the cc-switch binaries, the installer, and a provider preset. Harness configuration (including a real ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json) is written by cc-switch, which supports 7 harnesses; lite only configured claude and codex.

Revision 4. Storage moved from a PVC to a cluster-internal RustFS instance (see rustfs.md), which removes the multi-replica problem. All routes nest under /install. /install is unauthenticated.

docs.title: Host model
docs.text:
litellm.ecouncil.ae:443
                          │
                   nginx ingress (unchanged)
                          │  /  ->  litellm-proxy:4000
                          │
                 litellm gateway pod (unchanged deployment)
                          │
        ┌─────────────────┼──────────────────────┐
        │                 │                      │
        ▼                 ▼                      ▼
   /v1/*, /ui       /install/*               RustFS (cluster-internal)
   (upstream,       (slice: generated          rustfs.adeo-litellm:9000
    unchanged)       script + proxied           buckets: client-mirror, logs
                     artifact reads +
                     /install/admin/* writes)

No ingress changes. The existing Prefix / rule delivers /install/* to the gateway; the slice registers the routes and proxies artifact reads to RustFS. RustFS has no ingress and is reached only over the cluster network.

docs.title: Why in-app (unchanged from v2, still the core decision)
docs.text:
• Uniformity. One deployment, one ingress rule, one thing to monitor.
  • The gateway has memory. /install is generated by code that reads general_settings, the request host, and the manifest, so the script always carries the gateway's own canonical base URL.
  • Upstream precedent. The app already mounts StaticFiles for /ui and /swagger, and OICM already serves an APIRouter slice (litellm/proxy/oicm_routes.py) pinned by drop-detection tests. This is the same pattern again.
  • The slice is the RustFS boundary. It does not implement object-storage semantics (RustFS does); it adds auth, path containment, hashing, and manifest consistency, which RustFS cannot.

docs.title: Route map (all under /install)
docs.text:
Route Auth Mechanism Content GET /install none router handler, generated POSIX bootstrap script GET /install/manifest.json none router handler -> RustFS version/hash manifest GET /install/cc-switch/<file> none router handler -> RustFS cc-switch release archive / install.sh / checksums GET /install/providers/adeo/<harness>/v<N>.json none router handler -> RustFS (baked fallback) versioned per-harness cc-switch preset (canonical shape, sentinels only) * /install/admin/* PROXY_ADMIN router handlers -> RustFS write surface (see admin-sync.md)

The whole surface is one prefix, so the firewall allows litellm.ecouncil.ae and nothing else, and a single ingress rule covers it. The admin sub-path is still separable at the ingress if you later want to restrict writes by network range.

One consequence to state plainly: because everything shares /install, the public reads cannot be firewalled separately from the admin writes by prefix alone. If that ever matters, split /install/admin into its own ingress rule; it is one path, not a redesign.

docs.title: The slice
docs.text:
litellm/proxy/client_distribution/
├── __init__.py          ← re-exports router
├── routes.py            ← APIRouter: /install, /install/*, /install/admin/*
├── generator.py         ← pure script generator (manifest + base URL -> text)
└── storage.py           ← thin S3 client helper shared with the logging config
  • routes.py builds a standalone APIRouter and lazily imports proxy_server globals inside handlers, matching voice_routes.py / oicm_routes.py.
  • Wiring is one line in proxy_server.py next to the existing mounts: app.include_router(client_distribution.router).
  • Drop-detection tests in tests/unit/proxy/test_oicm_drop_detection.py pin the wiring so an upstream merge that clobbers the line fails a test.
  • No StaticFiles mount this time: reads are proxied from RustFS by a handler, because the bytes live in a bucket, not a directory. (That is the one place v4 diverges from v2's mechanism.)

docs.title: The full first-run flow
docs.text:
curl -fsSL https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/install | sh
        │
        ▼
  [install script]                    (runs on the dev machine)
        │  uname -s, uname -m, libc detect (MINGW/MSYS -> windows archive)
        │  GET /install/manifest.json
        ▼
  install cc-switch  ──── GET /install/cc-switch/cc-switch-cli-<target>.tar.gz
        │   (mirror of the upstream per-platform release archive + checksums)
        ▼
  cc-switch -> ~/.local/bin/cc-switch
        ▼
  prompt for the user's admin-issued API key
        ▼
  diagnostic: GET <base>/api/v1/models with that key   (abort if it fails)
  -> key-scoped model list, each entry with its real context_length
        ▼
  list the harnesses cc-switch supports; user picks which to configure
  (multi-select, NOT all-by-default — the user may keep a non-gateway config
   for a harness they do not pick)
        ▼
  for each chosen harness:
        read the pinned preset (path, sha256) from the manifest
        GET /install/providers/adeo/<h>/v<N>.json, verify sha256,
        compose with jq (sentinel substitution: base URL + key + models,
        per-model context windows, the manifest's max_output_tokens cap)
        provider add --config-file --overwrite
            (id = adeo-litellm-<last4 of the key>: one stable id per key,
             re-runs overwrite it in place via the fork's upsert flag)
        cc-switch use <id> --app <h>    -> writes that harness's config file
        ▼
  done

The installer is a generic orchestrator: it knows no per-harness JSON shape, and every harness (claude, codex, gemini included) goes through the same preset + compose + --config-file path. Each harness's cc-switch config structure lives in its own versioned preset slice, pinned by the manifest, so revising one harness touches nothing else.

No authentication is needed to download the binary or read the manifest. The user's key is only used for the /api/v1/models diagnostic and to fill the provider's apiKey field. cc-switch writes each selected harness's native config file; harnesses not selected are left untouched.

docs.title: Sizing and isolation
docs.text:
• No volume in the gateway pod. The gateway holds no artifact bytes; it streams them from RustFS per request, so pod memory is unaffected by artifact size.
  • RustFS is cluster-internal, no ingress, NetworkPolicy allowing only the gateway. Single-node StatefulSet + PVC (see rustfs.md).
  • Multi-replica: no longer a constraint. RustFS is shared, so the gateway can scale out freely. (Open question 8 is resolved and removed.)

docs.title: What stays untouched upstream
docs.text:
• cc-switch: byte-identical upstream release archives (mirrored), never rebuilt.
  • The coding harnesses themselves: installed by users through their own channels; cc-switch writes their config.
  • The proxy's config, auth, model list, routing: unchanged apart from the one router include line the drop test pins.

docs.title: Deployment (v4 — gateway slice, RustFS backend)
docs.text: v4: no artifact pod, no ingress changes, no PVC. Artifacts live in a cluster-internal RustFS instance (rustfs.md); the gateway proxies reads and writes to it.

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
1. RustFS. One StatefulSet + PVC in adeo-litellm, S3 API on rustfs.adeo-litellm.svc.cluster.local:9000, two buckets (litellm-client-mirror, litellm-logs). No ingress, NetworkPolicy allows only the gateway. Full detail in rustfs.md.
  2. Gateway pod change. No volume. Just env vars for the RustFS endpoint and credentials (secretKeyRef), added to the existing Deployment next to the other secret-backed env vars.
  3. Slice wiring. The proxy_server.py line pinned by the drop-detection test (see architecture.md): app.include_router(...). Rides the normal image build.
  4. Admin sync API. The write surface in admin-sync.md, which talks to RustFS on the admin's behalf.

No new ingress. No volume mount. No CronJob.

docs.title: Gateway env additions
docs.text:
# in deploy/base/gateway/proxy/deployment.yaml, alongside existing env
- name: RUSTFS_ENDPOINT_URL
  value: "http://rustfs.adeo-litellm.svc.cluster.local:9000"
- name: RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY
  valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials, key: access-key}}
- name: RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY
  valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials, key: secret-key}}

The slice's storage.py helper and the (later) s3_callback_params both read these names, so the endpoint and credentials have one source of truth. See rustfs.md for the DRY rationale.

If RustFS is unreachable, the slice returns 503 on artifact reads and the admin API, and the gateway still boots and serves /v1 — the same "gateway never depends on the artifact store" rule, now with RustFS as the dependency instead of a volume.

docs.title: Filling the store: the admin sync API
docs.text:
The admin runs the idempotent push loop from admin-sync.md on a machine with internet access: fetch the pinned cc-switch archives, verify each against upstream's checksums.txt, PUT each artifact under its versioned path, then PUT the manifest last. The gateway hashes on write and skips unchanged objects, so re-running is cheap and safe. The gateway writes to the litellm-client-mirror bucket; the admin never touches RustFS directly.

The fetch script itself lives in examples/ per the layer's doc conventions (runnable things are not docs), and follows the repo's CI supply-chain rules (download to file, verify checksum, never curl | bash, pin by full URL + version).

docs.title: Rollout sequence
docs.text:
1. Phase 0 proof still applies as written in rollout.md — the containerized --network none test of the install chain does not involve the cluster.
  2. Deploy RustFS + buckets + NetworkPolicy + the credentials Secret.
  3. Add the gateway env vars and roll out the image that includes the slice wiring.
  4. Admin syncs the artifacts via the API.
  5. Verify from the workstation: curl -fsSL https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/install returns the generated script; curl -fsSL .../install/manifest.json returns the manifest.
  6. Pilot: 2-3 internal users run the full journey.
  7. Fix what the pilot surfaces; announce; retire hand-rolled setup scripts.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Remove the gateway env vars and/or the slice wiring line -> /install/* 404s; nothing else in the gateway is affected. The drop test trips on this state by design.
  • Installed clients keep working: lite talks only to /v1; a client whose mirror disappears is fully functional, it just cannot update.
  • Store rollback: publish the previous manifest (the race-guard retention keeps it briefly); the next /install run pins users to the older version.
  • Bucket loss: re-run the admin sync loop; the API's idempotency means no partial-state cleanup is needed.

docs.title: Scaling note
docs.text: The multi-replica constraint from v3 is gone. RustFS is shared, so the gateway can scale out without an RWX PVC or baked-in artifacts. The admin write path is a single master-key caller, so concurrent gateway replicas reading from RustFS is the normal object-storage case, not a coordination problem.

docs.title: Implementation Plan
docs.text: v6 pivot (2026-10-14): cc-switch-cli replaces the lite CLI. The served client is now the cc-switch static binary, not the uv-installed lite Python CLI. The uv / wheelhouse / managed-Python mirror tiers and the lite login step are dropped. See PLAN.md (single plan of record) and history/lite-cli-PLAN.md for the superseded design.

docs.title: Milestone boundaries
docs.text:
DONE (kept, reused by the cc-switch design)
────────────────────────────────────────────
RustFS deployment (per-environment)
S3 storage wrapper (storage.py)
/install read routing (public artifact GETs)
/install/admin authenticated write surface
Jinja2 open-context generator

REVALIDATE / REPLACE (the lite-era results do not carry over)
────────────────────────────────────────────
artifact population   -> cc-switch archives, not uv/python/wheels
manifest schema       -> schema 5 (cc_switch_version + cc_switch_artifacts + harnesses)
installer template    -> generic orchestrator, store-served + baked fallback
harness presets       -> versioned providers/adeo/<h>/v<N>.json slices (all 7 harnesses, schema 5)
platform matrix       -> 4 musl/universal targets
security model        -> trust split, credential perms, no self-update
end-to-end tests      -> redo against cc-switch

NEW RELEASE GATE (cc-switch)
────────────────────────────────────────────
cc-switch v5.11.1 mirrored + manifest published
clean-machine install (egress blocked)
gateway-key validation diagnostic
claude config verified
codex config verified
open-code config verified
second /install run is a no-op (idempotent reconcile)
gateway model add/remove + resync
gateway key with restricted models
rollback (config restore) test
public internet fully blocked
-> prod

The old lite/uv Phases 1-3 map to the DONE block. The old Phase 4/5 (uv artifact population, lite e2e) do not count as done for the cc-switch architecture — they are replaced by the REVALIDATE and NEW RELEASE GATE blocks above. The phase text below is the lite/uv history, retained for reference; the cc-switch work is tracked against the gate. Phase 5 surfaced and fixed two mirror bugs: the pinned Python is now 3.13.12 / build 20260303 / install_only_stripped (uv 0.10.9's actual metadata), and a PEP 503 wheelhouse index route backed --find-links (since removed with the rest of the lite/uv tier). Next: Phase 6 (the one clean prod apply). Step-by-step build order for the v4 design (PLAN.md, architecture.md, rustfs.md, admin-sync.md).

Everything below is grounded in the current source tree and the live adeo-litellm namespace as of 2026-10-12:

  • Gateway image: registry.adeoaiengine.ecouncil.ae/openinnovationai/platform/mlops/mlops-serving/litellm-src:jya0-v1.102.0
  • deployment/litellm-proxy runs 2 replicas (this matters: the object store backend is what makes multi-replica safe; a ReadWriteOnce PVC would have blocked this)
  • Ingress litellm-proxy serves both hosts, Prefix / -> litellm-proxy:4000, TLS via litellm-ecouncil-ae-tls (dash-named secret)
  • No object store deployed yet in adeo-litellm; no NetworkPolicy objects exist in the namespace at all
  • Secrets in-cluster: litellm-master-key (prod) and litellm-master-key-dev (dev mounts this one, verified live) — the admin sync key therefore differs per environment
  • Pod labels (verified live): prod app=litellm-proxy, dev app=litellm-proxy-dev — usable as NetworkPolicy selectors
  • Slice pattern precedent: litellm/proxy/oicm_routes.py, wired at proxy_server.py:18897-18899 in a fork-appended block, pinned by tests/unit/proxy/test_oicm_drop_detection.py

docs.title: The operating rule: everything lands on dev first
docs.text:
Nothing touches prod until dev is fully verified. Concretely:

  1. Every phase below runs against the dev overlay (make litellm-src-release-dev, kubectl apply -k deploy/overlays/dev) and against the dev Deployment (litellm-proxy-dev) only.
  2. Dev is proven by living with it: run the whole flow (install, login, configure, agent turns) on dev, and let it soak until there is confidence in the configuration.
  3. No shadow commands. Nothing is fixed or created by hand in the cluster (kubectl exec, mc mb ad hoc, hot patches, imperative edits). Every change lands as an idempotent manifest in git, so the deployed state is always reproducible from kubectl apply. The one exception in this plan is one-shot bucket creation, which is itself a manifest (a Job with mc mb --ignore-existing, so it is idempotent and re-runnable from git, not a hand command). Where an object has a Kubernetes immutability limit that a plain re-apply cannot cross (a Job's spec.template), the recovery is written down next to the object rather than performed by hand: see "Idempotency and re-apply" in Phase 1.
  4. Once dev is verified and the manifests are known-good, prod gets one round of clean kubectl apply -k deploy/overlays/prod (plus the ImagePull restart the Makefile performs). No incremental prod changes, no prod-specific hand edits: prod receives exactly the bytes dev validated.

Why this is safe here: dev and prod share the same image tag (litellm-src:$(LITELLM_SRC_TAG), per the Makefile caveat), so the dev build already carries the prod payload; the prod rollout only pins the manifests and restarts. The slice itself is additive (one router include), so the prod apply is one atomic, revertible change.

Phases are ordered so each one is independently verifiable and the dev gateway never serves a broken /install at any point. Phases 1-5 are dev-only. Phase 6 is the single prod cut-over.

docs.title: Phase 1 — object store deployment (no code, no risk, DEV)
docs.text:
Goal: a running S3-compatible store with both buckets, reachable only from the gateways. Deployed to the namespace now, but nothing consumes it until Phase 3 wires the slice; the dev gateway gets env vars first, prod's are added only at Phase 6.

Backend: RustFS, not MinIO. MinIO Community Edition is end of life. The minio/minio GitHub repo was archived read-only in April 2026, the Docker Hub images were deleted in September 2026, and quay.io refuses anonymous pulls. There is no pullable minio/minio at any version, so the v4 doc's docker.io/minio/minio:RELEASE.2026-04-01T00-00-00Z was never obtainable. RustFS (Apache-2.0, actively maintained) is the replacement, and it is S3-compatible, which is the only contract LiteLLM needs: the logging path builds a stock boto3.client("s3", endpoint_url=...) (litellm/integrations/s3.py:74) and the v2 path hand-rolls SigV4 over raw HTTP against {endpoint}/{bucket}/{key}. Neither has any MinIO-specific code.

Pinned image, already mirrored into Harbor (public rustfs project):

registry.adeoaiengine.ecouncil.ae/rustfs/rustfs:1.0.1
sha256:38fcb422c93174dada595d1aedec0e942a16a2a01a0ecca896c4a563e1f463b5

Everything below was verified by running that exact image locally as a non-root, read-only-rootfs container: it starts standalone, /health and /health/ready both return 200, boto3 S3v4 path-style put/get/list/multipart all work, mc mb --ignore-existing succeeds and is re-runnable, and a bucket re-create returns success rather than an error.

One store per environment, not a shared one. Dev and prod share the adeo-litellm namespace, so a single unsuffixed store would give both gateways the same StatefulSet, PVC, credentials, and buckets, and a dev sync could write prod's data. So the store is per-environment, exactly like the gateway: the base in deploy/base/rustfs/ is prod's store verbatim, and the dev overlay (deploy/overlays/dev/rustfs/) renames everything to -dev, re-labels it, and replaces the credentials and bucket names. Dev therefore has its own rustfs-dev StatefulSet, data-rustfs-dev-0 PVC, litellm-rustfs-credentials-dev Secret, and litellm-client-mirror-dev / litellm-logs-dev buckets, and a rustfs-dev NetworkPolicy that admits only litellm-proxy-dev and the dev store's own pods. Prod's is the symmetric shape without the suffix.

The label handling is the subtle part, and the reason a plain nameSuffix is not enough:

  • nameSuffix renames objects but rewrites no label or selector, so on its own the dev StatefulSet would still carry and select app: rustfs (prod's value) and cross-select prod's pods in the shared namespace.
  • A labels transformer cannot fix it, because it would also rewrite the NetworkPolicy's ingress from podSelector to the store's own label and break the allow rule (verified: from ended up rustfs-dev, allowing only the store to reach itself).
  • So the store's label is spread by a kustomize replacements to exactly the sites that carry it (the StatefulSet and Service labels/selectors, the NetworkPolicy podSelector, and the bootstrap Job's own label), and the NetworkPolicy's from gateway label is patched per environment. The store and its bootstrap Job share one label, so one from rule admits both.

The dev parity test pins all of this: each prod store object must have a suffixed dev counterpart, the dev store and Service must carry the dev label, the credentials and bucket names must differ, and the NetworkPolicy must select its own environment's store and gateway.

New manifests: the base store in deploy/base/rustfs/rustfs.yaml and the dev-only overrides in deploy/overlays/dev/rustfs/. This is the object set, and it is what is applied to the cluster; kubectl apply -k deploy/overlays/dev is the only write path, so nothing here is created by hand.

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials, namespace: adeo-litellm}
type: Opaque
stringData: {access-key: ..., secret-key: ...}   # generate, never commit real values
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
metadata: {name: rustfs, namespace: adeo-litellm, labels: {app: rustfs}}
spec:
  serviceName: rustfs
  replicas: 1
  selector: {matchLabels: {app: rustfs}}
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: rustfs}}
    spec:
      securityContext: {runAsUser: 10001, runAsGroup: 10001, fsGroup: 10001, fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch}
      containers:
        - name: rustfs
          image: registry.adeoaiengine.ecouncil.ae/rustfs/rustfs:1.0.1
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          securityContext:
            {readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, runAsNonRoot: true, allowPrivilegeEscalation: false,
             capabilities: {drop: [ALL]}}
          env:
            - {name: RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY, valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials, key: access-key}}}
            - {name: RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY, valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials, key: secret-key}}}
            - {name: RUSTFS_VOLUMES, value: "/data"}
            - {name: RUSTFS_ADDRESS, value: "0.0.0.0:9000"}
            - {name: RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE, value: "false"}
            # The image bakes RUSTFS_OBS_LOG_DIRECTORY=/logs and a read-only rootfs
            # cannot create it, which is a FATAL startup error. An explicit empty
            # value routes logs to stdout (verified: "OBS log directory not
            # configured and logs outputs to stdout").
            - {name: RUSTFS_OBS_LOG_DIRECTORY, value: ""}
          ports: [{name: endpoint, containerPort: 9000}]
          readinessProbe: {httpGet: {path: /health/ready, port: endpoint}, initialDelaySeconds: 10, periodSeconds: 5, timeoutSeconds: 3}
          livenessProbe: {httpGet: {path: /health, port: endpoint}, initialDelaySeconds: 30, periodSeconds: 10, timeoutSeconds: 3}
          resources: {requests: {cpu: 100m, memory: 256Mi}, limits: {cpu: "1", memory: 1Gi}}
          volumeMounts: [{name: data, mountPath: /data}]
  volumeClaimTemplates:
    - metadata: {name: data}
      spec:
        accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
        storageClassName: longhorn-crypto-global   # existing class, referenced not created
        resources: {requests: {storage: 10Gi}}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata: {name: rustfs, namespace: adeo-litellm, labels: {app: rustfs}}
spec: {selector: {app: rustfs}, ports: [{name: endpoint, port: 9000, targetPort: endpoint}]}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata: {name: litellm-rustfs-bootstrap, namespace: adeo-litellm}
data:
  bootstrap.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
    set -eu
    : "${RUSTFS_ENDPOINT_URL:?}"; : "${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY:?}"; : "${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY:?}"
    i=0
    until mc alias set rustfs "$RUSTFS_ENDPOINT_URL" "$RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY" "$RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
      i=$((i + 1))
      [ "$i" -ge 30 ] && { echo "rustfs not reachable after 30 attempts" >&2; exit 1; }
      echo "waiting for rustfs (attempt $i)"; sleep 2
    done
    for bucket in litellm-client-mirror litellm-logs; do mc mb --ignore-existing "rustfs/$bucket"; done
    mc ls rustfs
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata: {name: litellm-rustfs-bootstrap, namespace: adeo-litellm, labels: {app: litellm-rustfs-bootstrap}}
spec:
  backoffLimit: 6
  ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 3600
  template:
    metadata: {labels: {app: litellm-rustfs-bootstrap}}
    spec:
      restartPolicy: Never
      securityContext: {runAsNonRoot: true, runAsUser: 65532, runAsGroup: 65532, fsGroup: 65532}
      containers:
        - name: mc
          image: registry.adeoaiengine.ecouncil.ae/minio/mc:latest
          command: [/bin/sh, /scripts/bootstrap.sh]
          env:
            - {name: RUSTFS_ENDPOINT_URL, value: "http://rustfs.adeo-litellm.svc.cluster.local:9000"}
            - {name: RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY, valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials, key: access-key}}}
            - {name: RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY, valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials, key: secret-key}}}
            - {name: MC_CONFIG_DIR, value: /tmp/.mc}
          volumeMounts: [{name: script, mountPath: /scripts, readOnly: true}]
      volumes:
        - name: script
          configMap: {name: litellm-rustfs-bootstrap}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata: {name: rustfs, namespace: adeo-litellm}
spec:
  podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: rustfs}}
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
    - from:
        - podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: litellm-proxy}}
        - podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: litellm-proxy-dev}}
        - podSelector: {matchLabels: {app: litellm-rustfs-bootstrap}}
      ports: [{protocol: TCP, port: 9000}]

Four things about that spec, each verified:

  • RUSTFS_OBS_LOG_DIRECTORY must be set empty. The image's own ENV sets it to /logs, and with readOnlyRootFilesystem: true telemetry initialization fails hard ([FATAL] Observability initialization failed: ... Read-only file system (os error 30)) and the container exits 1. Empty is the clean fix; the alternative is an emptyDir at /logs, which works but emits a permission warning and needs a second volume.
  • No /tmp or other writable mount is needed. Verified running with a read-only rootfs and only /data mounted.
  • No imagePullSecrets. Kyverno's add-image-pull-secrets ClusterPolicy injects registry-credentials into every pod in this cluster, which is why no existing manifest declares it either.
  • The storage class is referenced, not created. longhorn-crypto-global is an existing encrypted, Delete-reclaim class; this manifest creates no StorageClass. It was chosen over the cluster default longhorn-crypto-retain so a deleted StatefulSet does not leak its volume. Because the manifest is shared, prod binds the same class.

The Job and the NetworkPolicy are the two pieces that keep the deployment reproducible:

  • The bootstrap Job is required, not optional: RustFS has no MINIO_DEFAULT_BUCKETS equivalent, so this is the only way the buckets get created. It runs the mc client (already in Harbor at registry.adeoaiengine.ecouncil.ae/minio/mc:latest, sha256:512a1cb685940ded1b0ff55470a226a3830e16305a3e0f1bfbb77056171601fd), which works unchanged against RustFS. Readiness is gated on mc alias set (which fails loudly, exit 1, when the endpoint is not up) rather than mc ready, which was observed to exit 0 even against a dead endpoint and is therefore not a usable gate. runAsUser: 65532 is pinned because the mc image runs as root by default and would otherwise trip runAsNonRoot; mc runs correctly as any non-root uid.
  • The NetworkPolicy (the first in this namespace) allows ingress to app: rustfs port 9000 only from the prod and dev gateway pod labels (both verified live) plus the bootstrap Job's label. This manifest is shared by dev and prod by design: the object store is a common dependency, and the policy covering both labels is what makes the Phase 6 prod apply a no-surprise diff.

docs.title: Idempotency and re-apply
docs.text:
kubectl apply -k deploy/overlays/dev is safe to run any number of times. kubectl diff -k deploy/overlays/dev exits 0 against the applied state, so a re-apply changes nothing semantically.

  • The Secret and the StatefulSet report configured on every apply (the API server normalizes a couple of fields), but the diff is empty, so it is metadata-only and not drift.
  • The Job is the one object with a caveat: a Job's spec.template is immutable. If the bootstrap script in the ConfigMap changes, the apply fails with field is immutable. The documented recovery is delete-then-apply in the same round: kubectl -n adeo-litellm delete job litellm-rustfs-bootstrap then re-apply. ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 3600 reaps the completed Job after an hour, so once the script is stable a routine re-apply needs no delete. That TTL matches the repo's other Jobs (deploy/oicm/provision-alain.yaml).
  • Bucket creation itself is idempotent independently of the Job lifecycle: mc mb --ignore-existing succeeds on an existing bucket, and RustFS's own duplicate-bucket response is success, not error.

Steps (all dev-scoped verification; this is what was run):

  1. Generate credentials; commit the Secret manifest following the same convention as litellm-master-key.yaml in this private repo.
  2. kubectl apply -k deploy/overlays/dev (the overlay includes base/shared), then verify: kubectl -n adeo-litellm rollout status statefulset/rustfs, the Job completes, and the Job's log lists both buckets.
  3. Verify isolation: from a pod in another namespace, the S3 endpoint must NOT be reachable; from a litellm-proxy-dev pod, it must.

Exit: RustFS ready, both buckets exist (created by the Job, not by hand), gateway-only reachability confirmed. Prod is untouched: the shared manifest is in git, but deploy/overlays/prod has not been applied and no env var points prod at RustFS yet.

docs.title: Phase 2 — the slice (code, unit-tested, not yet wired)
docs.text:
Goal: litellm/proxy/client_distribution/ exists, fully tested, not yet mounted. Environment-neutral: code and tests only, nothing applied anywhere.

Files, following the oicm_routes.py structure exactly:

litellm/proxy/client_distribution/
├── __init__.py        ← re-exports router
├── routes.py          ← APIRouter + all handlers (public reads, generated /install, admin writes)
├── generator.py       ← pure function: manifest + base_url -> script text
└── storage.py         ← boto3/botocore client factory reading the shared env vars

Key implementation points, each grounded in what exists:

  • storage.py reads RUSTFS_ENDPOINT_URL, RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY, RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY (new env vars added in Phase 3). boto3 is already a litellm main dependency (pyproject.toml: boto3>=1.43.1,<2.0), so no new dependency. Use the BaseAWSLLM-free simple path: a plain boto3.client("s3", endpoint_url=...) created once per worker, matching how litellm/integrations/s3.py builds its client from params.
  • routes.py:
  • GET /install — unauthenticated; calls generator.render(...); returns text/x-shellscript with Content-Type: application/x-sh. Source of base_url: LITELLM_PUBLIC_BASE_URL env (add in Phase 3) with request-host fallback.
  • GET /install/{path:path} — unauthenticated proxy read from RustFS (get_object, stream). 404 if absent, 503 if RustFS is down. Content types by extension (.json, .tar.gz, .zip, .whl, .sha256).
  • * /install/admin/v1/* — dependencies=[Depends(user_api_key_auth)] + _require_admin copied from the oicm_routes.py precedent (LitellmUserRoles.PROXY_ADMIN check). Handlers: manifest GET/PUT, artifact PUT (stream to RustFS, sha256 on the fly, skip-if-same), artifact DELETE (409 if manifest-referenced), inventory GET.
  • Path containment: normalize the key against litellm-client-mirror/ and reject escapes (cannot touch litellm-logs).
  • generator.py: pure, no FastAPI imports. The template is a Jinja2 document rendered with a structured context (RenderContext: base URL, versions, platforms list) built from manifest schema 2. Rendered with SandboxedEnvironment(autoescape=False, undefined=StrictUndefined), so a template referencing an undefined variable fails /install loudly (500) rather than shipping a broken script. The template keeps only the three origin modifications from installer-script.md; resume is a version-check short-circuit (--force is idempotent) with no install_state.json state machine, and harness detection is removed (the lite CLI owns that).
  • Follow repo code conventions: Final annotations, frozen dataclasses, MappingProxyType, typed everything, no Any. # noqa only with named rule + reason.

Tests (co-located, mirroring tests/unit/proxy/client_distribution/):

  • test_generator.py — render with a known manifest + base URL; assert the three origin overrides, the lite config set line, that no upstream URL (astral.sh, github.com, pypi.org) appears, and the Jinja2 contract: undefined variable raises, no HTML escaping of shell metacharacters, a {% for %} loop over platforms, and store/baked-in templates render identically.
  • test_routes.py — handler-level tests with a stubbed storage layer (dependency-injected, not monkeypatched, per repo rules): unauth GET works; admin routes 403 for non-admin; manifest PUT rejects a manifest referencing a missing object (409); artifact PUT is idempotent (second identical PUT -> unchanged: true); DELETE rejects while manifest-referenced; path escape rejected.
  • Drop-detection additions to tests/unit/proxy/test_oicm_drop_detection.py: test_client_distribution_router_mounted_on_app (route paths present), test_client_distribution_module_has_router (router non-empty). Pattern copied verbatim from test_voice_routes_router_is_mounted_on_app.

Exit: all tests green locally (python -m pytest tests/unit/proxy/client_distribution/ -q and the two new drop tests).

docs.title: Phase 3 — wiring (one block, both env vars, DEV FIRST)
docs.text:
Goal: the slice mounts on the app; the dev gateway can reach RustFS.

  1. proxy_server.py: add to the fork-appended block (after line 18899, next to the oicm_status_router include):
# OICM same-origin client distribution (/install). Co-located vertical slice.
from litellm.proxy.client_distribution.routes import router as client_distribution_router

app.include_router(client_distribution_router)
  1. Env vars, split by the parity-test rule above:
# BASE deployment (deploy/base/gateway/proxy/deployment.yaml) — prod values;
# dev overlay overrides each one with its own endpoint, Secret, and bucket:
- name: RUSTFS_ENDPOINT_URL
  value: "http://rustfs.adeo-litellm.svc.cluster.local:9000"
- name: RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY
  valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials, key: access-key}}
- name: RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY
  valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials, key: secret-key}}
- name: RUSTFS_BUCKET
  value: "litellm-client-mirror"

# DEV overlay (deploy/overlays/dev/gateway/deployment.yaml) — overrides the
# base's prod values with dev's own store, plus the per-environment base URL:
- name: RUSTFS_ENDPOINT_URL
  value: "http://rustfs-dev.adeo-litellm.svc.cluster.local:9000"
- name: RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY
  valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials-dev, key: access-key}}
- name: RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY
  valueFrom: {secretKeyRef: {name: litellm-rustfs-credentials-dev, key: secret-key}}
- name: RUSTFS_BUCKET
  value: "litellm-client-mirror-dev"
- name: LITELLM_PUBLIC_BASE_URL
  value: "http://localhost:14001"   # dev is reached via port-forward

The parity test is the tripwire for this split. oicm-litellm-layer/tests/deploy/test_dev_prod_parity.py fails if dev and prod drift in any way the overlay does not declare: env vars present in only one environment must be added to _DEV_ONLY_ENV_VARS / _PROD_ONLY_ENV_VARS with a reason, and value differences to _EXPECTED_ENV_DIFFS. It also fails on stale declarations, so every move between phases must update the test in the same commit.

The clean split, given the per-environment store:

  • RUSTFS_ENDPOINT_URL / RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY / RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY / RUSTFS_BUCKET go in the base deployment with prod values (base IS prod). The dev overlay overrides each one with dev's own endpoint, Secret, and bucket name. All four are declared in _EXPECTED_ENV_DIFFS.

  • LITELLM_PUBLIC_BASE_URL is dev-only for now (declared in _DEV_ONLY_ENV_VARS). At Phase 6 it gets its prod value (https://litellm.ecouncil.ae) in the prod overlay and moves to _EXPECTED_ENV_DIFFS.

  • Release to dev: make litellm-src-release-dev (builds litellm-src:$(LITELLM_SRC_TAG), pushes to Harbor, pins the base image, and rolls out only the dev Deployment; prod keeps serving its already-running containers — that is the documented behavior of the target). CAUTION from the Makefile: dev and prod share the same image tag, so this build overwrites the bytes behind the tag for both; the dev-only rollout is what keeps prod untouched.

Verify (dev only):

curl -fsSL <dev-host>/install                      # generated script
curl -fsSL <dev-host>/install/manifest.json       # 404 until Phase 4, but route resolves
kubectl -n adeo-litellm logs deploy/litellm-proxy-dev | grep -i "client_distribution" | head

The dev host is reachable via port-forward per the datasource runbook (kubectl -n adeo-litellm port-forward deploy/litellm-proxy-dev 14001:4000) or via its ingress host if one is wired; confirm which before running the curls.

Exit: /install serves the generated script on dev; empty store 404s on artifact reads, not on the script itself. Prod untouched.

docs.title: Phase 4 — artifact sync (populate the store, shared but keyed to dev first)
docs.text:
Goal: the buckets contain the mirror content.

The store is shared (one RustFS instance, both gateways can read it), but the sync writes are made through the dev gateway's admin API so the write path itself is what gets exercised and verified.

The fetch script lives in examples/ per layer conventions (runnable things are not docs): oicm-litellm-layer/examples/client-distribution/sync-mirror.sh.

Run on this workstation (internet access):

  1. Fetch uv 0.10.9 release artifacts + .sha256 sidecars for the 8 platform-matrix.md targets from the astral-sh/uv GitHub release; verify each checksum.
  2. Resolve the litellm[cli] closure at the gateway's version (litellm_cli_version == gateway version per decision 7): uv tool install 'litellm[cli]==1.102.0' into a scratch venv, copy the wheels out of uv's cache (uv cache dir), or uv pip compile equivalent.
  3. Fetch the python-build-standalone archives for the pinned CPython (3.13.9) matching the pinned uv's expectations.
  4. Fetch the uv installer script itself (https://astral.sh/uv/0.10.9/install.sh), checksum it.
  5. Compute sha256 for everything; write manifest.json per the schema in mirror-content.md.
  6. Push per the admin-sync.md loop against the dev gateway: artifacts first (PUT /install/admin/v1/artifact/...), manifest last (PUT /install/admin/v1/manifest). The bearer token is the dev master key (the litellm-master-key-dev Secret, verified live as the one litellm-proxy-dev mounts): read it at run time from the Secret, never hardcode it.

Supply-chain rules apply to the fetch script: download to file + verify SHA-256 before use; pin every tool by exact version + full URL; never curl | bash.

Exit: curl -fsSL <dev-host>/install/manifest.json returns the real manifest; inventory (with the dev key) lists all objects with matching hashes. Prod still serves nothing from /install because it has no env vars and no router wiring yet — by design.

docs.title: Phase 5 — end-to-end validation (DEV)
docs.text:
Goal: a clean machine installs lite with zero external egress, entirely against dev.

Per rollout.md Phase 0, hardened for this environment:

# On this workstation (which HAS internet, so use network isolation):
docker run -it --network none \
  -v /tmp/mirror-seed:/seed:ro \
  ubuntu:24.04 bash
# inside: curl against a localhost:8000 seed copy first (Phase 0 of rollout.md)

Full e2e against the dev gateway (workstation with HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:1 to fail-closed any accidental egress, or the port-forward):

curl -fsSL <dev-host>/install | sh
lite --version
lite login                       # or: --api-key from the env
lite configure claude            # or: lite opencode / lite codex
claude                           # a real turn through the dev gateway

Soak: per the operating rule, live with this on dev — repeat installs, re-runs (the resume/idempotency path), an update cycle (re-sync a manifest bump), wrong-key recovery — until the configuration is boring. Fix anything that surfaces by editing the manifests/code in git and re-applying to dev, never by hand-patching the cluster.

Exit: lite installs, authenticates, configures the harness, and a real agent turn routes through /v1 on dev with the user's key; --no-index resolution shows zero external requests; a re-run of /install is a no-op.

docs.title: Phase 6 — the one clean prod apply, then pilot and GA
docs.text:
Goal: prod receives, in one round, exactly what dev validated.

Pre-flight (all read-only):

kubectl kustomize deploy/overlays/prod | kubectl diff -k deploy/overlays/prod   # review: ONLY the expected delta
kubectl -n adeo-litellm rollout status deployment/litellm-proxy                  # prod healthy before

The single prod round (this is the entire prod change):

  1. Prod overlay gets its LITELLM_PUBLIC_BASE_URL value (https://litellm.ecouncil.ae), declared in _EXPECTED_ENV_DIFFS — or the existing dev declaration simply keeps covering it, since the test already expects that one value difference. The RUSTFS_* vars are already in the base (Phase 3), identical for both environments. The router include is already in the image bytes (same tag, from the dev build). So the actual prod delta at this point is: the prod LITELLM_PUBLIC_BASE_URL value (if not yet present), the image pin (if the tag moved), and nothing else.
  2. kubectl apply -k deploy/overlays/prod — one clean apply of the known-good manifests. This picks up: RustFS (already running, no-op diff), the NetworkPolicy (no-op, already applied with dev), the gateway env vars, and the image pin. Then kubectl -n adeo-litellm rollout restart deployment/litellm-proxy + rollout status (or make litellm-src-release once, which does build + pin + apply + restart in one step — but since the image is already pushed from the dev phase, the apply-and-restart alone is the cleanest single prod action).
  3. Verify prod: curl -fsSL https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/install, /install/manifest.json, and one full user journey (install -> login -> configure -> one agent turn).

If anything looks wrong in the kubectl diff pre-flight, stop: fix it in git, re-run the dev phases affected, and come back. Prod never gets an unverified delta.

Then pilot and GA per rollout.md: 2-3 internal users, one week, watch install success rate / keyring / PATH quirks / /v1 latency during parallel installs. Then announce with the two-command story and the cautious two-step form from security.md.

docs.title: Definition of done
docs.text:
• Phases 1-5 all green on dev, and dev has soaked (install, re-run, wrong-key recovery, update cycle)
  • The Phase 6 pre-flight diff showed only the expected delta; the single prod apply succeeded; prod serves the full flow
  • Drop-detection tests green in CI (test_oicm_drop_detection.py)
  • make check passes on the touched files (the repo-wide gate)
  • The mkdocs build renders this folder clean
  • A real user (you) has installed lite via https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/install and completed a real Claude Code / OpenCode turn through the prod gateway

docs.title: Rollback at every phase
docs.text:
• Phase 1: kubectl delete -k deploy/overlays/dev (or git-revert + apply); nothing consumes the RustFS objects yet. Deleting the StatefulSet does not delete its PVC (Kubernetes leaves volumeClaimTemplates PVCs in place), so the data survives; the class's Delete reclaim policy only applies if the PVC itself is deleted, which is a deliberate separate step.
  • Phase 2: pure code addition; revert the commit
  • Phase 3: revert the two-line wiring + env vars; the drop tests trip by design (that is the tripwire working). Re-apply the dev overlay.
  • Phase 4: the store being empty only 404s artifact reads; /install script itself still serves (it does not read the store to render). Delete objects via the admin API if a clean slate is wanted.
  • Phase 5: nothing to roll back on dev beyond Phase 3/4 reverts.
  • Phase 6: revert the base/overlay manifest edits and re-apply -k deploy/overlays/prod + rollout restart — prod returns to its pre-change state in one round, the same way it received the change. Installed clients keep working; lite talks only to /v1.

docs.title: The Served Install Script (/install)
docs.text:
Design rule: download one static binary, configure the user's harnesses with it, add nothing. The script installs cc-switch-cli (a single static Rust binary) from the gateway mirror and uses it to register our gateway as a provider and write the user's chosen harness config files. There is no uv, no Python, no wheelhouse, and no lite CLI.

The end user already holds an admin-issued gateway key, so there is no login step. cc-switch supports 7 harnesses (claude, codex, gemini, open-code, hermes, open-claw, pi) and writes each one's native config file — including a real ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json, which the retired lite CLI never did.

The script is not a static file: the gateway slice renders it at request time from a Jinja2 template and a structured context (base URL, adopted versions, platform list) built from manifest.json (see architecture.md and the generator contract below).

The script is served at GET /install and is unauthenticated: downloading the binary and reading the manifest need no credential. The user's key is prompted for interactively and used only for the /api/v1/models diagnostic and the provider's apiKey field. See security.md.

The steps below double as first install and reconciliation: the same /install run installs the binary if absent, then re-validates the key and re-syncs the provider + model list. One command, both jobs.

UX order: the key and harness prompts run first, so a bad key or a wrong pick fails fast before any download starts; the jq bootstrap, cc-switch install, and per-harness configure all run after the user has answered.

docs.title: 1. Prompt for the gateway key + diagnostic
docs.text:
The script prompts for the user's gateway virtual key (visible input, so a pasted key can be checked before Enter) and validates it before anything is installed. This is a per-developer virtual key, never the proxy master/admin key:

curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "$BASE_URL/api/v1/models?limit=2000" \
  > "$TMP/models.json" \
  || die "that key was rejected by $BASE_URL; check it with your platform admin"

A wrong key fails here, before any download begins and before any harness file is written. The endpoint is the OpenRouter-compatible models API: it is key-scoped (each user sees exactly their accessible models) and every entry carries its real context_length from live backend discovery, which feeds step 4.

The script filters the fetched list down to text-generation models by excluding utility families by name (embeddings, speech/STT/TTS/voice, OCR, transcribe, image generation, rerank, doc-layout, whisper) and UUID-named document-processing models. The payload carries no capability signal, so a name-based exclusion is the only available filter; it keeps every real coding model (GLM, Qwen, Kimi, DeepSeek, ...) rather than the old include-list, which silently dropped whole families.

docs.title: 2. Harness selection
docs.text: The script lists the harnesses cc-switch can configure and asks the user which to wire (numbered multi-select). Harnesses not picked are left alone — the user may already have a non-gateway config for one of them. The list is baked into the script at render time (the menu must appear before jq is bootstrapped, so it cannot parse the fetched manifest); it is sorted alphabetically so menu numbers stay stable across syncs, and adding a harness remains a store sync, not a script change.

docs.title: 3. Install: jq bootstrap, cc-switch
docs.text:
jq and cc-switch are installed from the gateway mirror only after the prompts are answered, so there is no download wait before the user has said anything. Both are sha256-verified against the manifest, the client-side source of truth for integrity (admin sync verifies upstream's checksums.txt at ingest time and records the verified hash in the manifest; see admin-sync.md):

VER="$CC_SWITCH_VERSION"   # rendered from the manifest
FILE="$(jq -r --arg t "$TARGET" '.cc_switch_artifacts[$t].file' "$TMP/manifest.json")"
WANT="$(jq -r --arg t "$TARGET" '.cc_switch_artifacts[$t].sha256' "$TMP/manifest.json")"
curl -fsSL "$BASE_URL/install/cc-switch/$VER/$FILE" -o "$TMP/ccs.tgz"
echo "$WANT  $TMP/ccs.tgz" | sha256sum -c -
tar -xzf "$TMP/ccs.tgz" -C "$INSTALL_DIR"

The script detects OS/arch/libc and downloads the matching archive from the immutable versioned path /install/cc-switch/<version>/. Musl builds (linux-x64-musl, linux-arm64-musl) are statically linked, so the binary runs on any libc. That is why there is no Python or uv tier at all. If cc-switch --version already matches cc_switch_version, the download is skipped. jq follows the same versioned-mirror flow under /install/jq/<version>/ (pins live in the script itself: reading them from the manifest would already require jq).

docs.title: 4. Per-harness provider reconcile
docs.text:
The script is a generic orchestrator: it embeds no per-harness JSON shape. For each chosen harness it reads the pinned preset (path, sha256) from the manifest's harnesses map, fetches /install/providers/adeo/<h>/v<N>.json, verifies its sha256 against the manifest, then composes the final config with one generic jq walk(): sentinels in the preset (__BASE_URL__, __BASE_URL_V1__, __API_KEY__, __DEFAULT_MODEL__, __DEFAULT_MODEL_CONTEXT__, __MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, the models placeholders below) are replaced with the gateway URL, the key, the key's model list, each model's real context window from step 2, and the manifest's default output cap. Every harness — claude, codex, gemini included — goes through the same provider add --config-file path; the config shape is entirely the preset's business, so revising one harness touches nothing else.

Per-model context lands wherever the harness has a real, verified knob; the preset picks the placeholder matching its shape:

Placeholder Composes to Used by ["__MODELS_ARRAY__"] [{id,name}] (v1 presets) — ["__MODELS_ARRAY_CTX__"] [{id,name,contextWindow?}] pi, open-claw ["__MODELS_ARRAY_CTX_SNAKE__"] [{id,name,context_length?}] hermes {"__MODELS_OBJECT__": null} {id:{name}} (v1 presets) — {"__MODELS_OBJECT_LIMIT__": null} {id:{name,limit:{context?,output}}} open-code {"__MODELS_CATALOG__": null} {models:[{model,displayName,contextWindow?}]} codex: cc-switch turns it into Codex's model_catalog_json plus a generated catalog file, the only way Codex's model picker learns the key's models (Codex has no model discovery)

A model whose context the gateway does not report simply omits the context key; for the single-model harnesses the compose drops the whole field: claude loses CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS, codex loses the entire model_context_window TOML line (a first-class supported state — cc-switch itself defaults the window to 128000 when the key is absent).

Output cap. The manifest carries max_output_tokens (default 65536, i.e. 64K). It is written into every harness that has a real output knob: claude's CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS env key and opencode's per-model limit.output. codex, gemini, pi, hermes and open-claw have no verified output-limit key (gemini's writer drops any env key outside its hardcoded allow-list, codex's config surface has no such TOML key), so their presets carry only the context. Changing the default is a manifest edit + re-sync, no gateway rebuild.

The key is passed via a --config-file under umask 077, never on the command line (argv is world-readable via /proc), and runtime values are merged with jq, never sed string substitution:

umask 077
# compose: jq walk() over the preset, sentinel substitution
jq 'walk(...) $PRESET > "$TMP/provider.json"

# One stable id per gateway key: its last 4 chars, lowercased and
# dash-stripped to satisfy cc-switch's id charset. Re-running the script
# refreshes the same provider in place via --overwrite (our cc-switch
# fork's upsert flag), so a rotated key or changed model list replaces
# the stored config; nothing piles up.
PROVIDER_ID="adeo-litellm-$(printf '%s' "$API_KEY" | tail -c 4 \
  | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | tr -d '-')"
cc-switch provider add --app "$HARNESS" --id "$PROVIDER_ID" \
  --name "ADEO LiteLLM" --config-file "$TMP/provider.json" --overwrite
cc-switch use "$PROVIDER_ID" --app "$HARNESS"    # the success gate
rm -f "$TMP/provider.json"

The --overwrite flag is the one fork-carried change in cc-switch (branch jya0-v5.11.1): stock provider add is insert-only and its only update path is the interactive edit prompt. With the flag, an existing id is updated in place through the same ProviderService::update the edit prompt uses; a nonexistent id fails loudly. The script also keeps a compat path: on a stock binary the duplicate-add error for an existing id is treated as the no-op it is (identical content), so the script still works un-patched, minus true refresh.

cc-switch use writes the harness's native config file (~/.config/opencode/opencode.json for open-code, ~/.claude/settings.json for claude — only once ~/.claude/ exists, ~/.codex/config.toml likewise: cc-switch writes lazily when the app's config dir is present, which is stock behavior identical with its own field-mode add). Verified against cc-switch-cli v5.11.1. After the loop the script runs cc-switch env check to surface any conflicting environment variables.

Revisions do not accumulate: one provider per harness per key, identified by the key's last 4 chars. Re-runs overwrite it in place (the fork's --overwrite), so there is no stale catalog row to clean up and no TUI housekeeping. A different key creates a different provider, which is the intended multi-key story.

docs.title: Generator contract (Jinja2, store-backed template)
docs.text:
The template is served from the object store (templates/install.sh.tmpl) when a copy exists, falling back to the copy baked into the gateway image (generator._TEMPLATE) when the store copy is missing or unreadable. The store copy is pushed through the admin-gated write API (PUT /install/admin/v1/artifact/templates/install.sh.tmpl, PROXY_ADMIN only), so iterating on the install flow is an admin sync, not an image rebuild. See security.md "What lives where".

The slice's /install handler renders the template with Jinja2. The template is a Jinja2 document, not a find-replace string, so it can grow conditionals and loops without the renderer changing.

The render context is open: every key in manifest.json is exposed to the template, plus base_url and the typed platforms / harnesses lists. The keys the template actually references:

Variable Type Source base_url str LITELLM_PUBLIC_BASE_URL env/config, request host as fallback cc_switch_version str manifest.json cc_switch_version max_output_tokens int (default 65536) manifest.json max_output_tokens platforms list of {target, archive_ext} manifest.json platforms harnesses list of {harness, version, path, sha256} manifest.json harnesses; the menu list is baked from it at render time

Rendering is sandboxed, strict, and not autoescaped (SandboxedEnvironment(autoescape=False, undefined=StrictUndefined)):

  • StrictUndefined — a template that references a variable we did not pass raises at render time. /install returns 500 with the error rather than serving a half-rendered installer to every client.
  • autoescape=False — shell metacharacters (&, <, >) are not turned into HTML entities.

The generator is pure (manifest + base URL in, script text out) and unit tested in the slice's co-located module: the cc-switch download, the manifest-hash verification, the harness-selection prompt, and the per-harness backup + delete-then-add + use sequence all have regression tests.

A template change is a gateway code change and ships with the image (code review + redeploy), so it is validated by the generator's unit tests before it ever reaches a developer.

docs.title: Harness configuration lives in cc-switch
docs.text: The script does not write harness config files itself and does not scan for harnesses. It offers the list cc-switch supports, the user picks, and cc-switch writes each chosen harness's native config. This replaces both the retired report-only "Detected harnesses" summary and the lite configure commands, which only ever covered claude and codex.

docs.title: Resume behaviour
docs.text:
Re-running is safe and cheap:

  • The cc-switch binary install is a version-check short-circuit; a matching cc-switch --version skips the download.
  • The provider reconcile is delete-then-add under a config backup, because provider add rejects a duplicate id and provider edit is interactive-only. cc-switch preserves unrelated keys in the harness config file across the use.
  • A wrong key is caught by the /api/v1/models diagnostic before any harness file is written, so a bad key never leaves a half-configured harness.

docs.title: Idempotency and model resync
docs.text:
1. Script fetches /install/manifest.json first.
  2. If cc-switch exists and matches the manifest's cc_switch_version, skip the download.
  3. Otherwise download + manifest-hash-verify + extract in place.

Model resync is explicit, not live. The harness does not continuously read /api/v1/models. When the gateway's model set changes, the user re-runs /install (or /install | sh -s -- --sync): the script re-fetches /api/v1/models with the key and re-writes each configured provider's model list and per-model context windows via the same overwrite reconcile, so one command covers both first install and resync.

Version policy: the mirror pins exactly one cc-switch version (cc_switch_version in the manifest). A bump re-pins it and the admin publishes the new archives; the outgoing set is retained until the new manifest is live, to cover a client mid-download.

docs.title: Codex's model catalog needs a daemon restart
docs.text:
Codex 0.165.0 keeps a managed app-server per CODEX_HOME and reads model_catalog_json once at startup. A catalog written by this installer therefore stays invisible to the interactive /model picker until that daemon restarts, even though codex exec -m <model> works immediately (it never consults the picker). Verified empirically: a home with a correct config and catalog still listed only the OpenAI built-ins until the daemon was stopped, then listed all seven gateway models.

This is why the closing message is more than "restart the harness". When codex was one of the chosen harnesses and a daemon is running, the script names the real fix: quit Codex, or pkill -f 'codex app-server'. The check is pgrep-guarded so a minimal host without pgrep never fails an install over a hint.

docs.title: Windows (Git Bash / WSL)
docs.text:
Native PowerShell /install.ps1 is deferred. Windows is supported through the shells that already ship bash:

  • Git Bash (ships with Git for Windows) and WSL both run the script unchanged.
  • Under Git Bash / MSYS, uname -s returns MINGW64_NT-... (or MSYS_NT-...), not Linux. The script maps MINGW* / MSYS* to the Windows cc-switch archive (windows-x64.zip).

docs.title: Failure modes the script must handle
docs.text:
• Mirror missing a platform archive -> clear message naming the exact URL that 404'd.
  • Checksum mismatch -> abort before extraction, "artifact store may be corrupt, contact platform team".
  • Key rejected -> abort at the diagnostic, before any harness file is written.
  • No curl -> the script cannot bootstrap; error says so.
  • No jq -> bootstrapped from the mirror (/install/jq/<version>/..., official jqlang static binaries, SHA-256 pinned in the script because reading the pin from the manifest would already need jq). Only dies if the mirror has no build for the platform.
  • No trusted CA roots (curl exit 60 or 77) -> the script names the OS package to install (apt-get install ca-certificates / apk add ca-certificates); a CA bundle cannot be fetched over TLS that itself needs the bundle.
  • RustFS unreachable -> the artifact fetch returns 503 from the slice; the script aborts with the URL, never falls back to the internet.

docs.title: Mirror Content — exact bytes we serve
docs.text:
Everything under the mirror is produced by the admin sync script (see admin-sync.md) on a machine that does have internet, then pushed into the cluster over the gateway's admin REST API into the RustFS bucket litellm-client-mirror. The dev machine only ever consumes, through the gateway.

Storage decision (v4): RustFS, a cluster-internal S3-compatible store in adeo-litellm. v3 chose a PVC; v4 moved to object storage because it removes the multi-replica constraint entirely and because LiteLLM already ships S3 logging support (integrations/s3.py, s3_v2.py) that can share the same instance. RustFS replaces the originally sketched MinIO because MinIO Community Edition reached end of life (repository archived, images deleted from Docker Hub). See rustfs.md.

One current version of everything. The mirror holds exactly one cc-switch version. One previous version set is retained only as a race guard: a client that started a download moments before a version swap should still be able to finish, so the swap keeps the outgoing set until the incoming one is fully published.

docs.title: Object layout in the bucket
docs.text:
litellm-client-mirror/
├── manifest.json
├── cc-switch/<version>/cc-switch-cli-<target>.<ext>
├── jq/<version>/jq-<platform>        # official jqlang static binaries
├── providers/adeo/<harness>/v<N>.json       # per-harness presets (all 7)
└── templates/install.sh.tmpl                 # optional store override

Served to clients as /install/manifest.json, /install/cc-switch/..., /install/jq/..., /install/providers/adeo/<harness>/v<N>.json.

docs.title: manifest.json
docs.text:
Single source of truth for versions and hashes, served at /install/manifest.json. It is fetched by the install script first, and its SHA-256 values are the client-side integrity source of truth: the install script verifies each downloaded archive against the manifest, not against a separately-downloaded checksums file. The gateway also reads it to build the install-script render context.

Schema 5 carries a platforms array so the install template can iterate the target matrix as data, a cc_switch_artifacts map of target -> file + sha256, a harnesses map pinning every harness to a versioned preset (no mode field: all harnesses compose the same way), and an optional max_output_tokens integer (default 65536): the per-request output cap the installer writes into harness configs that have a real output knob (claude CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS, opencode limit.output). Changing it is a manifest edit + re-sync, no gateway rebuild. There is no backwards compatibility with schema 4: the gateway accepts only schema: 5.

jq lives outside the manifest, pinned in the script itself. The install script needs jq to parse the manifest, so the jq version + per-platform SHA-256 digests cannot be read from the manifest (chicken and egg). They are literal pins in the template, mirrored by sync-mirror.sh from the official jqlang release (verified against the release's sha256sum.txt sidecar), and served at /install/jq/<version>/<file>.
