docs.title: Design Attributes
docs.text:
Custom voices can be designed by combining attributes:

{
  "instructions": "female,british accent,young adult,high pitch"
}

Or via the voice field:

{
  "voice": "design:female,british accent,young adult,high pitch"
}

Available attributes:

Category Options gender male, female age child, teenager, young adult, middle-aged, elderly pitch very low pitch, low pitch, moderate pitch, high pitch, very high pitch style whisper accent_en american accent, british accent, australian accent, chinese accent, canadian accent, indian accent, korean accent, portuguese accent, russian accent, japanese accent dialect_zh 河南话, 陕西话, 四川话, 贵州话, 云南话, 桂林话, 济南话, 石家庄话, 甘肃话, 宁夏话, 青岛话, 东北话

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
All errors return JSON with an error or detail field:

Status Code Meaning Example 400 Bad request (e.g. streaming with non-PCM format) {"detail": "Streaming only supports response_format='pcm'"} 404 Resource not found (profile, model) {"detail": "Profile 'my_voice' not found"} 405 Method not allowed {"detail": "Method Not Allowed"} 409 Conflict (profile already exists) {"detail": "Profile 'my_voice' already exists"} 413 Upload too large {"detail": "Upload too large: 30.0MB exceeds limit of 25MB"} 422 Validation error {"detail": "Unsupported voice value 'foo'..."} 500 Internal server error {"detail": "Synthesis failed: ..."} 503 Service unavailable (model loading / at capacity) {"detail": "Script synthesis at capacity"} 504 Request timeout {"detail": "Synthesis timed out after 120s"}

docs.title: Python Client Example
docs.text:
import requests

BASE_URL = "http://localhost:8080"
API_KEY = None  # Set if auth is enabled
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}"} if API_KEY else {}

# Basic synthesis
response = requests.post(
    f"{BASE_URL}/v1/audio/speech",
    headers={**headers, "Content-Type": "application/json"},
    json={
        "model": "omnivoice",
        "input": "Hello from Python!",
        "voice": "nova",
        "response_format": "wav",
    },
)
with open("output.wav", "wb") as f:
    f.write(response.content)

# Voice cloning (one-shot)
with open("reference.wav", "rb") as ref:
    response = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/v1/audio/speech/clone",
        headers=headers,
        data={
            "text": "This is cloned speech.",
            "ref_text": "The reference text.",
            "speed": "1.0",
        },
        files={"ref_audio": ref},
    )
    with open("cloned.wav", "wb") as f:
        f.write(response.content)

docs.title: OpenAI SDK Compatibility
docs.text:
The server is designed as a drop-in replacement for the OpenAI TTS API:

    base_url="http://localhost:8080/v1",

    voice="nova",
    input="Hello from the OpenAI SDK!",
)
response.write_to_file("output.wav")

docs.title: Drama 3 through the gateway: the three gaps, and who owns them
docs.text:
Status: fixed. The drama3 provider slice (litellm/llms/drama3) owns the TTS param surface and voice management, the create_voice route parses multipart, and the code smell detection pass (oicm-litellm-layer/docs/techniques/ code_smell_detection_technique.md) audited the slice after implementation. Written 2026-11-03.

Drama 3 is served by an sglang-omni pod that supports voice cloning, persistent voices, streaming, batch synthesis, and full sampling control. Through the LiteLLM gateway only default-voice non-streaming TTS and inline direction tags reach it. Three separate defects cause that, and all three are in this fork, not upstream.

docs.title: Ownership summary
docs.text:
Defect Layer Upstream or ours references, stream, top_k, seed, language dropped from TTS bodies litellm/main.py speech() optional-params assembly Upstream design, we just have no provider config to bypass it POST /v1/audio/voices multipart returns 500 litellm/proxy/voice_routes.py create_voice Ours, this route does not exist upstream POST /v1/audio/voices JSON returns 400 "not supported for provider=hosted_vllm" litellm/endpoints/voice/main.py Ours, base_llm/voice/ does not exist upstream

Upstream main has no litellm/proxy/voice_routes.py and no litellm/llms/base_llm/voice/, verified with git ls-tree -r --name-only upstream/main | grep -E "voice". Every voice-management route in this fork is local code.

docs.title: Defect 1: the TTS param whitelist
docs.text:
litellm/main.py speech() builds the outbound body from exactly three optional parameters:

optional_params = {}
if response_format is not None:
    optional_params["response_format"] = response_format
if speed is not None:
    optional_params["speed"] = speed
if instructions is not None:
    optional_params["instructions"] = instructions

Anything else you send is accepted, logged, and never forwarded. This is upstream behaviour, not a fork regression: upstream/main has the same three lines at litellm/main.py:9017.

What routes around it is ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_text_to_speech_config, which returns a BaseTextToSpeechConfig per provider. When a config is returned, speech() dispatches to it instead of the OpenAI branch, and the config owns map_openai_params, so it can forward whatever the upstream server accepts. This fork already uses that mechanism for OmniVoice, which forwards an arbitrary body via _collect_passthrough.

hosted_vllm has no entry in that dispatch table, so Drama 3 falls through to the OpenAI branch and inherits its whitelist.

docs.title: Defect 2: the multipart 500
docs.text:
litellm/proxy/voice_routes.py create_voice reads the body twice:

body = await request.body()
data = orjson.loads(body)

A multipart upload cannot be parsed as JSON, so the request fails with RuntimeError: Stream consumed and returns HTTP 500. The pod's own POST /v1/audio/voices is multipart by contract, so the two can never meet.

docs.title: Defect 3: the JSON path rejects the provider
docs.text:
Sending JSON instead reaches a different wall, in litellm/endpoints/voice/main.py:117:

litellm.BadRequestError: Voice management is not supported for provider=hosted_vllm

The voice subsystem dispatches through get_provider_voice_config, which returns a BaseVoiceConfig for HAMSA and OMNIVOICE only. hosted_vllm returns None.

So the gateway has two voice routers that both refuse this model, for different reasons.

docs.title: Why a custom provider is the right fix
docs.text:
The three defects have one shared shape: the gateway has a generic extension point per capability, and hosted_vllm is not registered in it. Drama 3 is not a hosted_vllm model in any meaningful sense. It is an sglang-omni TTS server with its own richer contract that happens to speak /v1/audio/speech.

Registering it as hosted_vllm was the reason the controller misclassified it as chat before the tier-0 fix, and it is the reason its body gets rewritten now.

docs.title: Proposed shape
docs.text:
A drama3 provider, following the existing oicm_providers slice:

litellm/llms/drama3/
  text_to_speech/transformation.py   Drama3TextToSpeechConfig
  voice/transformation.py            Drama3VoiceConfig

Drama3TextToSpeechConfig.map_openai_params forwards the nine fields the pod accepts (input stays in the body; references, top_k, top_p, temperature, max_new_tokens, stream, stream_format, repetition_penalty) and lets extra_body carry anything else, so a future pod field needs no gateway change.

Drama3VoiceConfig implements the multipart upload, list, and delete against the pod's own registry rather than the generic JSON acreate_voice action.

Two things to settle before building it:

  • The controller would need to register the model with the new provider instead of hosted_vllm. That is a provider change in the discovery controller, gated the same way the tier-0 task change was.
  • Streaming needs the gateway route to stop buffering. voice_routes.py's audio_speech already builds a StreamingResponse, so the buffering is likely in the OpenAI handler returning a complete HttpxBinaryResponseContent. Worth confirming before promising streaming in the same change.

docs.title: Cheaper alternative, if the custom provider is too much
docs.text: Register hosted_vllm in get_provider_text_to_speech_config with a config that forwards the body verbatim. That fixes defect 1 for Drama 3 and for every other self-hosted TTS server without a new provider enum, but leaves both voice-routers broken. It is a much smaller diff and covers the capability gap that actually matters to callers today (cloning and sampling), if not voice management.

docs.title: Current workaround
docs.text:
Call the pod directly. It needs no auth:

kubectl -n adeo port-forward deploy/j-51096511-94c6-4240-901a-86cccb5eb08a 8080:8080

docs.title: Piece not verified
docs.text: StreamingResponse exists at the route level, so the buffering may be removable without touching the OpenAI handler. Not investigated. Do not promise streaming until it is measured end to end.

docs.title: Drama 3 registration: why the mode is wrong and why fields are dropped
docs.text:
Status (2026-11-03): Defect 1 is FIXED and deployed. Both controllers run oicm-discovery-controller:0.1.0-20261103-4d922d8, and fishaudio/drama-3 registers as mode: audio_speech with oicm_task: Text-to-Speech and health_check_voice: default on prod and dev. The fix was not the chat-precedence change explored below: it came from OICM's declared inference_task, used as tier 0 with a mounted-surface gate. See CAPABILITY_REGISTRATION_REVIEW2.md. Defect 2 is FIXED too (2026-11-04): the drama3 provider slice (litellm/llms/drama3/) forwards the Drama 3 schema fields, verified live against dev with a 10-point sentinel suite. The exploration below is kept as the record of the root cause.

Two independent defects surfaced while writing the Drama 3 usage guide. They have different root causes and need different fixes, so they are recorded separately here.

The short version: openapi.json is read correctly. The controller's problem is the order in which it consults the paths it reads. The dropped fields are a separate, gateway-side problem that no amount of controller work will fix.

docs.title: Defect 1: mode is chat because chat is checked first
Evidence
docs.text:
Run against the live pod's actual openapi.json:

CHAT_PATH present : True
TTS_PATH present  : True
detected mode     : chat -> litellm: chat
detected provider : hosted_vllm

detect_mode_from_paths in controller/models.py:211 short-circuits at line 229:

if CHAT_PATH in paths:
    return "chat"

The pod exposes /v1/chat/completions because sglang-omni serves the whole omni surface, so chat wins and /v1/audio/speech is never considered. The probe itself is fine; only the precedence is wrong for this class of pod.

docs.title: Second, latent bug in the same table
docs.text:
Even if the chat short-circuit were removed, the mode would still be wrong. Feed the same paths through the table:

what the TTS branch WOULD return if chat did not win:
    audio_transcription

_PATH_MODES (controller/models.py:185) lists TRANSCRIPTION_PATH before TTS_PATH, and the table returns its first hit. This pod exposes both /v1/audio/transcriptions and /v1/audio/speech, so it resolves to audio_transcription.

This is the same class of bug the existing comment already documents for diarize versus transcription ("Diarize before transcription: a coro pod serves both surfaces"). That fix ordered one pair correctly and left the next pair exposed. Any pod that serves transcriptions and TTS hits it.

docs.title: Consequence
docs.text:
The model registers as mode: chat, so:

  • POST /v1/chat/completions reaches the pod and fails with Drama 3 request: the speech input must be text or an object with text and references.
  • POST /v1/audio/speech still works, because routing resolves by model name and the registered api_base already ends in /v1.
  • Anything grouping models by declared mode (dashboards, capability filters, auto-routers) mislabels the model.

docs.title: Proposed fix
docs.text:
Not yet applied; this section is the design.

  1. Reorder the table so speech precedes transcription. Put TTS_PATH (and HAMSA_TTS_PATH) before TRANSCRIPTION_PATH. A pod exposing a speech endpoint is a speech model, for the same reason the diarize comment gives. Ordering by specificity rather than by historical accident is the general rule; _PATH_MODES should say so in a comment rather than rely on each pair being fixed when it bites.

  2. Stop letting chat unconditionally win. The current rule is deliberately conservative, and the docstring explains why: a chat server that also exposes a transcription endpoint must not be registered as an audio model, or every request 404s. The rule that preserves that intent while covering this pod is to check whether the chat path is actually usable. Two options:

  3. Path-ratio heuristic (cheap, no extra request). If the pod exposes chat plus exactly one audio surface and no streaming responses, prefer the audio mode. Fragile, because it infers intent from counts.

  4. Serve-intent probe (accurate, one extra request). Probe the pod's /v1/models for supported_task_types, which the controller already reads in _discover_model_ids. If the pod advertises speech only, register text_to_speech even when /v1/chat/completions exists. This is the option that matches what the pod actually declares rather than guessing from path shapes.

The probe-based option is preferable, and _probe_capability_facts already establishes the pattern for asking a pod what it can do.

  1. Add a regression test. controller/models.py has no test that a speech-only pod listing chat is classified as speech. The existing controller tests cover exclusions and deploy parity, not mode precedence, which is why this shipped.

docs.title: Is a new provider needed for the mode fix?
docs.text: No. Mode and provider are independent axes here, and the mode fix is entirely about path precedence. A provider entry would not change detect_mode_from_paths.

docs.title: Defect 2: request fields are dropped by the gateway, not the controller
Evidence
docs.text:
The same request, pod-direct versus through the gateway, using values the pod rejects outright:

Request Pod direct Gateway stream: true with response_format: "wav" 400 stream=true requires response_format='pcm' 200 audio/wav references → https://example.invalid/nope.wav 400 Could not resolve media URL hostname 200 audio/wav

The pod rejects both. The gateway returns audio, so the fields never arrive.

docs.title: Cause
docs.text:
detect_provider returns hosted_vllm, and get_provider_text_to_speech_config has no branch for it, so it returns None. litellm/main.py:8397 then takes its OpenAI TTS branch:

elif custom_llm_provider == "openai" or (
    custom_llm_provider in litellm.openai_compatible_providers
    and custom_llm_provider not in AZURE_OPENAI_AUDIO_PROVIDERS
    and text_to_speech_provider_config is None
):

That branch requires a string voice (hence the voice is required error on an otherwise valid Drama 3 request) and builds the upstream call from a fixed parameter set: model, input, voice, response_format, speed, instructions. The rest of **kwargs goes to logging. So references, stream, and any future model-specific field are dropped while the response looks perfectly valid.

docs.title: Would a Fish Audio provider fix this?
docs.text:
Yes, and this is the case where a provider is the right answer. A provider config would:

  1. Replace the OpenAI branch, removing the spurious voice requirement.
  2. Supply transform_text_to_speech_request, which returns a dict_body built verbatim, so references and stream reach the pod unchanged.
  3. Let get_supported_openai_params declare exactly what the pod accepts, so genuinely unsupported fields fail loudly instead of being silently discarded.

The base interface already supports all three; nothing needs inventing. BaseTextToSpeechConfig.transform_text_to_speech_request returns a TextToSpeechRequestData whose dict_body is forwarded as-is.

Registration would mirror the existing OICM slices:

  • litellm/llms/fishaudio/{text_to_speech/transformation.py, common_utils.py}
  • a FISHAUDIO member on litellm.LlmProviders
  • a branch in get_provider_text_to_speech_config in litellm/llms/oicm_providers/registry.py
  • "fishaudio" added to KNOWN_PROVIDERS in controller/models.py

One wrinkle worth deciding before implementation: detect_provider matches on a substring of owned_by or the model id. Here owned_by is sglang-omni and the model id is fishaudio/drama-3, so a "fishaudio" token would match the id. That works, but it means the provider is inferred from the checkpoint name rather than the serving software, which is exactly the ambiguity the TODO(future) in detect_provider already calls out. It also means any other sglang-omni-served TTS model needs its own entry rather than inheriting one.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Superseded. The ordered recommendation below was the first pass; FISHAUDIO_DRAMA3_ROBUST_FIX_DESIGN.md replaces it after live verification falsified parts of it (the pod publishes no supported_task_types, so the serve-intent probe had no data source, and VibeVoice-ASR shows the chat-first rule protects a real case). Kept for the record of what was considered.

Land them in this order:

  1. Provider slice for fishaudio (gateway). This is what restores streaming and voice cloning, which are the features people actually want from Drama 3. It also removes the voice requirement, which is the first thing every caller trips over.
  2. _PATH_MODES reorder (controller). Small, self-contained, and fixes the mislabel for every pod that serves both speech and transcription.
  3. Chat-precedence fix (controller). Needs the serve-intent probe and a careful test, because the current rule exists to prevent a real 404 failure mode. Do not weaken it without covering the transcription-with-chat case it protects. (Verification note: this probe cannot be built today; this pod publishes no supported_task_types. The robust-fix design replaces this step with a declared ConfigMap MODE override.)

Until step 1 lands, the usage guide documents the current behaviour accurately, so callers are not surprised by a 200 with the wrong audio.

docs.title: Drama 3 registration: a robust fix, and the patterns behind it
docs.text:
Superseded for the registration half by CAPABILITY_REGISTRATION_BY_PROBE.md. That document replaces the mode-detection ideas here (Patterns 2 and 3) with behavior probing, after verification showed path shape cannot distinguish VibeVoice-ASR (correctly chat) from Drama 3 (incorrectly chat). Pattern 1, the hosted_vllm TTS pass-through config, still stands and is now independent.

Follow-up to FISHAUDIO_DRAMA3_REGISTRATION_DIAGNOSIS.md. That document correctly identified the two defects but proposed detection heuristics as the fix. This one replaces those proposals with an established-pattern design, after live verification falsified part of the earlier plan.

docs.title: Why the earlier plan was not robust
docs.text: The diagnosis proposed a "serve-intent probe" reading supported_task_types from /v1/models. Verified live: this pod publishes no supported_task_types, and its /model_info carries engine counters only (request_backlog, tp_size, etc), no task metadata. A probe cannot read what the server does not publish. Path-shape heuristics were never going to be robust either: VibeVoice-ASR registers as chat correctly, because it is an ASR model served through the chat surface, while Qwen3-ASR registers as audio_transcription via the native surface. A path cannot tell those apart; only the deployment's declared intent can.

docs.title: The patterns, and where each one applies
Pattern 1 — Pass-through proxy (the openai route out of Drama 3's field drop)
docs.text:
The field drop is the classic gateway anti-pattern: the proxy understands too much, so any backend field it doesn't know about silently vanishes. Established remedy, used verbatim by AWS API Gateway's proxy integrations: the proxy forwards the request body uninterpreted and lets the authoritative server validate it ("adding a field needs no gateway change"). Postel's law: be conservative in what the proxy adds, liberal in what it forwards, and let the endpoint that owns the schema do the rejecting.

Applied here, minimal form: a per-modality pass-through TTS config for hosted_vllm, because sglang/vLLM-family serving stacks already speak the OpenAI speech shape natively, so any OpenAI-shaped TTS pod gets correct behavior without a per-checkpoint provider entry. Concretely:

  • litellm/llms/hosted_vllm/text_to_speech/transformation.py — HostedVLLMTextToSpeechConfig(BaseTextToSpeechConfig)
  • transform_text_to_speech_request returns dict_body built from model + input + every non-internal kwarg (the _collect_passthrough shape already exists in-house in litellm/llms/inception/text_to_speech/transformation.py:27 and litellm/llms/omnivoice/common_utils.py:69; hoist it to litellm/litellm_core_utils/llm_request_utils.py next to the existing serialize_multipart_form_fields rather than copying it a third time)
  • the entrypoint condition in litellm/main.py:8396 — custom_llm_provider in litellm.openai_compatible_providers and text_to_speech_provider_config is None — must narrow to exclude hosted_vllm once its config exists, otherwise the generic branch is never reached
  • the final dispatch tuple at litellm/main.py:8776 — the hardcoded ("hamsa", "inception", "omnivoice") allowlist — must gain "hosted_vllm" (and should be replaced by a membership test on a registry, not a literal tuple, so the next provider doesn't need a main.py edit)

End-to-end streaming is already plumbed and requires no new code, verified: the generic handler posts dict_body with stream=request_data["dict_body"].get("stream") is True (llm_http_handler.py:12296), the pod returns chunked PCM, HttpxBinaryResponseContent.aiter_bytes delegates to httpx's streaming iterator, and the proxy route already wraps the response in StreamingResponse(_audio_speech_chunk_generator(response), ...) (proxy_server.py:13061). A client's stream: true + pcm flows through untouched. No new proxy code needed for streaming delivery.

The voice requirement disappears as a side effect, because the config path replaces the OpenAI branch that imposed it.

What pass-through does not fix: the "unknown speech request field" errors the pod itself returns. That is the correct division of labor — the pod owns its schema, the proxy forwards, and a client sending style gets a loud 400 from the authority, not a silent 200 from the middlebox.

docs.title: Pattern 2 — Declarative reconciliation (declared intent beats inferred shape)
docs.text:
Kubernetes operator pattern: the controller's job is to reconcile observed state toward declared state, and where intent is ambiguous, the declaration wins, with detection as the fallback. The strongest form of declaration here already exists in the codebase's own conventions: the per-deployment ConfigMap (configmap-{uuid}-main), which the controller already reads for MODEL_ID and EXTRA_ARGS (local_deployments.py:122,173).

Add MODE as a read ConfigMap field with a documented enum:

MODE=audio_speech   # or chat, audio_transcription, diarization, ...

Detection order becomes: ConfigMap MODE override wins; otherwise fall back to today's detect_mode_from_paths. This is the same override philosophy as HEALTH_CHECK_MODELS-style knobs, and matches the operator best practice of "prefer what the workload declares over what a controller can infer".

Why not add supported_task_types publishing to the pod? It would be the most honest signal (the serving software computing its own capabilities), but it requires an sglang-omni upstream change, crossing a repo boundary this fix should not take on. The ConfigMap field is the in-boundary equivalent: a human declares intent once per deployment, at deploy time, which is when the human knows the intent.

docs.title: Pattern 3 — Drain the inferred-path swamp (mode detection ordering)
docs.text:
Declarative override first, but the fallback detection still exists, so order it by usefulness, not by historical accident. The current _PATH_MODES table maps paths to modes in the order they were added, so TRANSCRIPTION_PATH (added for Qwen3-ASR) precedes TTS_PATH (added later), and a pod exposing both resolves to audio_transcription. VibeVoice proves the reverse pair is equally real. The table should be ordered by the mode a client can actually call:

  1. TTS path present (and chat cannot usefully serve it) -> text_to_speech
  2. Transcription path present (and chat cannot usefully serve it) -> audio_transcription
  3. Diarize, OCR, embedding, rerank — unchanged
  4. Chat remains the default last resort

With the ConfigMap override as the primary mechanism and this table as fallback, the diarize-before-transcription comment (controller/models.py:188) becomes a historical note rather than load-bearing ordering.

docs.title: Pattern 4 — Reconcile drift, do not invent a new source of truth
docs.text: A design where the controller stamps mode from ConfigMap needs a drift rule or it creates a second source of truth: someone edits the ConfigMap, the next full sync stamps the new mode into the row, and nothing tells the operator the row drifted from the declaration. Operator practice: the reconciler PATCHes observed state toward declared state, and logs the transition. The controller already has this exact shape for model registration itself — _pick_richest_entry dedupes rows each 300s sync. Extend the same discipline to mode: the registered row's model_info.mode follows the ConfigMap on every full sync, with a one-line log when it changes.

docs.title: What this deliberately does not do
docs.text:
• No new fishaudio provider. The checkpoint name is not the serving contract; hosted_vllm is. Drama 3 is an OpenAI-speech-shaped pod behind hosted_vllm, exactly like its sglang/vLLM siblings. A per-checkpoint provider would need one entry per future TTS checkpoint and teaches the controller nothing general.
  • No capability probing of the chat endpoint. Sending synthetic traffic to a pod to guess its mode adds load, adds failure modes, and still guesses. The ConfigMap declaration is a human's answer, not an inference.
  • No touching the chat-first protection for VibeVoice-class pods. The chat-first rule protects a real case; the ConfigMap override is what handles Drama 3-class pods, so the heuristic never has to be weakened.
  • No upstream (sglang-omni) changes. Out of scope for a gateway-side fix; supported_task_types publishing is noted as the ideal future signal.

docs.title: Fix sequence
docs.text:
1. hosted_vllm pass-through TTS config (Pattern 1). Self-contained, restores stream + references + removes the voice requirement for every OpenAI-shaped TTS pod, and the streaming path is already fully plumbed. Test by replaying the §3 probe pairs from the usage guide: stream: true + wav must 400, invalid references must 400, and a streaming PCM request must arrive chunked.
  2. ConfigMap MODE + controller stamping (Patterns 2 + 4). Fixes the mislabeled chat mode for existing deployments (including Drama 3) without touching detection.
  3. _PATH_MODES reorder (Pattern 3). The residual ordering bug, ordered by usefulness once the override exists.

Each step is independently shippable and independently revertible, which is the property that makes the sequence robust rather than merely correct.

docs.title: Hamsa STT Research: Source Code Crawl, Protocol Analysis, and OpenAI Compatibility Assessment
1. K8s Access Commands
docs.text:
SSH tunnel to the K8s API server (needed before any kubectl command):

sshpass -p 'Password123' ssh -fN \
  -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o ServerAliveInterval=30 \
  -o ServerAliveCountMax=3 \
  -o ExitOnForwardFailure=yes \
  -L 6443:10.34.104.10:6443 \
  adeo@10.34.104.99

All kubectl commands use:

KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl ...

docs.title: 2. Hamsa Pod Discovery
docs.text:
Find the Hamsa STT pod:

KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl get pod -n adeo

Key identifiers:

Pod:      j-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231-8458b5c7b7-x8wbr
Service:  s-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231 (ClusterIP, namespace: adeo)
Endpoint: 10.42.8.132:8080
URL:      ws://s-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080

docs.title: 3.1 List the Hamsa app directory
docs.text:
KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl exec -n adeo \
  j-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231-8458b5c7b7-x8wbr -- \
  ls -la /app/app/

docs.title: 3.2 Read main.py (FastAPI app + routes)
docs.text:
KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl exec -n adeo \
  j-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231-8458b5c7b7-x8wbr -- \
  cat /app/app/main.py

docs.title: 3.3 Read ws_handler.py (WebSocket protocol + VAD)
docs.text:
KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl exec -n adeo \
  j-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231-8458b5c7b7-x8wbr -- \
  cat /app/app/ws_handler.py

docs.title: 3.4 Read auth.py (Fernet encryption)
docs.text:
KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl exec -n adeo \
  j-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231-8458b5c7b7-x8wbr -- \

docs.title: 3.5 Read .env (encryption keys + config)
docs.text:
KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl exec -n adeo \

docs.title: 4.1 REST /transcribe (from inside Hamsa pod)
docs.text:
KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl exec -n adeo \
  j-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231-8458b5c7b7-x8wbr -- \
  python3 -c "
import urllib.request, json, base64

with open('/app/test-adeo-30s.wav', 'rb') as f:
    audio_b64 = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode()

payload = json.dumps({
    'audio': audio_b64,
    'lang': 'auto',
    'eos_enabled': False,
    'threshold': 0.3
}).encode()

req = urllib.request.Request(
    'http://localhost:8080/transcribe',
    data=payload,
    headers={
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'x-api-key': 'gAAAAABo-1oxslqx1hGc8nGn_7iWiD0jwAGE7tDk3MgA-t_9gM05qFZIP1tTiBgJpDkTaTrf7OHe9RLj2AjspUYuKxAqVnPjIJ6AD6q-0E8paCMBreZ8pGc='
    }
)
resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req)
print(json.loads(resp.read()))
"

Result:

{
  "text": "السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته، اليوم الاربعاء الثامن عشر من ديسمبر 2025...",
  "gender": "Male",
  "eos": null,
  "processing_time": 1.088,
  "duration": 29.83
}

docs.title: 4.2 WebSocket /ws (from LiteLLM pod, with real-time pacing)
docs.text:
This was the critical test. Sending all chunks at once produces zero transcriptions because the VAD (Silero) expects streaming audio with natural speech/silence patterns. Adding a 100ms delay between chunks (simulating real microphone pacing) triggers the VAD correctly.

KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl exec -n adeo-litellm \
  litellm-proxy-57b4c9985d-6c8bx -- python3 -c "
import asyncio, websockets, json, wave, numpy as np

async def test():
    target = 'ws://s-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080/ws'
    upstream_api_key = 'gAAAAABo-1oxslqx1hGc8nGn_7iWiD0jwAGE7tDk3MgA-t_9gM05qFZIP1tTiBgJpDkTaTrf7OHe9RLj2AjspUYuKxAqVnPjIJ6AD6q-0E8paCMBreZ8pGc='

    async with websockets.connect(target) as ws:
        handshake = {
            'type': 'handshake',
            'api_key': upstream_api_key,
            'options': {
                'silence_timeout': 30,
                'sample_rate': 16000,
                'min_silence_duration_ms': 300,
                'min_speech_ms': 600,
                'client_logging': True,
                'vad_threshold': 0.3,
                'eos_enabled': True,
                'eos_threshold': 0.3,
                'audio_type': 'PCM',
                'noise_cancellation': False
            }
        }
        await ws.send(json.dumps(handshake))
        ack = await asyncio.wait_for(ws.recv(), timeout=10)
        print(f'Handshake ack received')

        with open('/tmp/test-adeo-30s.wav', 'rb') as f:
            with wave.open(f) as wav:
                sample_rate = wav.getframerate()
                n_frames = wav.getnframes()
                n_channels = wav.getnchannels()
                audio_data = wav.readframes(n_frames)

        # Resample 48kHz -> 16kHz using numpy interpolation
        audio_np = np.frombuffer(audio_data, dtype=np.int16).astype(np.float32)
        if n_channels > 1:
            audio_np = audio_np.reshape(-1, n_channels).mean(axis=1)
        if sample_rate != 16000:
            num_samples = int(len(audio_np) * 16000 / sample_rate)
            ratio = num_samples / len(audio_np)
            indices = np.arange(num_samples) / ratio
            audio_np = np.interp(indices, np.arange(len(audio_np)), audio_np)
        audio_int16 = audio_np.astype(np.int16)
        raw_pcm = audio_int16.tobytes()

        chunk_size = 3200  # 100ms of 16kHz 16-bit mono audio
        chunks = [raw_pcm[i:i+chunk_size] for i in range(0, len(raw_pcm), chunk_size)]

        async def send_audio():
            for chunk in chunks:
                await ws.send(chunk)
                await asyncio.sleep(0.1)  # CRITICAL: real-time pacing
            print(f'Sent {len(chunks)} chunks')

        async def receive_messages():
            transcriptions = []
            try:
                while True:
                    msg = await asyncio.wait_for(ws.recv(), timeout=20)
                    data = json.loads(msg)
                    if data['type'] == 'transcription':
                        transcriptions.append(data)
                        t = data['data'].get('transcription', '')
                        print(f'Transcription: {t!r}')
                    elif data['type'] == 'log':
                        print(f'Log: {data[\"data\"]}')
                    else:
                        print(f'Unknown: {data[\"type\"]}')
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                print('No more messages')
            print(f'Total transcriptions: {len(transcriptions)}')

        await asyncio.gather(send_audio(), receive_messages())

asyncio.run(test())
"

Result:

docs.title: 5.1 REST API: POST /transcribe
docs.text:
Auth: x-api-key header with Fernet-encrypted key value.

Request (JSON body):

{
  "audio": "base64-string-or-list-of-floats",
  "prompt": "optional context prompt",
  "lang": "auto",
  "eos_enabled": false,
  "eos_threshold": 0.3,
  "gender_detection": false,
  "speaker_identification": false,
  "wake_word": false,
  "threshold": 0.3
}

Response:

{
  "text": "transcribed text",
  "gender": "Male",
  "eos": null,
  "processing_time": 1.088,
  "duration": 29.83,
  "speaker_embeddings": null,
  "wake_word_match": null,
  "similarity_score": null
}

docs.title: 5.2 WebSocket API: WS /ws
docs.text:
Auth: api_key field inside the handshake JSON message (not HTTP headers). Value is the Fernet-encrypted key.

Protocol flow:

Client -> Server: handshake message (JSON, text)
Server -> Client: handshake_ack message (JSON, text)
Client -> Server: binary PCM audio chunks (or {"type":"media","payload":base64} text messages)
Server -> Client: transcription messages (JSON, text) - triggered by VAD
Server -> Client: log messages (JSON, text)
Server -> Client: error messages (JSON, text)

Handshake message:

{
  "type": "handshake",
  "api_key": "gAAAAAB...Fernet-encrypted...",
  "options": {
    "silence_timeout": 30,
    "sample_rate": 16000,
    "min_silence_duration_ms": 300,
    "min_speech_ms": 600,
    "client_logging": true,
    "vad_threshold": 0.6,
    "eos_enabled": true,
    "eos_threshold": 0.6,
    "audio_type": "PCM",
    "noise_cancellation": false
  }
}

Transcription message (server -> client):

{
  "type": "transcription",
  "data": {
    "transcription": "السلام عليكم",
    "gender": "Male",
    "eos": { "prediction": 1 },
    "speaker_info": null
  },
  "duration_ms": 3200
}

Log message (server -> client):

{
  "type": "log",
  "data": "Speech detected. Running HamsaASR transcription...",
  "duration_ms": 100
}

Audio format: Raw PCM 16-bit signed, 16kHz, mono. Chunk size 3200 bytes (100ms). Must be sent with real-time pacing (100ms between chunks) for VAD to trigger correctly. Dumping all chunks at once produces zero transcriptions.

VAD: Silero VAD (JIT-loaded). Configurable threshold (0.0 to 1.0). Detects speech segments and triggers transcription only when speech is detected followed by silence.

docs.title: 5.3 Authentication: Fernet Encryption
docs.text:
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet

ENCRYPTION_KEY = "pbFK_uqlqLoNHuoiuuQZykzoeK5S8oEGh63pSwNfec0="
SECRET_API_KEY = "HuoiuuQZykzoeK5S8o"

cipher_suite = Fernet(ENCRYPTION_KEY.encode())
encrypted_key = cipher_suite.encrypt(SECRET_API_KEY.encode())
# Result: gAAAAABo-1oxslqx1hGc8nGn_7iWiD0jwAGE7tDk3MgA-t_9gM05qFZIP1tTiBgJpDkTaTrf7OHe9RLj2AjspUYuKxAqVnPjIJ6AD6q-0E8paCMBreZ8pGc=

REST uses x-api-key header. WebSocket uses api_key field in handshake JSON.

docs.title: 6. Hamsa Cloud API (from docs.tryhamsa.com)
docs.text: The self-hosted instance has a different API surface than the Hamsa cloud platform. Here is what the cloud offers.

docs.title: 6.1 Cloud REST STT: POST /v1/realtime/stt
docs.text:
Auth: Authorization: Token <api-key> header.

Request (JSON body):

{
  "audioBase64": "WAV-base64-string",
  "language": "ar",
  "isEosEnabled": false,
  "eosThreshold": 0.3
}

Response:

{
  "text": "transcribed text"
}

Note: The cloud returns a simple {"text": "..."} while the self-hosted returns {"text": "...", "gender": "...", "processing_time": ..., "duration": ...}.

docs.title: 6.2 Cloud Async STT: POST /v1/jobs/transcribe
docs.text: Async batch transcription from media URLs. Returns a jobId, results delivered via webhook. Not relevant for real-time use.

docs.title: 6.3 Cloud WebSocket API: wss://api.tryhamsa.com/v1/realtime/ws
docs.text:
Auth: ?api_key=YOUR_API_KEY query parameter or X-Api-Key header.

Message format (unified for TTS and STT):

interface WebSocketMessage {
  type: "tts" | "stt" | "response" | "error" | "info" | "ack" | "end";
  payload?: object;
}

STT request (client -> server):

{
  "type": "stt",
  "payload": {
    "audioBase64": "base64-audio-data",
    "language": "ar",
    "isEosEnabled": true,
    "eosThreshold": 0.3
  }
}

STT response (server -> client): plain text string (not JSON):

مرحبا بك في خدمة همسة

This is a request/response pattern (send complete audio, get text back), not a streaming VAD pattern. The cloud WebSocket STT is essentially the REST endpoint over WebSocket.

docs.title: 6.4 Key Difference: Cloud vs Self-Hosted
docs.text: Feature Cloud API Self-Hosted STT REST endpoint POST /v1/realtime/stt POST /transcribe STT REST request {audioBase64, language} {audio, lang, gender_detection, ...} STT REST response {text} {text, gender, eos, processing_time, duration, ...} WebSocket endpoint wss://api.tryhamsa.com/v1/realtime/ws ws://host:8080/ws WebSocket STT Request/response (send full audio, get text) Streaming VAD (send PCM chunks, get segment transcriptions) WebSocket auth ?api_key= query param api_key field in handshake JSON (Fernet-encrypted) WebSocket message format {type: "stt", payload: {audioBase64, ...}} {type: "handshake", api_key, options} then binary PCM VAD Server-side, not exposed Client streams PCM, server VAD triggers transcription Gender detection Not in cloud STT Supported (returns gender per segment) Speaker identification Not in cloud STT Supported (returns speaker_info) Wake word Not in cloud STT Supported (wake_word_match, similarity_score) Noise cancellation Not in cloud STT Supported (Krisp, configurable) Dialect/language switcher In voice agents, not raw STT lang: "auto" TTS POST /v1/realtime/tts-stream Not in self-hosted STT pod

docs.title: 7. hamsa_livekit Plugin (from GitHub repo)
docs.text: The hamsa-ai/hamsa_livekit repo is a LiveKit Agents plugin that wraps the Hamsa cloud API (not the self-hosted instance).

docs.title: 7.1 STT Module (stt.py)
docs.text:
HAMSA_STT_BASE_URL = "https://api.tryhamsa.com/v1/realtime/stt"

Key observations from the source code:

  • Uses POST /v1/realtime/stt (cloud REST endpoint, not WebSocket)
  • Auth: Authorization: Token {api_key} header
  • Sends audioBase64 (WAV format, 16kHz) with language, isEosEnabled, eosThreshold
  • Parses response: response_json["data"]["text"] (note: this expects {success, data: {text}} wrapper, which differs from the documented {text} response)
  • Capabilities: streaming=False, interim_results=False (batch only, no streaming)
  • Converts LiveKit AudioBuffer to WAV base64 via rtc.combine_audio_frames(buffer).to_wav_bytes()
  • Hardcodes confidence=1.0 and gender="Male" (Hamsa cloud doesn't return these)
  • No VAD, no WebSocket, no real-time streaming

docs.title: 7.2 TTS Module (tts.py)
docs.text:
BASE_URL = "https://api.tryhamsa.com/v1/realtime/tts-stream"
  • Uses cloud TTS streaming endpoint
  • Auth: Authorization: Token {api_key} header
  • Sends {speaker, dialect, text, mulaw} as JSON
  • Receives raw audio chunks (8192 bytes each) streamed back
  • Supports 24+ Arabic voices across 9 dialects
  • Sample rate: 16kHz default, configurable

docs.title: 7.3 What Can Be Reused
docs.text:
The LiveKit plugin targets the cloud API, which has a simpler protocol than our self-hosted instance. However:

  • The STT module's request format (audioBase64 + language + isEosEnabled + eosThreshold) is similar to what the self-hosted /transcribe accepts, just with different field names
  • The TTS module is not applicable since our self-hosted instance is STT-only
  • The cloud WebSocket protocol ({type: "stt", payload: {audioBase64}}) is a request/response pattern, fundamentally different from our self-hosted streaming VAD WebSocket

The LiveKit plugin code confirms that Hamsa's own cloud STT is a simple batch transcription API with no streaming, no VAD, no gender detection, and no speaker identification in the cloud STT product.

docs.title: 8.1 OpenAI Transcription API (POST /v1/audio/transcriptions)
docs.text:
OpenAI's transcription API is a batch endpoint:

POST /v1/audio/transcriptions
Content-Type: multipart/form-data

file: <audio file>
model: whisper-1
language: optional
prompt: optional
response_format: json (default), text, srt, verbose_json, vtt
temperature: 0-1
timestamp_granularities: segment, word

Response (json format):

{
  "text": "transcribed text"
}

Response (verbose_json format):

{
  "task": "transcribe",
  "language": "arabic",
  "duration": 29.83,
  "text": "full transcription",
  "segments": [...],
  "words": [...]
}

docs.title: 8.2 Mapping: Self-Hosted Hamsa to OpenAI Transcription
docs.text:
OpenAI Field Hamsa Self-Hosted Status file (multipart upload) audio (base64 in JSON) Adapter converts multipart file to base64 model Not applicable (single model) Can be ignored or mapped to "hamsa-stt" language lang ("auto" or specific) Direct mapping prompt prompt Direct mapping response_format: json {text} from response Direct mapping response_format: verbose_json Not supported Would need to fabricate segments/duration response_format: text/srt/vtt Not supported Would need to format output temperature Not supported Ignored timestamp_granularities Not supported Ignored

Functionality lost in REST adapter:

  • gender detection (Hamsa returns it, OpenAI format has no field for it)
  • eos (end-of-speech) detection
  • processing_time and duration (could be mapped to verbose_json duration)
  • speaker_embeddings and speaker_identification
  • wake_word detection and similarity_score

docs.title: 8.3 OpenAI Realtime API (WebSocket)
docs.text:
OpenAI's Realtime API is a bidirectional event-driven protocol for full voice conversations (STT + LLM + TTS in one session). Key events:

Client -> Server: session.update (configure modalities, voice, turn detection)
Client -> Server: input_audio_buffer.append (base64 PCM chunks)
Client -> Server: input_audio_buffer.commit
Client -> Server: response.create
Server -> Client: session.created
Server -> Client: conversation.item.created
Server -> Client: response.audio_transcript.delta (streaming text)
Server -> Client: response.audio.delta (streaming TTS audio)
Server -> Client: response.done

docs.title: 8.4 Mapping: Self-Hosted Hamsa WebSocket to OpenAI Realtime
docs.text:
OpenAI Realtime Hamsa WebSocket Status session.update handshake with options Partial: Hamsa options map to some session config input_audio_buffer.append (base64) Binary PCM chunks Adapter must decode base64 to binary PCM input_audio_buffer.commit Not needed (VAD auto-detects) Different paradigm response.create Not needed (VAD auto-triggers) Different paradigm response.audio_transcript.delta transcription message Adapter translates format response.audio.delta (TTS) Not supported Hamsa STT pod has no TTS Turn detection (server VAD) Silero VAD Both use VAD, but different implementations Interruption handling Not supported Would need adapter logic Function calling / tools Not supported Not applicable to STT-only Multiple modalities (text + audio) STT only Hamsa STT pod has no TTS/LLM

Functionality lost in WebSocket adapter:

  • gender detection per transcription segment
  • eos (end-of-speech) prediction per segment
  • speaker_info and speaker identification
  • Configurable VAD parameters (vad_threshold, min_speech_ms, min_silence_duration_ms, silence_timeout) - OpenAI Realtime exposes server VAD config but with different parameter names and semantics
  • noise_cancellation (Krisp) - OpenAI has its own noise cancellation
  • audio_type selection (PCM vs MULAW)
  • Real-time segment-level transcription (Hamsa transcribes per VAD-detected segment; OpenAI streams token-level deltas)

Functionality that cannot be expressed in OpenAI format at all:

  • gender field (no OpenAI equivalent)
  • speaker_embeddings (no OpenAI equivalent)
  • wake_word_match and similarity_score (no OpenAI equivalent)
  • eos.prediction (OpenAI has turn_detection but the semantics differ)

docs.title: 8.5 Summary: What Hamsa Would Lose
docs.text:
If we make Hamsa fully OpenAI-compatible, these self-hosted features have no OpenAI API equivalent and would be inaccessible through the OpenAI-compatible interface:

  1. Gender detection - Hamsa returns gender: "Male"/"Female" per transcription segment. OpenAI has no gender field.
  2. Speaker identification - Hamsa can identify and return speaker info. OpenAI has no speaker ID in transcription.
  3. Speaker embeddings - Hamsa returns embedding vectors. OpenAI has no equivalent.
  4. Wake word detection - Hamsa can detect wake words and return similarity scores. OpenAI has no equivalent.
  5. EOS (end-of-speech) prediction - Hamsa returns a prediction score per segment. OpenAI's turn detection is similar but not exposed as a per-segment value.
  6. Configurable VAD parameters - Hamsa exposes vad_threshold, min_speech_ms, min_silence_duration_ms, silence_timeout. OpenAI Realtime exposes some VAD config but with different semantics.
  7. Noise cancellation - Hamsa supports Krisp. OpenAI has its own solution but it's not configurable through the same parameters.
  8. MULAW audio support - Hamsa accepts MULAW 8kHz. OpenAI uses PCM 24kHz.

Mitigation: These features could be preserved by keeping the native Hamsa WebSocket endpoint (/v1/hamsa/stt/ws) alongside any OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Clients who need gender detection, speaker ID, or wake word would use the native endpoint. Clients who just need transcription text would use the OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

docs.title: 9.1 REST: OpenAI-Compatible Adapter (Low Effort)
docs.text:
Create a provider adapter that maps POST /v1/audio/transcriptions to Hamsa's POST /transcribe:

Client (OpenAI SDK) -> LiteLLM /v1/audio/transcriptions -> Hamsa /transcribe
                         (multipart -> JSON base64)
                         (OpenAI response <- Hamsa response)

This gives full OpenAI transcription compatibility. Gender/eos/speaker data is dropped (no OpenAI field for it).

docs.title: 9.2 WebSocket: Keep Native Endpoint (No OpenAI Realtime Mapping)
docs.text:
The self-hosted WebSocket protocol is fundamentally different from OpenAI Realtime:

  • Hamsa: streaming PCM in, VAD-triggered segment transcriptions out
  • OpenAI Realtime: full conversation protocol (STT + LLM + TTS) with event-driven messages

Mapping Hamsa STT-only WebSocket to OpenAI Realtime would lose the TTS and LLM half of the Realtime API, making it a broken implementation. The native /v1/hamsa/stt/ws endpoint (via the existing startup hook) is the correct approach for streaming STT.

docs.title: 9.3 Hybrid Approach (Recommended)
docs.text:
Keep both endpoints:

  1. POST /v1/audio/transcriptions - OpenAI-compatible REST (new adapter)
  2. WS /v1/hamsa/stt/ws - Native Hamsa WebSocket (existing hook, preserves all features)

This gives OpenAI SDK compatibility for batch transcription while preserving the full feature set for real-time streaming use cases.

docs.title: 10. Network Topology and Internal vs External Access
10.1 Internal Cluster Service (REST and WS both work)
docs.text:
Service:  s-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231 (ClusterIP, namespace: adeo)
REST URL: http://s-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080/transcribe
WS URL:   ws://s-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080/ws

The internal service accepts:

  • REST: x-api-key header with Fernet-encrypted key. Returns 200 with transcription JSON.
  • WS: api_key field in handshake JSON. Returns handshake_ack with status: "authenticated".

docs.title: 10.2 External Inference Proxy (REST broken, WS broken)
docs.text:
REST URL: https://inference.adeoaiengine.ecouncil.ae/models/9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231/proxy/transcribe
WS URL:   wss://inference.adeoaiengine.ecouncil.ae/models/9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231/ws/ws

The external inference proxy at inference.adeoaiengine.ecouncil.ae has its own auth layer that is incompatible with the Hamsa Fernet key:

  • REST with x-api-key header: returns {"detail":"Authorization header is missing","status_code":401}
  • REST with Authorization: Bearer <key>: returns {"detail":"Invalid API key","status_code":401}
  • REST with Authorization: Token <key>: returns {"detail":"Invalid Authorization header","status_code":401}
  • REST with Authorization: <key> (no prefix): returns {"detail":"Invalid Authorization header","status_code":401}
  • WS: closes with 1008 (policy violation) Missing token in auth message

docs.title: 10.3 Internal Service Path Discovery
docs.text:
The internal service has different paths for REST vs WS:

  • /transcribe (REST POST) - works, returns transcription JSON
  • /ws (WebSocket) - works, returns handshake_ack
  • /ws/ws (WebSocket) - returns HTTP 403
  • Bare :8080 or :8080/ (WebSocket) - returns HTTP 403

docs.title: 10.4 Protocol Conversion
docs.text:
When the model is registered with a wss:// or ws:// api_base (as is natural for a WS-based service), REST calls need protocol conversion:

  • ws:// to http:// for REST
  • wss:// to https:// for REST (with SSL verification disabled for internal certs)
  • Keep ws:// or wss:// for WS

docs.title: 10.5 SSL Considerations
docs.text:
The internal cluster service uses HTTP (no TLS), so no SSL context needed. If using the external wss:// URL, SSL certificate verification fails because the cluster uses internal/self-signed certs. Disable verification with:

ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
ctx.check_hostname = False
ctx.verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE

docs.title: 11.1 Model Registration
docs.text:
The model is registered in the LiteLLM DB with:

{
  "model_name": "tryhamsa-stt",
  "litellm_params": {
    "api_base": "http://s-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080",
    "custom_llm_provider": "custom",
    "use_in_pass_through": true,
    "model": "custom/tryhamsa-stt"
  },
  "model_info": {
    "mode": "audio_transcription",
    "description": "Hamsa STT WebSocket-based real-time transcription service"
  }
}

Key fields:

  • use_in_pass_through: true - enables get_available_deployment_for_pass_through() to resolve this model
  • custom_llm_provider: "custom" - marks it as a custom provider, not a known LLM provider
  • mode: "audio_transcription" - tags the call type for logging
  • api_base - the internal cluster IP URL (no path suffix; routes are appended by the provider code)

docs.title: 11.2 LiteLLM Router: get_available_deployment_for_pass_through
docs.text:
from litellm.proxy.proxy_server import llm_router

deployment = llm_router.get_available_deployment_for_pass_through(model="tryhamsa-stt")
api_base = deployment.get("litellm_params", {}).get("api_base", "")

This applies native RPM/TPM/priority/cooldown/load-balancing and returns the deployment dict. Raises RouterRateLimitError (from litellm.types.router) if rate limits are exceeded. The error has a .cooldown_time attribute (seconds) that should map to HTTP 429 retry-after for REST and WS close code 1013 for WebSocket.

docs.title: 11.3 LiteLLM Built-in Pass-Through Endpoints
docs.text:
LiteLLM has a built-in generic pass-through system (pass_through_endpoints in general_settings or DB):

general_settings:
  pass_through_endpoints:
    - path: /hamsa
      target: http://s-9c57bce9-0583-4bf7-9443-08825220a231.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080
      headers:
        x-api-key: "gAAAAAB..."
      include_subpath: true
      auth: true

With include_subpath: true:

  • POST /hamsa/transcribe forwards to http://s-...:8080/transcribe
  • POST /hamsa/any-route forwards to http://s-...:8080/any-route

Limitations of the built-in system for Hamsa:

  1. The target is static. It does NOT resolve from the LiteLLM model registry, so no RPM/TPM/priority/cooldown/load-balancing from the router.
  2. WebSocket pass-through exists (create_websocket_passthrough_route) but the config-based registration only registers HTTP routes, not WS.
  3. No support for Hamsa's handshake api_key injection (the Fernet key must be injected into the first JSON message, not sent as an HTTP header).

docs.title: 11.4 LiteLLM LLM Provider Pass-Through
docs.text: LiteLLM has provider-specific pass-through endpoints (/anthropic/{endpoint:path}, /cohere/{endpoint:path}, /gemini/{endpoint:path}). These resolve the provider's api_base from provider config and forward arbitrary subpaths. But this is hardcoded to known providers via ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_model_info(). There is no generic "custom provider" version.

docs.title: 11.5 Recommended Architecture: Prefix-Scoped Catch-All
docs.text:
Register a prefix-scoped catch-all route (e.g. /tryhamsa/{endpoint:path}) that:

  1. Reads model from query param or body
  2. Calls get_available_deployment_for_pass_through(model) for RPM/TPM/priority
  3. Forwards the captured subpath to api_base + subpath

This avoids route conflicts with existing LiteLLM routes, provides model-registry-based rate limiting, and doesn't hardcode route paths like /transcribe or /ws.

REST flow:

POST /tryhamsa/transcribe?model=tryhamsa-stt
  -> user_api_key_auth
  -> get_available_deployment_for_pass_through("tryhamsa-stt")
  -> forward to api_base + "/transcribe" with x-api-key header

WS flow (requires handshake injection):

WS /tryhamsa/ws?model=tryhamsa-stt
  -> user_api_key_auth_websocket (via subprotocol)
  -> get_available_deployment_for_pass_through("tryhamsa-stt")
  -> forward to ws_url(api_base) + "/ws"
  -> inject Fernet key into first handshake JSON message

docs.title: 12.1 REST Transcription (internal cluster URL)
docs.text:
AUDIO_B64=$(base64 -w0 hello.wav)
curl -sk -X POST https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/custom/audio/transcriptions \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-05132025" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"tryhamsa-stt\",\"audio\":\"$AUDIO_B64\",\"eos_enabled\":false,\"eos_threshold\":0.3,\"lang\":\"auto\"}"

Response:

{
  "text": " Hello.",
  "gender": "Female",
  "eos": null,

docs.title: 12.3 Key Behavioral Notes
docs.text:
• Audio must be sent as raw binary PCM (16-bit signed, 16kHz, mono), not base64, over WebSocket
  • Chunk size of 3200 bytes (100ms at 16kHz 16-bit mono) with 100ms pacing between chunks is required for VAD to trigger
  • Dumping all chunks at once without pacing produces zero transcriptions
  • The handshake api_key field is overwritten by the gateway with the real Fernet key before forwarding to the upstream; clients can send a placeholder value
  • WebSocket auth from browser uses sec-websocket-protocol: openai-insecure-api-key.<litellm-key> subprotocol (same as OpenAI Realtime API pattern)

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
File: /app/app/auth.py

The TTS service uses Fernet symmetric encryption for API key authentication. The client must send an encrypted token in the x-api-key header. The server decrypts it and compares against the secret.

# /app/.env contains:
ENCRYPTION_KEY="pbFK_uqlqLoNHuoiuuQZykzoeK5S8oEGh63pSwNfec0="
SECRET_API_KEY="HuoiuuQZykzoeK5S8o"

The auth flow: 1. Server loads ENCRYPTION_KEY and SECRET_API_KEY from .env 2. Server creates a Fernet cipher from ENCRYPTION_KEY 3. Client sends x-api-key header with a Fernet-encrypted token 4. Server decrypts the token and compares to SECRET_API_KEY 5. If match, request proceeds; otherwise 401

The encrypted API key is generated by encrypting the SECRET_API_KEY with the ENCRYPTION_KEY:

from cryptography.fernet import Fernet
cipher = Fernet("pbFK_uqlqLoNHuoiuuQZykzoeK5S8oEGh63pSwNfec0=".encode())
encrypted = cipher.encrypt("HuoiuuQZykzoeK5S8o".encode()).decode()
# Result: gAAAAABqVlrPWkz1L8WH_nCl_9RQiRi9t6mHDWUPYBNMRoDW6kR4osW54hL5UzWdmM0So3Ur1Fs2ktmqKxhmMwrFs2XOMXeU2DVJhwKf6a1e35MSpvws8nA=

All endpoints except /health-check and / require the x-api-key header.

docs.title: Model Loading
docs.text:
File: /app/app/main.py (startup event)

At application startup, the model is loaded as a singleton:

@app.on_event("startup")
def load_models():
    tts_model = hamsaTTS(model_dir=Path("hamsa_models/HamsaTTSv2"), device="cuda:0")
    tts_model._initialize_inference()
    tts_model.load_speakers_from_directory(Path("speakers/"))
    app.state.preprocessor = TextPreprocessor()

The hamsaTTS class is a singleton (via __new__ override). It loads: - A tokenizer (AutoTokenizer from transformers) - An audio tokenizer (BiCodecTokenizer from hamsatts) - A vLLM AsyncLLMEngine for token generation - Speaker profiles from /app/speakers/ directory (each speaker is a .pt file containing global token IDs and semantic token IDs)

docs.title: 1. POST /tts/stream - Text-to-Speech Synthesis
docs.text:
File: /app/app/main.py

This is the main TTS endpoint. It accepts a JSON request and returns a streaming audio response.

docs.title: Request Model
docs.text:
class TTSRequest(BaseModel):
    text: str                                    # Required: text to synthesize
    speaker: str                                 # Required: speaker name (e.g. "jasem")
    language_id: str                             # Required: language code (e.g. "ar")
    lang: Optional[str] = "ar"                   # Optional: language override
    mulaw: Optional[bool] = False                # Optional: mu-law encoding (8kHz) vs PCM (16kHz)
    stream: Optional[bool] = False               # Optional: streaming mode (no WAV header)
    dialect: Optional[str] = None                # Optional: dialect code ("ksa", "msa", "eng")
    expressiveness: Optional[float] = 1.0        # Optional: 0.0-2.0, controls temperature
    speed: Optional[float] = 1.0                 # Optional: 0.5-2.0, speech speed multiplier

docs.title: Request Example
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://s-cd2850fc-5870-4a57-89da-5e978eee66f4.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080/tts/stream" \
  -H "x-api-key: gAAAAABqVlrPWkz1L8WH_nCl_9RQiRi9t6mHDWUPYBNMRoDW6kR4osW54hL5UzWdmM0So3Ur1Fs2ktmqKxhmMwrFs2XOMXeU2DVJhwKf6a1e35MSpvws8nA=" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "text": "مرحبا بك في اختبار تحويل النص إلى كلام.",
    "speaker": "jasem",
    "language_id": "ar",
    "mulaw": false,
    "stream": false,
    "dialect": "ksa"
  }'

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
• Content-Type: audio/wav
  • Format: StreamingResponse (FastAPI StreamingResponse with media_type="audio/wav")
  • Audio Format (when mulaw=false):
  • 16kHz, mono, 16-bit PCM WAV
  • Includes WAV header when stream=false
  • No WAV header when stream=true (raw PCM stream)
  • Audio Format (when mulaw=true):
  • 8kHz, mono, mu-law encoded
  • Audio is resampled from 16kHz to 8kHz, then converted from linear PCM to mu-law via audioop.lin2ulaw

docs.title: Internal Processing Flow
docs.text:
1. Text preprocessing: If stream=false, generate WAV header first (16kHz sample rate)
  2. Speaker resolution: Look up speaker (case-insensitive) in the loaded speakers dictionary. If not found, raises KeyError
  3. Dialect resolution: Use provided dialect (lowercased) or fall back to speaker's default dialect. If text is >80% English, override dialect to "eng"
  4. Expressiveness calculation: Converts expressiveness (0.0-2.0) to temperature and semantic token flag:
  5. 0.0 to 1.0: temperature = 0.1 + (expressiveness * 0.5), no semantic tokens
  6. 1.0 to 2.0: temperature = 0.4 + ((expressiveness - 1.0) * 1.1), with semantic tokens
  7. Pause token splitting: Text is split by <pause_short> and <pause_long> tokens. Newlines become <pause_short>. Short pauses generate 400-600ms of silence. Long pauses generate 800-1500ms of silence
  8. Sentence splitting: Each text chunk is preprocessed by TextPreprocessor.preprocess() which normalizes text and splits into sentences (desired_length=400, max_length=450 characters)
  9. Token generation: For each sentence, model.stream_tokens_to_audio() is called with:
  10. temperature (from expressiveness)
  11. batch_size=25
  12. overlap_tokens=10
  13. trim_ms=100.0
  14. top_k=25
  15. top_p=0.95
  16. use_semantic_tokens (from expressiveness)
  17. speed (from request)
  18. Audio output: Each generated audio chunk is trimmed (silence from start), optionally resampled for mu-law, and yielded as int16 bytes

docs.title: Expressiveness Mapping
docs.text: expressiveness temperature use_semantic_tokens Description 0.0 0.1 false Most deterministic, flat 0.5 0.35 false Mild variation 1.0 (default) 0.6 false Balanced 1.5 0.95 true Expressive with semantic tokens 2.0 1.5 true Most expressive, most random

docs.title: 2. POST /tts/voice_clone - Extract Voice Tokens from Audio
docs.text:
File: /app/app/main.py

Extracts speaker tokens (global token IDs and semantic token IDs) from an audio file. This is step 1 of the two-step voice cloning process.

docs.title: Request Model
docs.text:
class VCRequest(BaseModel):
    audio_url: str       # Required: URL to the reference audio file
    prompt_text: str     # Required: transcript of the reference audio

docs.title: Request Example
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://s-cd2850fc-5870-4a57-89da-5e978eee66f4.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080/tts/voice_clone" \
  -H "x-api-key: <encrypted_key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "audio_url": "https://example.com/reference.wav",
    "prompt_text": "This is the transcript of the reference audio."
  }'

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Returns the extracted voice tokens as JSON. The response contains global_token_ids and semantic_token_ids that can be used in the /tts/load_voice_cloning endpoint.

docs.title: Internal Flow
docs.text:
1. Calls model.voice_clone_from_audio(audio_url, prompt_text)
  2. The method downloads the audio from the URL
  3. Runs it through the BiCodecTokenizer to extract global and semantic tokens
  4. Returns the token arrays

docs.title: 3. POST /tts/load_voice_cloning - Register a Cloned Voice
docs.text:
File: /app/app/main.py

Registers pre-extracted speaker tokens as a named speaker in the model's in-memory speaker dictionary. This is step 2 of the two-step voice cloning process.

docs.title: Request Model
docs.text:
class VCLoadRequest(BaseModel):
    speaker_id: str                                                    # Required: name for the new voice
    global_token_ids: Union[List[int], List[List[int]], List[List[List[int]]]]
    semantic_token_ids: Union[List[int], List[List[int]], List[List[List[int]]]]
    dialect: str = "msa"                                               # Optional: dialect code
    prompt_text: str = ""                                              # Optional: reference transcript

docs.title: Request Example
docs.text:
curl -X POST "http://s-cd2850fc-5870-4a57-89da-5e978eee66f4.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080/tts/load_voice_cloning" \
  -H "x-api-key: <encrypted_key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "speaker_id": "my_custom_voice",
    "global_token_ids": [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]],
    "semantic_token_ids": [[10, 20], [30, 40]],
    "dialect": "ksa",
    "prompt_text": "Reference transcript"
  }'

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Returns confirmation that the speaker was added.

docs.title: Internal Flow
docs.text:
1. Calls model.add_speaker(speaker_id, torch.tensor(global_token_ids), torch.tensor(semantic_token_ids), dialect, prompt_text)
  2. The speaker is registered in the model.speakers dictionary (keyed by lowercased speaker_id)
  3. After registration, the new voice is immediately usable in /tts/stream by passing speaker="my_custom_voice"

Important: The registered speaker exists only in the model's in-memory state. If the pod restarts, custom voices are lost and must be re-registered.

docs.title: Dialect Support
docs.text: The following dialect codes are supported: - msa - Modern Standard Arabic (default for most speakers) - ksa - Saudi Arabian dialect - eng - English (auto-detected if text is >80% English) - Other dialects may be available per-speaker (stored in speaker profile)

docs.title: Model Architecture
docs.text:
File: /app/app/hamsaTTS.py

The hamsaTTS class is based on Spark-TTS architecture, adapted for Arabic:

class hamsaTTS:
    """
    Spark-TTS for text-to-speech generation using VLLMAsyncEngine
    for real-time token streaming.
    Implemented as a singleton.
    """

Key components: - Tokenizer: AutoTokenizer from transformers (for text tokenization) - Audio Tokenizer: BiCodecTokenizer from hamsatts (for audio encoding/decoding) - LLM Engine: AsyncLLMEngine from vLLM (for autoregressive token generation) - Sample Rate: 16000 Hz (native), 8000 Hz (mu-law mode)

The model uses a two-stage process: 1. Token generation: The LLM generates discrete audio tokens autoregressively from the input text, conditioned on speaker tokens 2. Audio synthesis: The BiCodecTokenizer decodes the generated tokens back into audio waveforms

The stream_tokens_to_audio() method is an async generator that yields audio chunks as they are generated, enabling real-time streaming.

docs.title: Text Preprocessing
docs.text:
File: /app/app/text_preprocessor.py

Before synthesis, text goes through preprocessing: 1. Arabic number conversion: ArabicNumberToWord.replace_numbers_with_words() converts numeric digits to Arabic words 2. Sentence splitting: txtsplit library splits long text into manageable chunks 3. Normalization: Various text normalization steps based on dialect 4. Chunking: Sentences are limited to ~400-450 characters

docs.title: Pause Token Support
docs.text:
The TTS supports inline pause tokens in the text:

Token Effect <pause_short> 400-600ms of silence (randomized) <pause_long> 800-1500ms of silence (randomized) \n (newline) Treated as <pause_short>

These tokens allow clients to control pacing and rhythm in the synthesized speech.
