docs.text:
To activate the 5 dead routes, these changes are needed in this order:

Layer 1: TextToSpeechRequestData schema (base_llm/text_to_speech/transformation.py:24) Add method: str field to the TypedDict so the contract is explicit.

Layer 2: voice_handler (llm_http_handler.py:11329) Add support for form_data+files, and read method to dispatch GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE instead of hardcoding client.post().

Layer 3: get_provider_voice_config (utils.py:9026) Change Literal["hamsa"] to Literal["hamsa", "omnivoice"] and add the OMNIVOICE branch.

Layer 4: SDK functions (main.py) Add ascript(), alist_voices(), acreate_voice_profile(), aupdate_voice_profile(), aget_voice_profile(), adelete_voice_profile().

Layer 5: Router methods (router.py) Add corresponding Router.ascript(), Router.alist_voices(), etc.

Layer 6: Proxy routes (proxy_server.py) Add @router.post("/v1/audio/script"), @router.get("/v1/voices"), etc.

Layers 1-3 are infrastructure changes. Layers 4-6 are mechanical additions that follow the existing aspeech/acreate_voice patterns.

docs.title: Comparison: How Hamsa voice management works vs what OmniVoice needs
docs.text:
Hamsa's HamsaVoiceConfig is simpler because it only does dict_body POST: - transform_create_voice_request returns TextToSpeechRequestData(dict_body=body) - voice_handler handles dict_body POST -> works

OmniVoice's OmniVoiceVoiceConfig needs form_data+files (for create_profile with ref_audio) and GET/DELETE/PATCH (for profile CRUD): - transform_create_voice_request returns TextToSpeechRequestData(form_data=..., files=..., method="PATCH") - voice_handler only handles dict_body POST -> broken

Hamsa's voice management is a single POST endpoint (/tts/voice_clone or /tts/load_voice_cloning). OmniVoice's is a full CRUD REST API with 6 endpoints. The voice_handler was designed for Hamsa's simple POST-only model and cannot handle OmniVoice's richer API surface.

docs.title: Clean aspects
docs.text:
• TTS and voice clone routes are fully wired, tested, and follow the same architecture as Inception and Hamsa
  • Config classes are well-structured with extracted helpers, derived constants, and modern type hints
  • _collect_passthrough is non-mutating (better than Inception's mutating version)
  • Internal params frozenset is comprehensive

docs.title: Gaps (all resolved)
docs.text:
• ~~2 of 4 config classes are dead code~~ All 4 config classes are now invoked in production
  • ~~voice_handler only supports dict_body POST~~ voice_handler/async_voice_handler now dispatch on body type and HTTP method via _send_voice_request_sync/_send_voice_request_async helpers
  • ~~TextToSpeechRequestData has no method field~~ Added method, form_data, files fields
  • ~~get_provider_voice_config only dispatches HAMSA~~ Now dispatches HAMSA and OMNIVOICE
  • ~~5 route types registered but no SDK functions/router methods/proxy routes~~ All 5 route types now have full SDK/router/proxy wiring
  • ~~No ascript SDK function~~ script/ascript SDK functions added

docs.title: Is the implementation "clean like Hamsa and Inception"?
docs.text:
For the 2 working routes: Yes. The TTS and voice clone configs follow the same pattern as Hamsa and Inception, with some improvements (modern types, non-mutating helpers, derived constants).

For the 5 previously dead routes: All infrastructure work is complete. The config classes are now fully reachable through the standard 7-layer architecture.

docs.title: Are the new routes expandable?
docs.text: All 7 routes are easily expandable: Adding new form params is a one-liner in the _TTS_FORM_KEYS / _CLONE_FORM_KEYS / _SCRIPT_FORM_KEYS tuples. The voice_handler now supports all HTTP methods and body types, so new voice management actions can be added without further infrastructure changes.

docs.title: pyannote Diarization Provider: Choices and Implementation Plan
docs.text:
Status: plan (2026-10-19). Records the design decisions for exposing a coro-served POST /v1/diarize through the OICM LiteLLM gateway as a pyannote provider, and the vertical-slice implementation plan across the litellm tree and the discovery controller.

Revision 2 (same day): coro now supports a configurable serving model id (commit 99633ba, CORO_PYANNOTE_DIARIZE_MODEL_ID), and the ADEO image bakes pyannote/community-1 (commit 8ddf659), so the gateway, the pod, and the client all agree on one id end to end. This removes the asymmetry Revision 1 left (gateway pyannote/community-1 vs pod community-1) and with it the reliance on the first-slash split landing exactly on the pod's enum value. Two mechanical consequences are recorded below: model_name becomes pyannote/community-1 (no longer the bare enum value), and the gateway must always populate the model form field (the pod's hardcoded Form default community-1 is rejected on the renamed deployment).

Revision 1 (same day): corrected the model id to the API enum value community-1 (the DiarizeRequest.model enum is precision-2, community-1, precision-3). The earliest draft used coro's Hugging Face pipeline id pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1, which is an engine-internal model-selection id, not an API model id. Provider detection moved to the OpenAPI path probe as a consequence.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
A coro deployment (the ASR/diarization engine, /home/jyao/DGE/coro) serves a pyannoteAI-exact POST /v1/diarize plus GET /v1/jobs/{jobId}. The contract is pinned by coro's conformance suite against the official docs.pyannote.ai/openapi.json fixture, so the pod side of the contract cannot drift. The gateway must make that endpoint reachable under LiteLLM virtual-key auth, routing, and spend logging, selectable by model id, with the pod address discovered dynamically by the OICM controller (no static api_base).

The H200 MIG gateway plan (coro ADR 0025) routes /v1/audio/transcriptions through LiteLLM to per-workload coro deployments "so the deployment must be selectable by model id". Diarization is the same requirement one surface over.

docs.title: C1. Provider name: pyannote, not coro; one id pyannote/community-1 end to end
docs.text:
Coro is a tool wrapper: the contract the gateway forwards to is pyannoteAI's DiarizeRequest/DiarizationJob/DiarizationJobOutput/ValidationErrorResponse shapes, and any future non-coro engine that serves the same contract (including pyannoteAI's own cloud) must be interchangeable behind the same provider. The provider is the contract; the engine is an implementation detail.

The serving model id is settings-driven on the pod (coro commit 99633ba, ServerSettings.pyannote_diarize_model_id, env CORO_PYANNOTE_DIARIZE_MODEL_ID): the pyannoteAI spec enum value community-1 stays the source default so the cloud contract holds for bare runs, and the ADEO image bakes CORO_PYANNOTE_DIARIZE_MODEL_ID=pyannote/community-1 (commit 8ddf659) for gateway deployments. The served weights never change; the id is the request/response-facing name only.

With the rename, one id serves all three roles and the earlier asymmetry is gone:

role id why client sends / model_name / spend-log model pyannote/community-1 matches the pod's accepted id, so what the client asks for is what the log says and what the pod echoes registered litellm_params.model pyannote/pyannote/community-1 controller payload is {provider}/{model_id}; the double prefix is what makes the first-slash split yield the pod's accepted id pod accepts and echoes (CORO_PYANNOTE_DIARIZE_MODEL_ID) pyannote/community-1 baked in the ADEO image

The double-prefix pyannote/pyannote/community-1 is not a mistake: the controller's _register_payload composes model = f"{provider}/{model_id}", and get_llm_provider strips exactly one leading pyannote/ before the SDK call, so the pod receives pyannote/community-1 verbatim. The client never types the double prefix; it types model_name. (community-1 as model_name would also work — the split would yield bare community-1, which bare coro runs accept but the renamed ADEO deployment rejects — but then the spend log and the UI would disagree with what the pod echoes. One id everywhere is the whole point.)

pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1 (coro's internal Hugging Face pipeline id, one layer below the API contract) appears nowhere in the gateway.

Consequences:

  • LlmProviders.PYANNOTE = "pyannote" in litellm/types/utils.py
  • Provider dir litellm/llms/pyannote/
  • The model form field is required at the gateway: coro's route keeps a hardcoded Form(default="community-1") even when the accepted id is renamed, so an omitted field is the spec-shaped 400 on the ADEO deployment (verified at coro HEAD). The gateway route defaults data["model"] to the deployment's model_name when the client omits it, so the common curl (-F file=@meeting.wav -F exclusive=true) works, and the config forwards the field verbatim to the pod
  • Because the id now contains the pyannote prefix, provider detection has a secondary signal: KNOWN_PROVIDERS matching on the id works again ("pyannote" in "pyannote/community-1"). The OpenAPI path probe (/v1/diarize in paths) remains the primary signal since it does not depend on the ConfigMap id being set correctly (see Slice G)

docs.title: C2. Full 7-layer vertical slice, not pass-through
docs.text: pass_through_endpoints targets a static URL and cannot resolve the controller-discovered pod api_base, so the route gets the full treatment: proxy route slice -> route_llm_request dispatch -> router methods -> SDK functions -> HTTP handler -> litellm/llms/pyannote/ config. This is the same call the VSA-PLAN made for the OmniVoice routes; the reasoning carries over verbatim.

docs.title: C3. Multipart in, JSON out; jobs and GET-poll out of scope for slice 1
docs.text:
Coro's transport delta from the cloud contract is multipart file + form fields instead of JSON body with url (fetching arbitrary URLs from a private cluster is an SSRF hole; the cloud requires a URL because it is multi-tenant). LiteLLM already parses multipart at Layer 1 (get_form_data), and the handler already forwards form_data + files (voice-clone path). The config builds the multipart POST with files={"file": (...)} and every form field passed through verbatim. No OpenAI param mapping is attempted: the diarize surface is not an OpenAI surface, and inventing one would extend a contract a third party owns, which is the exact error coro ADR 0015 rejects.

GET /v1/jobs/{jobId} is deliberately out of scope for slice 1: coro's POST returns the completed job inline (synchronous engine, hundreds-x real time), so a poll loop is a compatibility nicety, and coro keeps only the last 128 jobs in memory, so the gateway must not advertise durable retrieval. The route can be added later without touching the existing layers (new dispatch key + GET route in the slice).

docs.title: C4. Unsupported-field 400s pass through verbatim
docs.text: Coro rejects 14 DiarizeRequest fields with the spec's own ValidationErrorResponse shape, per field. The gateway does not intercept, translate, or pre-validate those: the 400 body is the vendor contract, and clients written against pyannoteAI's documented behavior read it as-is. The config declares no get_supported_openai_params mapping beyond the pass-through of form fields; drop_params does not apply because there is no OpenAI parameter vocabulary on this surface.

docs.title: C5. New mode value: diarization
docs.text:
model_info.mode today carries chat/embedding/completion/ image_generation/audio_transcription/rerank/moderations (and audio_speech via the controller's to_litellm_mode). Diarization is not transcription: coro's diarize returns speaker turns only, and mode drives both UI grouping and the controller's non-chat routing decisions. Register mode: "diarization":

  • litellm/types/utils.py: add "diarization" to the ModelInfo.mode Literal (the one in the model-prices schema block) and to supported_endpoints vocabulary if the dashboard's mode filter reads from there
  • litellm/proxy/_types.py ModelInfo: widen its Literal["embedding", "chat", "completion"] to include "diarization" (this is the class Deployment.model_info validates through litellm/types/router.py; check both Literals before relying on the value)
  • Controller _PATH_MODES: add ("/v1/diarize", "diarization") before the chat guard, following the ordering rule in detect_mode_from_paths (most specific first; a chat-capable server that also exposes diarize stays chat). Coro's OpenAPI at /openapi.json does advertise /v1/diarize, so the probe path already works.

The mode string is cosmetic for routing (dispatch is by route, not mode), but it keeps the Admin UI model list honest and gives the controller a value its tests can assert on.

docs.title: C6. Auth: no header injection
docs.text: Coro ships no authentication by design (ADR 0013 accepts the lint finding). validate_environment returns headers unchanged (Content-Type set by the multipart encoder). LiteLLM virtual-key auth sits in front at the proxy layer, which is the whole point of the gateway. No PYANNOTE_API_KEY env plumbing.

docs.title: C7. Cost: no pricing in slice 1
docs.text: Diarization has no token vocabulary. Pricing, if ever needed, is per-second of audio, which is a provider_specific_entry concern in the pricing resolver (controller/pricing/), not a token-price entry. Defer; log spend rows with zero cost and a follow-up ticket if billing matters. (coro's /v1/listen and /v1/audio/transcriptions surfaces keep their existing paths; this slice touches only /v1/diarize.)

docs.title: C8. Slice placement per oicm-slices.md
docs.text:
• Routes: new sibling slice litellm/proxy/diarization_routes.py (NOT inline in proxy_server.py), mounted next to the existing OICM router mounts at the bottom of proxy_server.py (after client_distribution_router), plus two thin mount lines
  • SDK functions: litellm/endpoints/diarization/ mirroring litellm/endpoints/voice/ (__init__.py re-export + main.py), re-exported lazily via litellm/__init__.py.__getattr__ so litellm.diarize resolves
  • Provider config: litellm/llms/pyannote/{common_utils.py,diarization/} following the hamsa/omnivoice dir shape
  • Registry: litellm/llms/oicm_providers/registry.py gains get_provider_diarization_config; ProviderConfigManager in litellm/utils.py delegates with one clean line
  • Drop-detection: extend tests/unit/proxy/test_oicm_drop_detection.py with test_diarization_routes_router_is_mounted_on_app and test_diarization_sdk_slice_wired_into_litellm_namespace

docs.title: C9. Response passthrough, not typed models
docs.text: The gateway returns the pod's DiarizationJob JSON as-is (minus hop-by-hop headers), same as create_voice returns the pod's JSON dict. Do not build Pydantic response models in the gateway: the contract's single source of truth is the pinned spec fixture in coro's tree, and duplicating it here would violate the DRY rule the coro ADRs are built on. Response models, if ever needed for the dashboard's generated types, are generated from the proxy's own OpenAPI export, which derives from the route's declared response shape.

docs.title: Slice A: types + registration (no runtime behavior)
docs.text:
1. litellm/types/utils.py: LlmProviders.PYANNOTE = "pyannote"; add "diarization" to the ModelInfoBase.mode Literal and to CallTypes/CallTypesLiteral (adiarize/diarize)
  2. litellm/proxy/_types.py: widen the ModelInfo.mode Literal
  3. litellm/constants.py: add /v1/diarize to API_ROUTE_TO_CALL_TYPES mapped to the new call types (both with and without the /v1 prefix, matching how /v1/audio/speech is double-listed)
  4. litellm/proxy/_types.py: add /diarize and /v1/diarize to LiteLLMRoutes.litellm_native_routes. This is SEPARATE from step 3 and is the one that governs authorization: API_ROUTE_TO_CALL_TYPES resolves call types (guardrails, spend), while llm_api_routes is a snapshot built at LiteLLMRoutes class-definition time. A route missing from every group is mounted and callable by the master key but 403s for every key_type=llm_api key. This was missed on the first implementation and shipped broken on 2026-10-19; tests/unit/proxy/test_oicm_drop_detection.py::test_fork_inference_routes_are_reachable_by_llm_api_keys now enforces it. If the route is a pod diagnostic rather than inference, list it in the router's OPS_ONLY_ROUTES instead of widening the allowlist
  5. litellm/utils.py: add get_provider_diarization_config to ProviderConfigManager, delegating to the registry slice
  6. litellm/llms/oicm_providers/registry.py: add get_provider_diarization_config(provider) returning PyannoteDiarizationConfig() for PYANNOTE
  7. Tests: registry dispatch test in tests/test_litellm/llms/oicm_providers/test_oicm_provider_registry.py

docs.title: Slice B: provider config (Layer 6)
docs.text:
litellm/llms/pyannote/
├── __init__.py
├── common_utils.py          ← PyannoteModelInfo(BaseLLMModelInfo)
└── diarization/
    ├── __init__.py
    └── transformation.py   ← PyannoteDiarizationConfig

PyannoteModelInfo: get_models returns ("pyannote/community-1",), the serving id the ADEO deployment accepts (the spec enum value community-1 is the bare-run default and is rejected by the renamed deployment; precision-2/precision-3 are cloud-only, the pod rejects them, so the gateway does not advertise them); get_api_base reads PYANNOTE_API_BASE (dev convenience only; prod comes from the controller's litellm_params). get_provider_info returns ProviderSpecificModelInfo(endpoint="/v1/diarize", mode="diarization").

PyannoteDiarizationConfig(BaseDiarizationConfig) - new base class, see Slice C. Methods:

  • get_complete_url: f"{api_base}/v1/diarize". The controller registers the bare ClusterIP for native-base providers; decide whether pyannote joins NATIVE_BASE_PROVIDERS (bare base, config appends /v1/diarize) or keeps the /v1 suffix convention. Decision: join NATIVE_BASE_PROVIDERS - coro serves other native surfaces (/v1/listen, WebSocket) from the same pod, so the bare base is the honest registration
  • validate_environment: no-op header return (C6)
  • transform_diarization_request: builds multipart. Inputs: the parsed form fields dict + the (filename, bytes, content_type) file tuple. Output: DiarizationRequestData(form_data=form_fields_minus_file, files={"file": file_tuple}). Every form field passes through verbatim, including model, exclusive, and the 14 unsupported fields (their 400s come back from the pod, C4)
  • transform_diarization_response: parses the JSON body and returns it as a dict (C9); attaches _hidden_params from response headers where the success-path header builder expects them

docs.title: Slice C: new handler entry point (Layer 5)
docs.text:
Add diarization_handler/async_diarization_handler to litellm/llms/custom_httpx/llm_http_handler.py next to voice_handler, because no existing handler takes (form_data, files) in and returns JSON out: the TTS handler returns binary, the voice handler takes JSON in. The shape mirrors voice_handler: validate_environment -> get_complete_url -> transform_diarization_request -> async_httpx_client.post(url, data=..., files=...) -> transform_diarization_response.

New base class BaseDiarizationConfig at litellm/llms/base_llm/diarization/transformation.py mirroring BaseAudioTranscriptionConfig's abstract-method set, plus DiarizationRequestData TypedDict (form_data: dict[str, str], files: dict[str, tuple[str, bytes, str]]). The multipart-heavy shape is why diarization is not squeezed into BaseAudioTranscriptionConfig: transcription's request data carries a single audio file and OpenAI-mapped optional params, while diarize forwards a whole form surface verbatim.

docs.title: Slice D: SDK functions (Layer 4)
docs.text:
litellm/endpoints/diarization/main.py:

  • adiarize(*args, **kwargs): executor wrapper exactly like acreate_voice
  • @client def diarize(model, file, exclusive=None, custom_llm_provider=None, api_base=None, ...): get_llm_provider -> get_litellm_params -> ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_diarization_config -> diarization_handler(...). The file parameter is the (filename, bytes, content_type) tuple (the route already normalized the upload to that shape at Layer 1)
  • __init__.py re-exports adiarize/diarize; litellm/__init__.py.__getattr__ gains the two names

docs.title: Slice E: router methods (Layer 3)
docs.text: litellm/router.py next to acreate_voice/_acreate_voice: adiarize() (public, fallbacks) and _adiarize() (deployment resolution + litellm.adiarize(**data)), borrowing _update_kwargs_before_fallbacks, async_get_available_deployment, _update_kwargs_with_deployment.

docs.title: Slice F: dispatch + route (Layers 1-2)
docs.text:
litellm/proxy/route_llm_request.py: add "adiarize" to the route_type Literal and "adiarize": "/v1/diarize" to ROUTE_ENDPOINT_MAPPING.

litellm/proxy/diarization_routes.py (new slice):

  • @router.post("/v1/diarize") + @router.post("/diarize") (double-listing matches every other audio route)
  • Handler mirrors audio_speech_clone's multipart flow: get_form_data, strip file, add_litellm_data_to_request, model resolution (data["model"] from the form, defaulted to the deployment's model_name (pyannote/community-1) when the client omits it — required, because the pod's hardcoded community-1 Form default is rejected on the renamed ADEO deployment), pre_call_hook(call_type="adiarize"), route_request(route_type="adiarize"), custom headers via ProxyBaseLLMRequestProcessing.get_custom_headers, return JSONResponse of the pod body (C9)
  • Mount in proxy_server.py next to the other OICM slice mounts: from litellm.proxy.diarization_routes import router as oicm_diarization_router + app.include_router(oicm_diarization_router)
  • Route allowlist: gateway/routes/allowlist.py and backend/routes/allowlist.py both list routes (e.g. /openapi.json); check whether the hardened surface gates audio routes and add /v1/diarize if so

docs.title: Slice G: discovery controller
docs.text:
Facts that drive the changes (verified against coro's served surface):

  • coro publishes /openapi.json (ADR 0013) whose paths include /v1/diarize, /v1/audio/transcriptions, /v1/listen, /v1/jobs/{jobId} and /health - so the controller's _probe_openapi_paths works unchanged
  • coro serves no /v1/models, so _discover_model_ids has no owned_by source: the deployment ConfigMap MODEL_ID is the model-id source. The coro workload's ConfigMap must set MODEL_ID=pyannote/community-1 (the same string the pod's CORO_PYANNOTE_DIARIZE_MODEL_ID is baked to, so the registered model_name, the pod's accepted id, and what the pod echoes all agree)
  • the model id (pyannote/community-1) now contains the pyannote substring, so KNOWN_PROVIDERS matching the id works as a secondary signal; the OpenAPI path probe stays primary since it does not depend on the ConfigMap id being set

oicm-litellm-layer/controller/models.py:

  1. detect_provider: add a path-based branch after the KNOWN_PROVIDERS loop, mirroring the paddlex branch: if "/v1/diarize" in paths and CHAT_PATH not in paths: return "pyannote". Also add "pyannote" to KNOWN_PROVIDERS — with the serving id pyannote/community-1 the id-substring match fires, making the ConfigMap id a redundant but harmless secondary signal; the path probe remains primary because it holds even when MODEL_ID is misconfigured
  2. NATIVE_BASE_PROVIDERS: add "pyannote" (C8/B decision above)
  3. _PATH_MODES: add ("/v1/diarize", "diarization") before TRANSCRIPTION_PATH. Order matters here as nowhere else: a coro pod serves both transcriptions and diarize, and the table returns its first hit, so diarize-first classifies coro pods as diarization. Pods serving transcriptions without diarize (vLLM ASR, vibevoice) are unaffected, and chat-capable servers never reach the table (chat guard)
  4. _NAME_MODES name fallback: add ("diariz", "diarization") token match for probe-failure fallback
  5. A coro deployment also serves /v1/audio/transcriptions; exposing that surface through the gateway is a separate slice (the OpenAI-compatible route, not this one) and is deliberately out of scope here

oicm-litellm-layer/controller/litellm_client.py _register_payload needs no change: it already stamps provider/model_id (pyannote/pyannote/community-1, the double prefix being what makes the first-slash split land on the pod's accepted id) and mode through. Verify the payload's model_info.mode="diarization" passes the Deployment validation (Slice A widening makes it legal).

Controller tests: extend tests/controller/test_models.py with the new detection rows (path-based pyannote detection from a coro-shaped path set; diarize-before-transcription ordering; the ("diariz", ...) name fallback; pyannote/community-1 register payload), and test_local_deployments.py with a coro-shaped openapi.json probe fixture (paths including /v1/diarize, /v1/audio/transcriptions, /health; no /v1/models).

docs.title: Slice H: docs + usage guide
docs.text:
• This document (plan/choices) in custom-providers/
  • usage-guides/PYANNOTE_DIARIZATION_GUIDE.md with curl examples against the live gateway (multipart file upload, exclusive=true, the per-field 400 behavior)
  • mkdocs.yml nav + docs-map.md entries for both
  • custom-providers/README.md provider table gains a pyannote row

docs.title: Implementation order and verification
docs.text:
1. Slice A (types + registration) - compile-only, run registry tests
  2. Slice B+C (config + handler) - unit tests with mocked httpx asserting the multipart POST shape (form fields verbatim, files={"file": ...}, URL {api_base}/v1/diarize)
  3. Slice D+E (SDK + router) - unit tests asserting dispatch to the handler for pyannote/... models
  4. Slice F (dispatch + route + mount) - drop-detection tests green; curl the live proxy with dev_config.yaml + a manual pyannote/pyannote/community-1 deployment entry pointing at a running coro pod, showing the pod's DiarizationJob body round-tripped verbatim with the served id pyannote/community-1 in the response (both command and output recorded per the repo's proof-of-fix convention)
  5. Slice G (controller) - controller test suite; on-cluster: coro deployment registered automatically, model_name and mode verified in /v1/model/info
  6. Slice H (docs) - make docs builds clean

Mutation-testing standard per repo CLAUDE.md applies to each slice's tests: the registry dispatch test must fail when the pyannote branch is removed, the multipart test must fail when a form field is dropped, and the drop-detection tests must fail when the router mount or lazy re-export is deleted.

docs.title: Risks / open questions
docs.text:
• model form field: the gateway defaults it to the deployment's model_name when the client omits it, so the common curl works; but it is NOT optional at the pod on the ADEO deployment. Coro's route keeps the hardcoded Form(default="community-1") while the accepted id is settings-driven (verified at coro HEAD): the default and the accepted id disagree once CORO_PYANNOTE_DIARIZE_MODEL_ID=pyannote/community-1 is baked, so a request that lets the default through gets the spec-shaped per-field 400 naming the accepted id. The gateway defaulting the field is what shields clients from that; a coro follow-up could make the Form default track the setting, but the gateway must not depend on it. A client explicitly sending model=precision-2 or model=community-1 gets the pod's own per-field 400, which is the vendor contract behaving
  • Timeout: coro diarizes at hundreds-x real time; a 2h meeting is ~3-5s, but gateway timeout should default generously (e.g. 600s) and be per-deployment overridable via litellm_params.timeout
  • excluded-field drift: if pyannoteAI's spec adds a DiarizeRequest field, coro's conformance suite fails first (upstream pin refresh), and the gateway passes the new field through verbatim (no gateway change needed) - the layering means spec drift is a coro concern, not a gateway one
  • Streaming/long-audio: out of scope; coro's sync job returns inline and the pod holds no durable queue

docs.title: Speaker Embeddings in /v1/diarize — Work Plan
docs.text: Request source: consumer-team feedback (2026-11-03): return per-speaker voice vectors from the pyannote deployment for their voice-ID flow (they match a vector to a confirmed name, i.e. enrolment by confirmation). Status: DELIVERED 2026-11-03 — live on the cluster. speakrs 0.7.1 (commit cf9e45b, wheel speakrs-0.7.1-cp311-abi3-manylinux_2_35_x86_64.whl), coro 00bcdcf on jya0-v1.5.2, image ffdabc3508f1, pod j-d4398150-0202-4e1c-ae9a-41be01288fd3-86cfd784fd-gcc9m. Live check passed: keys == speakers, 256 floats, revision 67f963b6…, and the default response stays byte-identical without the flag. Related: PYANNOTE_DIARIZATION_PROVIDER_PLAN.md (original provider slice), usage-guides/PYANNOTE_DIARIZATION_GUIDE.md (current contract + benchmarks).

docs.title: 1. What was asked
docs.text:
Add per-speaker voice vectors to the /v1/diarize response for the consumer's voice-ID flow (they match a vector to a confirmed name, i.e. enrolment by confirmation). v2 scope decision: the extension is opt-in via a request flag so the official pyannoteai-sdk client keeps working byte-identically forever; consumers who send the flag get:

"output": {
  "diarization": [...],
  "exclusiveDiarization": [...],
  "speakerEmbeddings": {
    "SPEAKER_00": [256 floats],
    "SPEAKER_01": [256 floats],
    "SPEAKER_02": null
  },
  "embeddingModel": {
    "id": "pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1",
    "revision": "<pinned HF commit sha>",
    "dim": 256
  }
}

Rules from the request:

  1. Additive only — existing fields unchanged, current consumers unaffected.
  2. Keys match labels — speakerEmbeddings keys are exactly the SPEAKER_xx strings appearing in exclusiveDiarization.
  3. Padded rows are null — a zero-padded speaker row must serialize as null, not a vector of zeros.
  4. Revision pinned and returned — vectors from different model revisions are not comparable; consumers must be told before an upgrade so members re-record voice IDs.

Cost: none extra at inference time (vectors already computed internally); response grows ~3 KB per speaker.

docs.title: 2. Where the vectors live today (verified in source)
docs.text:
The engine computes the right artifact already and throws it away at the SDK boundary. Chain:

Layer File (branch master = speakrs 0.7) What exists What's missing Engine src/pipeline/clustering.rs:136 weighted_centroids() One weighted 256-d centroid per kept speaker (VBx posterior-weighted mean of chunk embeddings — a soft assignment, better than a hard mean) Returned nowhere; TrainingEmbeddings::cluster() returns only ChunkSpeakerClusters Engine src/inference/embedding.rs:42 EMBEDDING_WIDTH = 256 — Engine src/pipeline/types/data.rs:274 DiarizationResult carries embeddings: ChunkEmbeddings (per-chunk) + hard_clusters No per-speaker centroid field Engine src/segment.rs:53 Speaker labels minted as SPEAKER_{idx:02} from the activation column index — (label ↔ centroid row identity, see §4) SDK crates/speakrs-sdk/src/pipeline.rs:319 to_diarization() — Discards everything but segments; must carry centroids + labels Bindings crates/speakrs-python/src/results.rs PyDiarizationResult segments, exclusive_segments, speakers, model_revision getters No speaker_embeddings getter coro coro/backends/diarization/speakrs.py diarize_pcm_full() returns (segments, exclusive_segments) Must return embeddings + revision too coro coro/api/pyannote/diarize.py pyannoteAI-exact DiarizationJobOutput Add the two new output fields LiteLLM litellm/llms/pyannote/diarization/transformation.py:86 transform_diarization_response = raw_response.json() — pure passthrough Nothing. New fields flow through unchanged.

docs.title: 3. Is this what the pyannoteAI cloud endpoint provides?
docs.text:
No — and that is fine, but it must be a conscious decision.

Checked against the pinned official pyannoteAI OpenAPI spec (coro/tests/api/pyannote/pyannoteai-openapi-v1.json, fetched from docs.pyannote.ai 2026-10-19). The official DiarizationJobOutput schema defines exactly:

Field In official spec In our response after this change diarization (required) yes yes (unchanged) exclusiveDiarization yes yes (unchanged) confidence optional 400-rejected (engine can't produce) speechProbability / crosstalkProbability / speakerProbability optional 400-rejected wordLevelTranscription / turnLevelTranscription optional 400-rejected (use /v1/audio/transcriptions) error / warning optional warning yes; error unused speakerEmbeddings absent new, ours embeddingModel absent new, ours

So the response becomes a superset of the cloud contract: every official field keeps its exact shape, and two self-hosted extensions are added inside output. This is the same posture the route already has for transport (file upload instead of the cloud's presigned-URL url) — exact where the spec speaks, explicit where self-hosting legitimately diverges. Consequences we accept:

  • The official pyannoteai-sdk client ignores unknown output keys (dicts), so it keeps working. LiteLLM's provider is passthrough, so it keeps working. No existing consumer can break (additive JSON keys).
  • The spec-conformance suite must be updated deliberately: it currently asserts our DiarizationJobOutput matches the pinned schema field-for-field. It must move to a superset assertion: official fields stay pinned (shape + required-ness), the two extensions get their own pinned assertions (presence, key-matching rule, dim, null rule), so a future upstream spec refresh still fails loudly on drift.
  • If pyannoteAI ever ships embeddings upstream, we reconcile then (rename/align — likely trivial since our shape matches their request template).

docs.title: 4. Design decisions (v2 — flag-gated, official-SDK-compatible)
docs.text:
1. Opt-in via a body flag: embeddings (optional, default absent). Replaces the earlier always-on idea after review. Rationale:
  2. Official SDK compatibility is the hard requirement: the official pyannoteai-sdk client posts exactly the spec's DiarizeRequest fields. An optional extra field that is absent by default keeps byte-identical requests from the official client passing through the gateway untouched — nothing to opt out of, nothing to strip.
  3. The extension behaves exactly like our transport divergence (file multipart instead of the spec's url): the request surface stays spec-shaped, self-hosted extensions are additive options.
  4. Absent → spec-exact response (no new keys at all). Present → the two additive output fields. Consumers who don't ask see zero change.
  5. embeddings=false behaves exactly like absent (spec-exact), so the flag never has three states to reason about.
  6. Where the flag lives end-to-end (all layers follow the same rule: absent means absent):
  7. coro route: embeddings: bool = Form(default=False) — the only new request-side line; not added to _UNSUPPORTED_FIELDS (it is our own extension, not a spec field we reject).
  8. coro pipeline: diarize_full(audio, *, exclusive, embeddings) — one keyword with a default; non-speakrs backends ignore it (they already raise for diarize_full itself, so no new error paths).
  9. speakrs wheel 0.7.1: zero request-side change. The result object grows a speaker_embeddings getter (always computed by the engine anyway, ~µs) and coro reads it only when the flag is set and otherwise serializes exactly as today. This keeps the wheel API additive-only — no config, no breaking method signatures.
  10. LiteLLM: zero change. The provider is already a multipart passthrough (transform_diarization_request forwards form_fields verbatim; transform_diarization_response returns raw_response.json()). An embeddings=true form field flows to the pod; new output keys flow back.
  11. Which vector: the weighted centroid (unchanged from v1). weighted_centroids() — VBx posterior-weighted mean of chunk embeddings, the representation the engine itself uses for assignment. Not L2-normalized; document and keep byte-stable across versions. Note: this matches the official pyannote.audio 4.x DiarizeOutput.speaker_embeddings semantics (hard-mean centroids there, posterior-weighted here — both 256-d wespeaker-family embeddings, labels-order-aligned rows, zero-pad → null).
  12. Label ↔ row identity guarantee (unchanged). SPEAKER_%02k ↔ centroid row k by construction (src/segment.rs:53 mints labels from the same activation column index the reconstruction step uses); pinned by a unit test.
  13. Null vs pruned (unchanged). speakrs prunes sub-threshold speakers, so in practice every label gets a vector; the all-zero-row → null rule is implemented anyway to match the requested contract.
  14. Revision source (unchanged). model_revision = pinned commit 67f963b6…; embeddingModel.id = pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1 (internal engine id; the request model field stays the serving id pyannote/community-1); dim = 256 from EMBEDDING_WIDTH — from a constant, never probed from data (the spike's dim-probe bug fixed).
  15. Corrections to the requester's runtime table (their guide assumes pyannote.audio 4.x on torch): torch.set_flush_denormal — N/A, our engine is Rust + CUDA. PYANNOTE_METRICS_ENABLED / HF_HUB_DISABLE_TELEMETRY — N/A, no telemetry exists in the Rust stack. "Pin the revision" — already true since 0.7 (MODEL_REVISION constant). "Short calls under 90 s" — trivially met: 30–45 s enrolment audio diarizes in <1 s engine time (727× single-stream RTFx measured).
  16. What we do NOT take from the consumer's spike (pyannote-service.zip, reviewed): his revision="local" default (we return the real pinned sha), his num_speakers pass-through (our contract 400s it — his request example doesn't send it anyway), and his data-probed dim (constant here). His core insight — return the embeddings the model already computes — is correct and is what this plan implements on the production engine.

docs.title: 6. Official pyannote SDK compatibility (the v2 driver)
docs.text:
The official pyannoteai-sdk client must keep working unchanged, forever. Verified mechanics:

  • The SDK posts exactly the spec's DiarizeRequest fields — it will never send embeddings. Absent flag → coro's Form(default=False) → the response contains only spec-shaped keys. Byte-identical to today.
  • The SDK's retrieve()/response handling tolerates extra keys on its own (it returns plain dicts), and we never add keys unless asked anyway.
  • LiteLLM passes unknown request fields through as multipart form fields (transform_diarization_request copies form_fields verbatim) and returns the pod's JSON verbatim (transform_diarization_response) — the flag and the new response fields need zero gateway changes.
  • Curl/plain-HTTP consumers add one form field: -F embeddings=true.
  • The spike's /v1/embed (single-range voice-print) is out of scope for the production route; his notebooks can keep using his local spike for that, or a follow-up adds ranges to the same flag.

docs.title: 7. Risks / open questions
docs.text:
• Cluster fast-path (< 2 training rows): synthesized centroid must still match label indexing; covered by 1.5 tests.
  • Byte-stability of vectors across patch versions: we pin the engine wheel version in the image; a future speakrs upgrade that changes clustering defaults silently invalidates consumer enrolment vectors — must be called out in the guide's upgrade note (§5.1) and in the deployment manifest.
  • Response size: 8-speaker meeting ≈ 8×256×~9 chars ≈ 20 KB — well within JSON response norms; no pagination needed.
  • Open: should embeddingModel.id be the internal engine id (pyannote/speaker-diarization-community-1) as the requester wrote, or the serving id (pyannote/community-1)? Plan assumes the requester's literal (internal id) — confirm with them only if it matters for their vector-comparison logic (it shouldn't; the revision is the load-bearing field).

docs.title: Gateway Field-Drop Investigation — why LiteLLM drops the PaddleX extensions
docs.text: Status: OPEN · needs human/operator inspection of the LiteLLM deployment Date: 2026-08-20 Author: HPS mistral-OCR integration Scope: this document is a problem statement + inspection checklist. It does not contain conclusions about the gateway internals — those must be verified by the reader against the live LiteLLM deployment at /home/jyao/ADEO/service/litellm and the running proxy.

docs.title: 1. Problem statement
docs.text:
When a request reaches the PaddleX HPS backend directly (no gateway), all three PaddleX-extension behaviors work:

Field Direct backend result confidence_scores_granularity="block" (stock Mistral) 16/16 blocks carry scores include_native_labels=true (extension) 16/16 blocks carry a native label threshold=0.3..0.99 (extension) block count changes with the value

When the same request is sent through the LiteLLM gateway (https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/ocr, key sk-05132025), the result differs:

Field Via gateway result Behaviour confidence_scores_granularity="block" (stock Mistral) 16/16 blocks carry scores FORWARDED include_native_labels=true (extension) 0/16 blocks carry a label DROPPED threshold=0.3/0.5/0.7/0.8/0.99 (extension) 16 blocks at every value DROPPED

Concluding statement: the gateway drops the two PaddleX-extension top-level request fields (include_native_labels, threshold), while it forwards the stock Mistral field (confidence_scores_granularity). Because the backend honours all three when hit directly, the drop is attributable to the LiteLLM gateway layer, not the backend. The exact mechanism is not determined here; the goal of this document is to let an operator find it.

docs.title: 2. What we already know (facts, verified directly against the backend)
docs.text:
1. The backend deploy/hps/api_compat/mistral_ocr_api/schema.py declares these fields on PaddleXOCRRequest:
  2. threshold: Optional[Any] (default None)
  3. include_native_labels: Optional[bool] (default False)
  4. layout_*, include_paddlex_metadata, filter_overlap_boxes, etc.
  5. service.process_ocr reads them via as_optional(getattr(request, ...)) and threads them into ConvertOptions / run_layout_detection.
  6. Stock Mistral field confidence_scores_granularity IS part of the official mistralai OCRRequest DTO (verified in mistralai/client/models/ocrrequest.py), so it is expected to pass through a schema-aware gateway.
  7. The extension fields are not part of the official OCRRequest DTO. A LiteLLM proxy that validates/strips the request body against the official schema would therefore remove them before forwarding to the backend.

docs.title: 3. Hypotheses to confirm/reject (each with a way to test)
docs.text: # Hypothesis How to confirm H1 LiteLLM validates the request body against the stock Mistral OCR schema and strips unknown top-level fields before forwarding. Inspect whether the /v1/ocr route applies a pydantic model/schema to the request body, and whether it serializes back only known fields. H2 The PP-DocLayoutV3 route/model entry has a passthrough or "allowed params" allow-list that excludes the extensions. Inspect the LiteLLM config (config.yaml / model_list entry for PP-DocLayoutV3) for an allow-list, allowed_*, or passthrough keys. H3 A LiteLLM middleware / convert_* hook rewrites or prunes the body before the request reaches the provider call. Grep the codebase for where the /v1/ocr request body is read and where it is forwarded, and whether any transform drops keys. H4 The gateway is not actually running our latest backend image (the one with include_native_labels) — but this is UNLIKELY since confidence_scores_granularity works. Confirm the backend image/digest the gateway routes to and that it includes the Option-A code. H5 LiteLLM requires the extension fields to be declared in the model's request_options/custom request_* config to pass them through. Check the PP-DocLayoutV3 model config for request_options/custom body overrides.

docs.title: 4.1 Locate the OCR route handler
docs.text:
• Find where /v1/ocr is routed: grep aocr, ocr, "/v1/ocr" in litellm/main.py and litellm/router.py.
  • Identify the request model class used for the OCR route (if any). It likely lives under litellm/ocr/ (e.g. ocr/request.py, ocr/types/...).
  • Print the fields of that request model: 
    grep -rn "class.*OCRRequest\|class.*OCROcrV1\|include_native_labels\|confidence_scores_granularity" litellm/ocr/

docs.title: 4.2 Determine whether unknown fields are stripped
docs.text:
• Look at how the request model is converted to a dict for the upstream call (model_dump(..., exclude_unset=...), exclude_none=, or manual field assembly). If it uses an explicit field list or exclude_unset, extension fields sent by the caller are dropped unless they are model fields.
  • Search for exclude_unset, exclude_none, model_dump, .get( on the OCR request object in the handler.

docs.title: 4.3 Check the PP-DocLayoutV3 model config on the gateway
docs.text:
• Open the config file the proxy loaded (e.g. config.yaml, or whatever --config points to at startup).
  • Locate the PP-DocLayoutV3 model group entry.
  • Look for: allowed_parameters / allowed_arguments, passthrough, request_options, additional_headers, drop_params, or any body transformation. Note whether it differs from the Qwen/... entries that succeed with extra fields.

docs.title: 4.4 Enable debug logging / trace the request
docs.text:
• Run (or inspect) the proxy with LITELLM_LOG=DEBUG (or --detailed_debug).
  • Send one OCR request with include_native_labels=true and threshold=0.3, then read the logs for the incoming body and the body sent upstream to PP-DocLayoutV3. Diff the two: the field that disappears is the one LiteLLM dropped and the log line naming it will show the mechanism (validation vs. allow-list vs. transform).

docs.title: 4.5 Verify the backend version behind the gateway
docs.text: • Confirm the gateway forwards to an HPS pod running the image that includes the Option-A schema. Quick check: hit the backend /v1/ocr directly (bypass gateway) with include_native_labels=true — if it returns labels, the backend is fine and the drop is upstream.

docs.title: 5. Reproducer (for whoever inspects)
docs.text:
Save the image to a file first, then send the two field-sets through the gateway:

# image path: deploy/hps/tests/mig_inference/input/08_document_scan.jpg
DATA_URI="data:image/jpeg;base64,$(base64 -w0 deploy/hps/tests/mig_inference/input/08_document_scan.jpg)"

# STOCK field (expected: forwarded -> 16/16 with confidence)
curl -sk https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/ocr -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-05132025' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"PP-DocLayoutV3\",\"document\":{\"type\":\"image_url\",\"image_url\":\"$DATA_URI\"},\"include_blocks\":true,\"confidence_scores_granularity\":\"block\"}"

# EXTENSION field (expected: dropped -> 0/16 labels)
curl -sk https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/ocr -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-05132025' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"PP-DocLayoutV3\",\"document\":{\"type\":\"image_url\",\"image_url\":\"$DATA_URI\"},\"include_blocks\":true,\"include_native_labels\":true}"

# EXTENSION field (expected: dropped -> 16 blocks)
curl -sk https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/ocr -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-05132025' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"PP-DocLayoutV3\",\"document\":{\"type\":\"image_url\",\"image_url\":\"$DATA_URI\"},\"include_blocks\":true,\"threshold\":0.99}"

The reusable probe is also committed at deploy/hps/tests/test_gateway_ocr.py.

docs.title: 6. What a fix will look like (once the mechanism is found)
docs.text:
• If H1/H3 (schema validation strips unknowns): add the extension fields to the OCR request model LiteLLM uses (or switch to a passthrough body for the PP-DocLayoutV3 route) so include_native_labels/threshold survive.
  • If H2 (allow-list): add the fields to the model entry's allow-list.
  • If H5 (request_options): declare the fields under the route's request_options so LiteLLM forwards them verbatim.

The backend needs no change; it already declares and honours the fields.

docs.title: 7. Blocking question for the operator
docs.text: Does the LiteLLM gateway that serves https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/ocr intend to pass arbitrary PaddleX-extension request fields through to the PP-DocLayoutV3 backend? If yes, the extension fields must be allow-listed / added to the OCR request schema at the gateway. If no, callers must hit the backend directly (or via a gateway that is configured to passthrough) to use include_native_labels/threshold.

docs.title: Inception TTS/STT: Gateway vs Pod-Direct Parity Check
docs.text:
Goal: Verify that the request and response shapes from the LiteLLM gateway for inception TTS and STT match the shapes when calling the inception pods directly from within the cluster

Date: 2026-08-03

docs.title: Gateway path
docs.text:
External curl to the LiteLLM gateway:

https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech        (TTS)
https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/transcriptions (STT)

Auth: Authorization: Bearer sk-05132025

docs.title: Pod-direct path
docs.text:
Python3 urllib.request from inside a litellm-proxy pod (adeo-litellm/litellm-proxy-7c9bb48cbb-56pfg; namespace was mlops at the time) to the inception pods directly:

http://s-9aff17c0-988c-4cb1-98b9-e99faa6e9cdc.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080/v1/audio/speech        (TTS)
http://s-e2e85fcc-c58a-4d41-91f7-1fffe6fc882b.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080/v1/audio/transcriptions (STT)

No auth header (inception pods don't require authentication)

docs.title: Model config (from /model/info admin endpoint)
docs.text:
inception-tts:
  litellm_params:
    api_base: http://s-9aff17c0-988c-4cb1-98b9-e99faa6e9cdc.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080/v1
    model: inception/inception-tts
    drop_params: true

inception-stt:
  litellm_params:
    api_base: http://s-e2e85fcc-c58a-4d41-91f7-1fffe6fc882b.adeo.svc.cluster.local:8080/v1
    model: inception/inception-stt
    drop_params: true

docs.title: Request shape
docs.text:
Field Gateway (user sends) Pod-direct (we send) LiteLLM transforms to model inception-tts inception/inception-tts inception/inception-tts (from litellm_params.model) input "Hello world, this is a parity test." same same (passed through) voice "alloy" "alloy" "alloy" (default if not provided) Content-Type application/json application/json application/json

The gateway maps the user-facing model name inception-tts to the internal litellm_params.model value inception/inception-tts before forwarding to the pod. The request body shape is identical: OpenAI-compatible JSON with model, input, voice fields.

docs.title: Response shape
docs.text:
Aspect Gateway Pod-direct HTTP status 200 200 Content-Type audio/mpeg audio/mpeg Body MP3 binary MP3 binary Body size 16080 bytes 15960 bytes (first test: 15432)

The body size difference is expected: the inception TTS model is diffusion-based and non-deterministic. Two pod-direct calls produced different sizes (15432 and 15960), confirming the variance is from the model, not from the gateway.

docs.title: Response headers
docs.text:
Gateway adds LiteLLM tracking headers not present in pod-direct response:

Header Gateway Pod-direct server absent uvicorn x-audio-format absent mp3 content-length absent (chunked) 15960 x-litellm-call-id present absent x-litellm-model-id present absent x-litellm-model-api-base present absent x-litellm-version present absent x-litellm-key-spend present absent x-litellm-response-duration-ms present absent x-litellm-callback-duration-ms present absent Security headers present (frame-options, CSP, etc.) absent

The gateway strips pod-native headers (server, x-audio-format) and adds LiteLLM tracking + security headers. The audio content itself is equivalent.

docs.title: TTS verdict
docs.text: Parity confirmed. The request body shape is identical (OpenAI JSON). The response is the same media type (audio/mpeg) with equivalent binary content. Size differences are due to model non-determinism, not gateway transformation. The gateway adds tracking headers and strips pod-native headers, which is expected proxy behavior.

docs.title: Request shape
docs.text:
Field Gateway (user sends) Pod-direct (we send) LiteLLM transforms to model inception-stt inception/inception-stt inception/inception-stt (from litellm_params.model) file multipart form file multipart form file multipart form file (via process_audio_file) Content-Type multipart/form-data multipart/form-data multipart/form-data

The gateway maps the model name the same way as TTS. The multipart form structure is preserved: a model field and a file field with the audio content. LiteLLM's transform_audio_transcription_request uses process_audio_file to normalize the file handle and rebuilds the multipart form, but the resulting shape matches what the pod expects.

docs.title: Response shape
docs.text:
Pod-direct raw response:

{"text":"شكرا.","audio_duration":1.0,"word_timestamps":[]}

Gateway response:

{
  "text": "شكرا.",
  "usage": null,
  "task": "transcribe",
  "audio_duration": 1.0,
  "word_timestamps": []
}

The gateway adds two fields not present in the pod-direct response:

Field Gateway Pod-direct Source text "شكرا." "شكرا." Pod (identical) audio_duration 1.0 1.0 Pod (identical) word_timestamps [] [] Pod (identical) usage null absent Added by transform_audio_transcription_response task "transcribe" absent Added by transform_audio_transcription_response

The usage and task fields are added by InceptionAudioTranscriptionConfig.transform_audio_transcription_response (in litellm/llms/inception/transcription/transformation.py). This normalizes the response to the OpenAI TranscriptionResponse shape, which includes usage and task fields that the inception pod doesn't natively return.

docs.title: Response headers
docs.text: Same pattern as TTS: gateway adds LiteLLM tracking headers, pod-direct returns uvicorn native headers.

docs.title: STT verdict
docs.text: Parity confirmed with expected enrichment. The request body shape is identical (multipart form with model + file). The response content is identical (text, audio_duration, word_timestamps match exactly). The gateway adds usage: null and task: "transcribe" fields to normalize the response to the OpenAI TranscriptionResponse schema. This is intentional transformation, not a shape mismatch. The transcription text itself (شكرا.) is identical through both paths.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Endpoint Request shape parity Response content parity Response shape difference TTS (/v1/audio/speech) Identical (OpenAI JSON) Equivalent (MP3 binary, non-deterministic sizes) Gateway adds tracking headers, strips pod headers STT (/v1/audio/transcriptions) Identical (multipart form) Identical (same text, duration, timestamps) Gateway adds usage: null and task: "transcribe" fields (OpenAI normalization)

Both paths produce equivalent results. The gateway's transformations are: 1. Model name mapping: inception-tts → inception/inception-tts (DB config lookup) 2. Response normalization: STT response enriched with usage and task fields to match OpenAI schema 3. Header management: LiteLLM tracking headers added, pod-native headers stripped

No data loss or shape corruption occurs through the gateway path. The inception implementation correctly preserves the OpenAI-compatible request/response contract while adding the tracking metadata expected from a proxy.

docs.title: Inception vs Hamsa: Logic Map & Code Smell Audit
docs.text:

docs.text:
main.py:7735  speech(model, input, voice, ...)
    │
    ├── get_llm_provider(model, custom_llm_provider, api_base)

    │   └── utils.py:8171  INCEPTION → InceptionTextToSpeechConfig()
    │
    ├── provider_config.map_openai_params(model, optional_params, voice, kwargs)
    │   ├── [INCEPTION] text_to_speech/transformation.py:46
    │   │   ├── _resolve_voice(voice) → str|None
    │   │   ├── pop _TTS_FORM_KEYS from optional_params → mapped_params

Inside text_to_speech_handler (base_llm_http_handler):

text_to_speech_handler(model, input, voice, provider_config, optional_params, ...)
    │
    ├── provider_config.validate_environment(headers, model, api_key, api_base)
    │   ├── [INCEPTION] returns headers unchanged (no auth injection)
    │   └── [HAMSA] calls _inject_auth_headers(headers, api_key)
    │       ├── resolves key via get_api_key (env HAMSA_API_KEY or passed)
    │       ├── raises BaseLLMException(401) if key missing
    │       ├── sets headers["x-api-key"] = resolved_key
    │       └── sets headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
    │
    ├── provider_config.get_complete_url(model, api_base, litellm_params)
    │   ├── [INCEPTION] _resolve_base(api_base) → strip trailing /v1 → + "/v1/audio/speech"
    │   └── [HAMSA] _resolve_base(api_base) + "/tts/stream"

    ├── provider_config.transform_text_to_speech_request(model, input, voice, optional_params, ...)

    │   │   └── _collect_passthrough(optional_params, request_body)
    │   │
    │   └── [HAMSA] builds {"text": input, "speaker": voice, "language_id": "ar", "stream": False}
    │       ├── conditionally add mulaw, dialect, expressiveness, speed, lang
    │       └── passthrough remaining (excluding HAMSA_INTERNAL_PARAMS)
    │
    ├── HTTP POST to provider URL with headers + body
    │
    └── provider_config.transform_text_to_speech_response(model, raw_response, logging_obj)
        ├── [INCEPTION] wraps in HttpxBinaryResponseContent(raw_response)

docs.title: 1.6 Authentication Flow
docs.text:
[INCEPTION]
    validate_environment() → returns headers unchanged
    Auth relies on OpenAI client passing api_key as Bearer token
    get_api_key() returns api_key or "no-api-key-required"
    No env var lookup (INCEPTION_API_KEY only used in chat config, not audio)

[HAMSA]
    validate_environment() → calls _inject_auth_headers(headers, api_key)
    _inject_auth_headers():
        ├── resolved_key = get_api_key(api_key)  # api_key or os.environ["HAMSA_API_KEY"]
        ├── raises BaseLLMException(401) if key is None
        ├── headers["x-api-key"] = resolved_key
        └── headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"

docs.title: 1.7 URL Construction
docs.text:
[INCEPTION TTS]
    _resolve_base(api_base) → strip trailing "/" → base
    if base ends with "/v1" (case-insensitive): base = base[:-3]
    return base + "/v1/audio/speech"

[INCEPTION STT]
    _resolve_base(api_base) → strip trailing "/" → base
    if base ends with "/v1" (case-insensitive): base = base[:-3]
    return base + "/v1/audio/transcriptions"

[HAMSA TTS]
    _resolve_base(api_base) → strip trailing "/" → base
    return base + "/tts/stream"

[HAMSA STT]
    _resolve_base(api_base) → strip trailing "/" → base
    return base + "/transcribe"

[HAMSA Voice]
    _resolve_base(api_base) → strip trailing "/" → base
    if action == "load": return base + "/tts/load_voice_cloning"
    else: return base + "/tts/voice_clone"

[HAMSA Realtime]
    _resolve_base(api_base) → strip trailing "/" → base
    https:// → wss://, http:// → ws://
    return base + "/ws"

docs.text:
Tool Provider Result pyflakes inception Clean (0 findings) pyflakes hamsa Clean (0 findings) ruff (F-category) inception All checks passed ruff (F-category) hamsa All checks passed ruff (full project config) inception All checks passed ruff (full project config) hamsa All checks passed ruff (strict, no project config) inception 2 PLC0415 (lazy imports inside functions) ruff (strict, no project config) hamsa 8 findings: 4 PLC0415, 1 PLR0915, 1 PLR0912, 1 SIM, 1 RET

Note: PLC0415 (import inside function) is in the project's ruff.toml external noqa list (line 11). The lazy imports are intentional to avoid circular import issues common in the litellm codebase.

Assessment: L1 is clean for both providers under the project's configured rules. No unused imports, no dead code detected by automated tools.

docs.title: inception/common_utils.py
docs.text:
• [OK] INCEPTION_INTERNAL_PARAMS is a frozenset (immutable). Good
  • [OK] InceptionAudioModelInfo inherits BaseLLMModelInfo. Follows the standard pattern
  • [SMELL: LOW] get_api_key returns api_key or "no-api-key-required" — a sentinel string rather than None. This is a design choice: inception pods don't require auth, so a placeholder is used. However, the string "no-api-key-required" could leak into headers if not handled downstream. In practice, validate_environment returns headers unchanged and the HTTP handler uses the api_key from litellm_params, so this sentinel is never sent as a real credential
  • [OK] _resolve_base follows the same pattern as hamsa: raises BaseLLMException(400) if api_base is missing. The lazy import of BaseLLMException is intentional (avoids circular import)

docs.title: inception/text_to_speech/transformation.py
docs.text:
• [OK] _TTS_FORM_KEYS is a tuple (immutable). Good
  • [OK] _resolve_voice is a module-level function, not a method. Clean separation
  • [OK] _collect_passthrough is a module-level function that filters against INCEPTION_INTERNAL_PARAMS. Reused in both map_openai_params and transform_text_to_speech_request. Good DRY
  • [SMELL: LOW] map_openai_params pops keys from optional_params (mutating the input dict). This is the standard litellm pattern (hamsa does the same), but it violates immutability. Not a fix for this pass since it matches the codebase convention
  • [SMELL: LOW] transform_text_to_speech_request pops _TTS_FORM_KEYS from optional_params again. By the time this is called, map_openai_params has already popped them. The second pop is defensive but technically dead code — the keys will always be None. Not harmful, but redundant
  • [OK] validate_environment returns headers unchanged. Correct for inception (no auth injection needed; pods are internal)
  • [OK] get_complete_url strips trailing /v1 before appending /v1/audio/speech. This prevents the double-/v1 bug that was fixed in commit 2ced4330a4
  • [OK] transform_text_to_speech_response wraps in HttpxBinaryResponseContent. Matches hamsa

docs.title: inception/transcription/transformation.py
docs.text:
• [OK] map_openai_params builds stt_known_keys as a local set. Clean
  • [OK] validate_environment returns headers unchanged. Correct
  • [OK] get_complete_url strips trailing /v1 before appending /v1/audio/transcriptions. Matches TTS pattern
  • [OK] transform_audio_transcription_request uses multipart form with process_audio_file. Standard OpenAI-compatible STT format
  • [OK] transform_audio_transcription_response extracts text, sets task, copies extras, stores full payload. Clean

docs.title: inception/chat/transformation.py
docs.text:
• [OK] InceptionChatConfig extends OpenAILikeChatConfig. Standard pattern for OpenAI-compatible chat
  • [OK] _get_openai_compatible_provider_info resolves api_base and api_key with env var fallbacks
  • [SMELL: LOW] get_supported_openai_params returns a hardcoded list including non-standard params like "diffusing" and "realtime". These are inception-specific extension params. Acceptable since inception has unique diffusion capabilities

docs.title: inception/completion/transformation.py
docs.text:
• [OK] InceptionTextCompletionConfig extends OpenAITextCompletionConfig. Standard
  • [OK] map_openai_params maps max_completion_tokens → max_tokens. Clean

docs.title: hamsa/common_utils.py
docs.text:
• [OK] HAMSA_INTERNAL_PARAMS is a frozenset. Good
  • [OK] HamsaModelInfo inherits BaseLLMModelInfo. Follows the same pattern as inception
  • [OK] get_api_key uses os.environ.get("HAMSA_API_KEY") as fallback. Standard env var pattern
  • [OK] get_api_base uses os.environ.get("HAMSA_API_BASE") as fallback. No default URL (unlike inception which has https://api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1). Correct: hamsa pods are internal and must be explicitly configured
  • [OK] _resolve_base follows the same pattern as inception. Clean
  • [OK] _inject_auth_headers is a static method that resolves key, raises on missing, sets x-api-key and Content-Type. This is the key differentiator from inception: hamsa requires explicit auth
  • [SMELL: LOW] HAMSA_INTERNAL_PARAMS includes the OpenAI audio params themselves ("model", "voice", "response_format", "speed", "instructions", "language", "prompt", "temperature", "timestamp_granularities", "stream"). Inception's frozenset does NOT include these. This is intentional: hamsa's map_openai_params pops these explicitly before passthrough, so they're in the internal set to prevent re-injection. Inception's _TTS_FORM_KEYS serves the same purpose for TTS, but inception's STT uses a local stt_known_keys set instead. Different approaches to the same problem

docs.title: hamsa/text_to_speech/transformation.py
docs.text:
• [SMELL: MEDIUM] map_openai_params has 15 branches (ruff PLR0912). The voice resolution, response_format mapping, speed mapping, instructions pop, extra_body merge, kwargs passthrough, and optional_params passthrough are all inline. Inception extracts _resolve_voice and _collect_passthrough as module-level functions, reducing method complexity. Hamsa should follow the same pattern
  • [SMELL: LOW] Voice resolution logic (lines 26-33) is duplicated inline rather than extracted to a helper function. Inception has _resolve_voice() as a reusable module function. Hamsa inlines the same str/dict/other pattern
  • [SMELL: LOW] map_openai_params raises BaseLLMException(400) if speaker is None. Inception's _resolve_voice returns None and lets transform_text_to_speech_request default to "alloy". Different design philosophies: hamsa requires explicit speaker, inception has a default. Both are valid for their respective APIs
  • [SMELL: LOW] transform_text_to_speech_request uses a chain of if "key" in optional_params: request_body[key] = optional_params.pop(key) for mulaw, dialect, expressiveness, speed, lang. This is 5 repetitive blocks. Could be a loop over a tuple of known hamsa-specific keys, but the current approach is readable
  • [OK] validate_environment calls _inject_auth_headers. Correct
  • [OK] get_complete_url returns base + "/tts/stream". No /v1 stripping needed since hamsa doesn't use OpenAI-compatible paths
  • [OK] transform_text_to_speech_response wraps in HttpxBinaryResponseContent. Matches inception

docs.title: hamsa/transcription/transformation.py
docs.text:
• [OK] map_openai_params maps language → lang. Clean
  • [OK] validate_environment calls _inject_auth_headers. Correct
  • [OK] get_complete_url returns base + "/transcribe". Clean
  • [OK] transform_audio_transcription_request uses JSON body with base64 audio. Different from inception's multipart form, but correct for hamsa's API
  • [OK] transform_audio_transcription_response matches inception's pattern exactly. Good consistency
  • [SMELL: LOW] Uses Union[dict, Headers] instead of dict | Headers (Python 3.10+). Inception uses dict | Headers. Cosmetic inconsistency

docs.title: hamsa/voice/transformation.py
docs.text:
• [OK] _SPEAKER_ALIASES and _AUDIO_PATH_ALIASES are frozensets. Good
  • [SMELL: LOW] Class-level constants _SPEAKER_ALIASES and _AUDIO_PATH_ALIASES are defined in the middle of the class (after transform_create_voice_request, before transform_create_voice_response). Convention is to put constants at the top of the class. Minor readability issue
  • [OK] transform_create_voice_request branches on voice_action ("load" vs "register"). Clean early-return pattern
  • [OK] transform_create_voice_response uses next() with frozenset alias lookup. Clean

docs.title: hamsa/realtime/handler.py
docs.text:
• [SMELL: MEDIUM] hamsa_realtime function has 59 statements (ruff PLR0915, threshold 50). The function handles WebSocket proxying with two nested async coroutines. Could be refactored to extract forward_client_to_backend and forward_backend_to_client as module-level functions taking explicit dependencies, but the current closure approach captures state cleanly
  • [SMELL: LOW] forward_backend_to_client catches Exception and logs it. This is broad but acceptable for a WebSocket proxy that must survive protocol errors
  • [OK] Handshake key injection is a clever security pattern: the API key is injected into the first handshake message rather than sent as a header. This matches hamsa's WebSocket protocol design
  • [OK] transform_realtime_response handles bytes→str decoding, JSON parsing with fallback. Robust

docs.title: Dispatch Pattern Consistency
docs.text:
speech() dispatch:
    ├── OpenAI SDK path (excludes inception via _CUSTOM_AUDIO_HANDLER_PROVIDERS, excludes hamsa via not-in-openai_compatible_providers)
    ├── elif hamsa → explicit branch (main.py:8163)
    └── elif inception → explicit branch (main.py:8192)
    → Both branches are structurally identical: import config, cast, set params, call text_to_speech_handler

transcription() dispatch:
    ├── OpenAI SDK path (same exclusion logic)
    └── elif provider_config is not None → generic catch-all (main.py:7653)
    → Both inception and hamsa fall through to the generic catch-all
    → This works because ProviderConfigManager resolves both configs

[SMELL: MEDIUM] Inconsistency: speech() has explicit elif branches for both hamsa and inception, but transcription() uses the generic catch-all for both. The TTS path requires explicit branches because text_to_speech_provider_config is resolved before the dispatch and passed into the OpenAI SDK branch. The STT path resolves provider_config before the dispatch too, so the generic catch-all works. But the asymmetry means: 1. If a new custom audio provider is added, it needs an explicit elif in speech() but not in transcription() 2. The speech() elif blocks are copy-paste identical (only the config class name differs), which is a DRY violation

docs.title: L4: Fix-Then-Recheck Results
docs.text: No fixes were applied in this audit pass. The findings are documentation-level observations. The L1 tools are clean, and the L2/L3 findings are architectural patterns that match the broader litellm codebase conventions.

docs.title: Are the implementations following the same pattern?
docs.text:
Partially yes, with intentional divergences.

Both providers follow the same structural pattern: 1. A common_utils.py with a *INTERNAL_PARAMS frozenset and a *ModelInfo(BaseLLMModelInfo) class 2. Per-endpoint transformation.py files with config classes inheriting from both the model info and the base config 3. The same method set: get_supported_openai_params, map_openai_params, validate_environment, get_complete_url, transform_*_request, transform_*_response 4. The same response wrapping pattern: HttpxBinaryResponseContent for TTS, TranscriptionResponse for STT

The divergences are intentional and driven by the upstream API shapes: - Inception uses OpenAI-compatible paths (/v1/audio/speech, /v1/audio/transcriptions) and multipart form for STT - Hamsa uses custom paths (/tts/stream, /transcribe) and JSON+base64 for STT - Inception doesn't inject auth headers (internal pods, no auth required) - Hamsa injects x-api-key via _inject_auth_headers

docs.title: Are both good implementations?
docs.text:
Yes, with minor improvements possible.

Inception strengths: - Extracts _resolve_voice and _collect_passthrough as module-level functions (better DRY) - _TTS_FORM_KEYS tuple centralizes the form key list - Simpler map_openai_params due to helper extraction

Inception weaknesses: - transform_text_to_speech_request re-pops _TTS_FORM_KEYS that were already popped in map_openai_params (redundant) - get_api_key returns a sentinel string "no-api-key-required" instead of None (could confuse downstream consumers)

Hamsa strengths: - _inject_auth_headers is a clean, reusable auth method used across all endpoints - Voice cloning and realtime support show good extensibility - HAMSA_INTERNAL_PARAMS includes the OpenAI audio param names, providing double protection against leakage

Hamsa weaknesses: - map_openai_params in TTS has too many branches (15 > 12 threshold) and inlines voice resolution instead of extracting a helper - Uses Union[str, Dict] instead of str | dict (older typing style, inconsistent with inception's modern str | dict) - transform_text_to_speech_request uses repetitive if "key" in optional_params: pop blocks instead of a loop - Class-level constants (_SPEAKER_ALIASES, _AUDIO_PATH_ALIASES) are placed in the middle of the class instead of at the top

docs.title: Recommendations (not fixed in this pass)
docs.text:
1. Hamsa TTS: Extract voice resolution to a module-level _resolve_speaker() function, matching inception's _resolve_voice() pattern. This would reduce branch count from 15 to within threshold
  2. Hamsa TTS: Replace the 5 repetitive if "key" in optional_params: pop blocks with a loop over a _HAMSA_TTS_KEYS tuple
  3. Hamsa: Migrate Union[str, Dict] to str | dict and List to list for consistency with inception and modern Python
  4. Hamsa voice: Move _SPEAKER_ALIASES and _AUDIO_PATH_ALIASES to the top of the class
  5. Inception TTS: Remove the redundant _TTS_FORM_KEYS pop in transform_text_to_speech_request (already popped in map_openai_params)
  6. main.py speech(): The hamsa and inception elif blocks are copy-paste identical. Consider extracting a shared _dispatch_custom_tts_provider(custom_llm_provider, config_class, ...) helper to eliminate the duplication
  7. main.py: Consider adding hamsa to _CUSTOM_AUDIO_HANDLER_PROVIDERS for consistency, even though it doesn't need to be excluded from the OpenAI SDK path (it's already excluded by not being in openai_compatible_providers). This would make the exclusion logic explicit rather than implicit

docs.title: Overall Verdict
docs.text: Both implementations are functional, well-structured, and follow the litellm provider pattern. The inception implementation is slightly cleaner due to better helper extraction. The hamsa implementation is more feature-rich (voice cloning, realtime) but has higher complexity in map_openai_params. Neither has any L1 tool findings, and the L2/L3 findings are minor architectural observations, not bugs. The 5 router-level params (use_in_pass_through, use_litellm_proxy, use_xai_oauth, use_chat_completions_api, merge_reasoning_content_in_choices) are consistently present in both INCEPTION_INTERNAL_PARAMS and HAMSA_INTERNAL_PARAMS, which was the fix that resolved the HTTP 500 TTS bug.

docs.title: Key observations
docs.text:
• The route is a thin HTTP handler. It does NOT call the provider directly. It delegates to route_request which goes through the full router → SDK → handler → config chain.
  • ref_audio is read from the UploadFile and stored as a FileTypes tuple (filename, bytes, content_type) in data["ref_audio"]. This tuple flows through all layers down to the config's transform_text_to_speech_request.
  • voice is set to "clone" as a sentinel value. The pod ignores it; it's there because the speech() SDK function signature requires voice: str.
  • text is renamed to input because the SDK speech() function uses input as the parameter name.
  • The response is always audio/mpeg via StreamingResponse, regardless of the actual response_format requested.

async def aspeech(self, model: str, input: str, voice: str, **kwargs):
    kwargs["model"] = model
    kwargs["input"] = input
    kwargs["voice"] = voice
    kwargs["original_function"] = self._aspeech
    self._update_kwargs_before_fallbacks(model=model, kwargs=kwargs)
    response = await self.async_function_with_fallbacks(**kwargs)
    return response

async def _aspeech(self, model: str, input: str, voice: str, **kwargs):
    deployment = await self.async_get_available_deployment(model=model, ...)
    self._update_kwargs_with_deployment(deployment=deployment, kwargs=kwargs)
    data = deployment["litellm_params"].copy()
    model_client = self._get_async_openai_model_client(deployment=deployment, kwargs=kwargs)
    response = litellm.aspeech(**{**data, "input": input, "voice": voice, "client": model_client, **kwargs})
    ...
    response = await response
    return response

docs.text:
The handler supports three body types via TextToSpeechRequestData: - dict_body — JSON POST (used by standard TTS) - ssml_body — raw XML body - form_data + files — multipart POST (used by voice clone)

The config class decides which body type by setting the appropriate field on TextToSpeechRequestData.

docs.title: Layer 6: Provider Config — voice/transformation.py
docs.text:
File: litellm/llms/omnivoice/voice/transformation.py

_CLONE_FORM_KEYS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "response_format", "speed", "stream", "num_step", "guidance_scale",
    "denoise", "t_shift", "position_temperature", "class_temperature",
    "duration", "language", "layer_penalty_factor", "preprocess_prompt",
    "postprocess_output", "audio_chunk_duration", "audio_chunk_threshold",
    "request_timeout_s",
)

class OmniVoiceVoiceCloneConfig(OmniVoiceModelInfo, BaseTextToSpeechConfig):
    def get_complete_url(self, model, api_base, litellm_params) -> str:
        base = self._resolve_base(api_base)
        if base.lower().endswith("/v1"):
            base = base[:-3]
        return base + "/v1/audio/speech/clone"

    def transform_text_to_speech_request(self, model, input, voice,
        optional_params, litellm_params, headers) -> TextToSpeechRequestData:
        ref_audio = optional_params.pop("ref_audio", None)
        ref_text = optional_params.pop("ref_text", None)
        form_fields = {"text": input}
        if ref_text is not None:
            form_fields["ref_text"] = ref_text
        for key in _CLONE_FORM_KEYS:
            value = optional_params.pop(key, None)
            if value is not None:
                form_fields[key] = value
        _collect_passthrough(optional_params, form_fields)
        if isinstance(ref_audio, tuple):
            files = {"ref_audio": ref_audio}
        elif isinstance(ref_audio, (bytes, bytearray)):
            files = {"ref_audio": ("ref_audio.wav", bytes(ref_audio), "audio/wav")}
        else:
            processed = process_audio_file(ref_audio)
            files = {"ref_audio": (processed.filename, processed.file_content, processed.content_type)}
        return TextToSpeechRequestData(form_data=form_fields, files=files)

    def transform_text_to_speech_response(self, model, raw_response, logging_obj):
        return HttpxBinaryResponseContent(raw_response)

docs.text: Step Method What happens 1 validate_environment Returns headers as-is (no API key needed for OmniVoice) 2 get_complete_url Strips trailing /v1, appends /v1/audio/speech/clone 3 transform_text_to_speech_request Pops ref_audio from optional_params, builds form_fields dict with text + clone params, returns TextToSpeechRequestData(form_data=..., files=...) 4 (handler sends multipart POST) httpx sends data=form_fields, files={"ref_audio": tuple} 5 transform_text_to_speech_response Wraps raw httpx.Response in HttpxBinaryResponseContent

docs.title: _collect_passthrough function
docs.text:
File: litellm/llms/omnivoice/common_utils.py:79

def _collect_passthrough(source: dict[str, Any], dest: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
    for key, value in source.items():
        if value is None or key in OMNIVOICE_INTERNAL_PARAMS or key in {"extra_body", "extra_headers"}:
            continue
        if isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
            continue
        dest[key] = value

Copies non-internal, non-None, non-dict/list values from source to dest. This is how extra params (not in _CLONE_FORM_KEYS) get forwarded to the pod as form fields. Tuples are allowed (for ref_audio).

return StreamingResponse(
    _audio_speech_chunk_generator(response),
    media_type="audio/mpeg",
    headers=custom_headers,
)

The response from the handler (HttpxBinaryResponseContent) is streamed back to the client as audio/mpeg.
