docs.title: 3. Health read path (the status source)
docs.text:
GatewayStatusReader.read(model_name, deployment_ids)      status_reader.py:37
  if prisma is None or not deployment_ids: return {}      # no DB, no status
  |
  +-- fetch_latest_health_checks_for_models(prisma, [model_name])
  |     db/health_check_latest.py:86
  |     SQL: SELECT DISTINCT ON (model_id, model_name) ...
  |          WHERE model_name = ANY($1) ORDER BY checked_at DESC
  |     ^ filters on model_name, NOT model_id
  |     by_id = {row.model_id: row for row in rows if row.model_id}
  |
  +-- _read_heartbeats()                                  status_reader.py:60
  |     fetch_latest_health_checks(prisma)   # all rows, no filter
  |     keep rows where model_id is None and
  |       model_name.startswith("oicm-source-")           # _SOURCE_ROW_PREFIX
  |     key by cluster name (prefix stripped)
  |     on any exception: log, return {}   # noqa: BLE001, decoration must not 500
  |
  +-- per deployment_id:
        _inputs(row, heartbeats)                          status_reader.py:76
          details = row.details if dict else {}
          cluster = details["cluster"]
          heartbeat = heartbeats.get(cluster)             # freshness source
          replicas = details["replicas"] -> desired/available
          -> GatewayStatusInputs(
               oicm_status=details["status"],
               serving_available=details["serving_available"],
               replicas_desired, replicas_available,
               observed_at=details["observed_at"],
               cluster=cluster,
               health_status=row.status,
               source_checked_at=heartbeat.checked_at)

The details keys are written by the controller's build_block (controller/status_persister.py:60), with cluster merged in at controller/status_persister.py:258. Verified against a live row (section 8).

docs.title: 4. Verdict resolution
docs.text:
GatewayStateResolver.resolve(inputs)                      gateway_status.py:135
  checked_at = inputs.source_checked_at                   # heartbeat, not model row
  stale      = _is_stale(checked_at)                      gateway_status.py:152
                 None -> True; age > 90s -> True
  availability = "unknown" if stale
                 else _availability(oicm_status, serving_available)  gateway_status.py:169
                   stopped|failed|deploying -> offline
                   Ready|Available -> _AVAILABILITY_BY_SERVING[serving]
                   else -> unknown
  -> GatewayStatus(oicm_status=inputs.oicm_status, ...)   gateway_status.py:82
       # the controller string, verbatim; no grouping

docs.title: The DTO carries OICM's vocabulary, not a derived one
docs.text:
gateway_status is {oicm_status, availability, stale, source, healthy, replicas, observed_at, checked_at}.

  • oicm_status is OICM's own string, passed through unchanged. A consumer that knows OICM can read it directly; we add no vocabulary of our own on top.
  • availability is the only derived field, because two facts cannot be expressed in OICM's vocabulary: a source that stopped reporting, and a deployment OICM still calls Ready whose pods serve nothing.
  • healthy is the native health verdict. It is an independent signal from oicm_status, per the design (OICM-STATUS-FEASIBILITY.md): OICM can report Ready while the health row says unhealthy.

GatewayStatus.endpoint_status() (gateway_status.py:95) maps that onto OpenRouter's numeric enum. Availability wins when it has an opinion, so a Ready deployment that is not serving becomes -2. Otherwise the raw status is consulted (gateway_status.py:64):

stale -> None (omit)
else _ENDPOINT_STATUS_BY_AVAILABILITY.get(availability)     # degraded -> -2, online -> 0
     or _ENDPOINT_STATUS_BY_OICM_STATUS.get(oicm_status, -2)  # Failed/-5, Stopped/-10, Deploying/-3
     or None if oicm_status is None

-1 is unassigned on purpose (reserved for a load-based signal; see docs/oicm-status/FEASIBILITY-ANSWERS.md).

docs.title: 5. Response shape
docs.text:
ListEndpointsResponse(
  id           = public_id            # canonical, e.g. litellm/hamsa-tts
  name         = display_name or upstream_model_id or public_id
  created      = identity.created or 0
  description  = "<public_id> served by the gateway across N deployment(s)."
  architecture = all-null/empty       # we observe none of it
  endpoints    = [GatewayEndpoint per deployment]
)

GatewayEndpoint (mapping/endpoints.py) subclasses the official PublicEndpoint and adds gateway_status, live_concurrency, and requests_last_30m. The extras survive because map_endpoints serializes through GatewayListEndpointsResponse, a ListEndpointsResponse subclass that redeclares endpoints: Sequence[GatewayEndpoint]. Redeclaring is what keeps the extra keys in the payload: assigning GatewayEndpoint values to the base list[PublicEndpoint] field would validate each one down to the base type and drop them. This replaces the earlier build-the-base-then-overwrite approach, which needed a typing.cast and a second per-endpoint dump.

Fields we compute vs. leave honestly empty:

Computed Source model_id AggregatedModel.logical_model_name (routing name) model_name deployment.identity.upstream_model_id (served id) name, tag, provider_name runtime kind from discovery context_length deployment limits (probe max_model_len) pricing.prompt / .completion litellm registry status section 4 gateway_status sections 3-4; oicm_status is the raw controller string latency_last_30m TTFT percentiles from Prometheus (30m window, ms) throughput_last_30m inverted per-token-latency histogram (tokens/sec) uptime_last_5m/30m/1d success/(success+failure)*100 from the counters live_concurrency in-progress gauge (our extension) requests_last_30m total-requests counter, 30m increase (our extension)

Left null/empty on purpose: max_prompt_tokens / max_completion_tokens (nothing populates the limit fields), quantization, supported_parameters, supports_tool_choice (all-false), native_tools, the three supports_* booleans. These are nullable fields, so None serializes as null, not omitted (verified live). perf_last_30m_by_workload is optional and never set, so it is the one field that is absent rather than null. status is the one optional field we control, and omitting it is how we say "no opinion".

docs.title: 6. Match key
docs.text:
{author}/{slug} matches the registered LiteLLM model_name, the string a caller puts in the request body. Both sides are canonicalized through OpenRouterModelMapper.canonical_id (mapping/openrouter.py:120), which prefixes the litellm namespace onto a bare id. Consequences:

  • Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 -> canonical Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8
  • hamsa-tts -> canonical litellm/hamsa-tts, reachable as either URL form
  • wrong/hamsa-tts -> canonical wrong/hamsa-tts -> no match -> 404

It is deliberately not the upstream served id. Live proof they differ, and that LiteLLM rejects the served name, is in design §31. model_name is also not unique (several clusters can share one), so one URL can return several endpoints.

docs.title: 7. Consumers of the output
docs.text: Consumer Reads Status OpenRouter-compatible clients /api/v1/models, both /endpoints forms live Admin UI /health/latest via model_id unchanged, source rows skipped OICM controller its own in-memory checked_at does NOT read source rows gateway_status on each endpoint source-row freshness via checked_at the intended consumer of source rows

docs.title: 8. Live verification (2026-10-07, dev)
docs.text:
Scraped, not assumed:

  • All 28 models: 28/28 canonical /endpoints URLs return HTTP 200; the 11 bare ids return HTTP 200 with byte-identical bodies; 22 endpoints carry status=0; 6 return empty-but-valid [].
  • Wrong author: 404 for both a discovered and an undiscovered bare id.
  • Unauthenticated: 401. Unknown model: 404.
  • One live details blob confirmed every key status_reader._inputs reads: cluster, status, serving_available, replicas.desired/available, observed_at (plus v, gateway_uuid, status_changed_at, error_msg, which this consumer ignores).
  • Observed status values in the table: Ready (505 rows), Deploying (2). The resolver maps all seven OICM statuses, so Available, Pending, Stopped, Failed, Undeploying are covered but unobserved in dev.
  • Prod pods untouched (started=2026-09-30).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: Finding Layer Where Fix PLR0911 7 returns in one function L1 gateway_status.py:82 Replaced the 6-branch if-chain with two declarative tables (_ENDPOINT_STATUS_BY_LIFECYCLE, _ENDPOINT_STATUS_BY_AVAILABILITY) and two lookups. Also makes the lifecycle-over-availability precedence explicit. B010 setattr with a constant name L1 routes/models.py:41 setattr(app_state, "openrouter_service", built) -> app_state.openrouter_service = built. source_status held the native health string, not the OICM status L3 gateway_status.py:145 The design (OICM-STATUS-FEASIBILITY.md:153) specifies source_status: status # Ready / Stopped / .... The implementation set it from health_status, so the raw OICM status was absent from the DTO and source_status merely duplicated healthy. Replaced with oicm_status, populated from inputs.oicm_status verbatim. lifecycle carried no information the raw status did not L3 gateway_status.py:163 The 5-bucket grouping was lossy with respect to the raw status it was derived from, and every consumer wanted the raw value. Removed; endpoint_status() now keys off availability then oicm_status.

docs.text:
• pyflakes and vulture (--min-confidence 80) both silent on the package.

docs.title: 10. Telemetry pass (2026-10-07, after the refactors)

docs.title: 11. What is still open
docs.text:
Verified against the tree on 2026-10-07, not taken from a doc. The full register with priorities is in docs/oicm-status/PROGRESS-AND-PAUSED-WORK.md.

Item Status Notes M2 engine-load telemetry not started No RuntimeTelemetryProvider / RuntimeTelemetrySnapshot / kv_cache_utilization in the tree. The instantaneous engine view, distinct from the windowed stats this map describes. reserved -1 endpoint status unassigned on purpose Blocked on M2; it is meant to signal an idle-then-burst endpoint. perf_last_30m_by_workload absent Needs a metric-to-workload classifier. runtime detection wrong for every deployment _detect_runtime_kind misses hosted_vllm, so provider_name/tag are openai-compatible and the vLLM/SGLang adapters never run. discarded capability enrichment dead work per request map_endpoints never reads capabilities. max_prompt_tokens / max_completion_tokens always null Only openai_compatible.py:78 builds ModelLimits, with context_length alone. data.architecture hardcoded empty _response_architecture() returns all-null.

Closed: M1 (Steps 13-18) and M3 Step 25, including all four telemetry fields and their percentiles. live_concurrency semantics were pinned on 2026-10-07: it is max by (model_id), the busiest replica's load, not the fleet-wide sum (see MAPPING-litellm-to-endpoints.md §8g).

docs.title: Mapping: litellm inputs to the /endpoints response
docs.text:
Reference for deciding what to fill next. Every field of GET /api/v1/models/{author}/{slug}/endpoints, where its value comes from, and what litellm data is currently unused.

Line refs are against commit 1a0b9d23c4. Live values verified on dev 2026-10-07, the telemetry fields scraped after traffic warmed the 30m window.

The latency/throughput/uptime rows are populated by litellm/proxy/openrouter_compat/enrichment/telemetry.py; the source decision and the realtime-vs-historical accuracy audit are in MAPPING-usage-metrics.md.

docs.title: 1. The two names (read this first)
docs.text:
Name What it is Where it comes from Where it appears routing name the string you put in a request body deployment.model_name the URL match key, endpoint.model_id, data.id served id what the runtime reports at /v1/models deployment.litellm_params.model, prefix stripped by the probe endpoint.model_name

They can differ (Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1 vs Qwen-Image-2.1) and litellm rejects the served id, so the URL matches the routing name. See design §31.

docs.title: 4. Pricing precedence
docs.text:
PricingResolver._resolve_deployment (pricing.py:47), first hit wins:

  1. deployment.model_info["input_cost_per_token"] + ["output_cost_per_token"]
  2. litellm.get_model_info(upstream_id) with the same two keys
  3. Pricing("0", "0") (unknown_policy="free")

Verified: litellm.get_model_info("Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8") misses, so for a deployment without explicit cost keys the price is 0, not a registry price. The live non-zero prices come from model_info (which litellm populates from litellm_params for a DB-registered model).

docs.title: 4b. Telemetry fields (latency / throughput / uptime)
docs.text:
Read by litellm/proxy/openrouter_compat/enrichment/telemetry.py (PrometheusDeploymentTelemetryReader), keyed by model_id, from the cluster Prometheus. All queries run concurrently, and the whole model_id map is cached for 15s so a burst of /endpoints calls costs one query set per TTL.

Field Metric Transform latency_last_30m litellm_llm_api_time_to_first_token_metric histogram_quantile over rate(...[30m]), seconds to ms throughput_last_30m litellm_deployment_latency_per_output_token histogram_quantile over rate(...[30m]), inverted to tokens/sec uptime_last_5m/30m/1d litellm_deployment_success_responses_total and ..._failure_responses_total increase per window, then success/(success+failure)*100 live_concurrency litellm_deployment_in_progress_requests max by (model_id), truncated to int requests_last_30m litellm_deployment_total_requests_total increase over 30m

Semantics, all chosen to match OpenRouter's contract:

  • Latency is time to first token, not total duration. The TTFT histogram is observed only for streamed requests, so a deployment with no recent stream reports null. This is honest, not a defect: at the moment of one dev check the TTFT count in the window was 1, so histogram_quantile could not resolve and the field was null; once a second sample landed it read {p50: 38.4, p75: 45.1, p90: 49.2, p99: 92.7}.
  • Throughput is per-request generation speed (the inverse of the latency-per-output-token histogram), which is OpenRouter's definition. The counter-rate alternative (rate(output_tokens)) is a fleet capacity metric that under-reports speed under low load; see MAPPING-usage-metrics.md §2.4.
  • Uptime is success/(success+failure)*100 over the window. Success and failure are read as two separate queries rather than one ratio, because a deployment with zero failures has no failure series at all and a PromQL vector division against a missing operand yields an empty vector. A missing success series means no traffic, reported as null; a missing failure series defaults to 0, so a healthy deployment reports 100.
  • All four percentiles are required. If any quantile is missing the whole distribution is reported as absent rather than fabricated from fewer points.

Two fields are extensions beyond the OpenRouter contract, on the same GatewayEndpoint subclass as gateway_status: live_concurrency (the live in-flight count) and requests_last_30m. OpenRouter has no top-level field for either; it only exposes request volume nested per workload inside perf_last_30m_by_workload, which we do not implement.

live_concurrency is the peak in-flight count on the busiest replica of the deployment (max by (model_id)), not the fleet-wide sum. See §8g.

docs.title: Nullable fields serialize as null, not omitted
docs.text: The SDK's @model_serializer keeps a nullable field when it is explicitly set, so latency_last_30m, throughput_last_30m, the uptime_* fields, max_*_tokens, and quantization all appear in the JSON as null when absent. Only perf_last_30m_by_workload (optional, never set) is dropped. Verified on live dev 2026-10-07.

docs.title: 5. The response envelope
docs.text: Field Value Source data.id canonical id canonical_id(f"{author}/{slug}") data.name display name, else served id, else public_id sources 10, probe 1 data.created identity.created or 0 probe 1 created, aggregated as first non-null data.description "{public_id} served by the gateway across N deployment(s)." generated data.architecture all-null/empty _response_architecture() hardcodes it

docs.title: 6. gateway_status
docs.text: Field Source oicm_status health details["status"], verbatim availability derived from oicm_status + details["serving_available"], or unknown when stale stale now - heartbeat.checked_at > 90s; None heartbeat means stale source details["cluster"] healthy the health row's own status == "healthy" replicas details["replicas"]["desired"/"available"] observed_at details["observed_at"] checked_at the oicm-source-<cluster> heartbeat row's checked_at

docs.title: 7. Unused litellm data (candidates, not defects)
docs.text: Available Read? Note general_settings no threaded through the whole call chain, never read litellm_params.model cache key only the served id comes from the probe, not from here model_info.id health join only model_info capability keys (supports_function_calling, supports_tool_choice, supports_reasoning, supports_response_schema) only via the list route the enricher runs on the endpoints route but nothing reads its output model_info context/limit keys no limits come from the probe registry supported_openai_params no (endpoints route) resolver exists, unused here identity.hugging_face_id, identity.canonical_id, identity.root, identity.parent no (endpoints route) list route only

docs.title: 8a. tag and provider_name are always "openai-compatible"
docs.text:
_detect_runtime_kind (registry.py:54) matches only the literal strings "sglang" and "vllm". A DB-registered model has litellm_params.model = "hosted_vllm/...", whose custom_llm_provider is "hosted_vllm" (verified). That matches neither, so every deployment falls through to the generic adapter.

Consequences, all live-confirmed:

  • every endpoint reports provider_name = "openai-compatible" and tag = "openai-compatible", so the runtime is not actually advertised
  • the vLLM adapter is never selected, so /openapi.json is never probed and api_capabilities is never populated
  • the SGLang adapter is never selected, so /model_info is never probed and has_image_understanding / is_generation are never read
  • the only way to reach either richer adapter today is a per-deployment model_info.discovery_runtime override

docs.title: 8b. Capability enrichment runs but its result is discarded
docs.text: get_model_endpoints (models_service.py:129) computes self._metadata_enricher.enrich(self._capability_enricher.enrich(page)), but map_endpoints reads only deployment.limits, deployment.identity, deployment.runtime, model.logical_model_name, and model.identity. It never reads capabilities. So both enrichers are dead work on this route. They are live on the list route.

docs.title: 8c. max_prompt_tokens / max_completion_tokens are always null
docs.text: Nothing populates limits.max_input_tokens or limits.max_completion_tokens: the probe sets only context_length, and the aggregator would compute them from those same unset fields. Confirmed by construction: the only non-test ModelLimits(...) call is discovery/adapters/openai_compatible.py:78, which sets context_length alone. They are not per-deployment values today, they are structurally empty. Verified live: both serialize as null.

docs.title: 8d. data.architecture is hardcoded empty
docs.text: _response_architecture() returns all-null. The real architecture (model_type, architectures, tokenizer, instruct_type) is available in model.architecture for SGLang deployments, and the modalities are in model.capabilities, but the endpoints route emits neither. The list route does map modalities.

docs.title: 8e. perf_last_30m_by_workload is not implemented
docs.text: OpenRouter keys this by workload type (text_generation, stt, tts). We have the per-deployment data to fill the text_generation bucket, but classifying a metric series by workload needs a mapping that does not exist yet. Left absent rather than fabricated.

docs.title: 8f. live_concurrency and requests_last_30m are extensions
docs.text: Both sit on the GatewayEndpoint subclass alongside gateway_status. OpenRouter has no top-level field for either, so a strict OpenRouter client ignores them. They are the only two telemetry fields not in the official contract, and they are documented as such at §4b.

docs.title: 8g. live_concurrency is the busiest replica's load
docs.text:
The query is max by (model_id) (litellm_deployment_in_progress_requests). The gauge carries one series per pod, so a model_id (one deployment) can have several. The field reports the peak in-flight count on the busiest replica, the load on that endpoint, not the fleet-wide sum across its pods.

This matches the reading MAPPING-usage-metrics.md §8f already called the honest one for a per-endpoint (deployment) field. Summing would make a deployment spread over four pods read four times busier than the same load on one pod, which is fleet occupancy rather than per-endpoint load. A model-group level surface can sum later if it needs the fleet view; this route is per-deployment, so it does not.

requests_last_30m stays a sum: request counts add up across replicas, concurrent occupancy does not.

docs.title: 9. What is still open
docs.text:
Recorded so these are not mistaken for finished. The full register, with priorities, is in docs/oicm-status/PROGRESS-AND-PAUSED-WORK.md.

Item Where Blocks M2 engine-load telemetry (running/queued requests, KV utilization) not started, no RuntimeTelemetryProvider in the tree the instantaneous engine view; the reserved -1 status depends on it reserved -1 endpoint status gateway_status.py, deliberately unassigned blocked on M2 perf_last_30m_by_workload not implemented (§8e) needs a metric-to-workload classifier runtime detection (§8a) registry.py::_detect_runtime_kind makes provider_name/tag/capabilities wrong for every deployment discarded enrichment (§8b) models_service.py dead work per request max_*_tokens always null (§8c) openai_compatible.py:78 two always-null fields data.architecture empty (§8d) _response_architecture() one always-empty envelope field

Not open: M1 (Steps 13-18) and M3 Step 25, including all four telemetry fields and their percentiles. live_concurrency semantics were pinned down on 2026-10-07 (§8g): it is the busiest replica's load, max by (model_id).

docs.title: 10. Verified live (dev, 2026-10-07)
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/models/zai-org/GLM-5.3/endpoints, after six streaming requests warmed the window:

latency_last_30m    : {p50: 37.7, p75: 44.1, p90: 47.9, p99: 68.0}     ms
throughput_last_30m : {p50: 400.0, p75: 266.7, p90: 222.2, p99: 202.0} tok/s
uptime_last_5m/30m/1d : 0.0 / 100.0 / 100.0
live_concurrency    : 0
requests_last_30m   : 11.35
status              : 0
max_prompt_tokens   : null (present, not omitted)

live_concurrency was also observed flipping 0 -> 1 mid-request, and the windowed fields were observed reading null / 0.0 while the window held no qualifying samples, then populating once it did. Those are the honest no-data answers, not defects.

docs.title: The max-vs-sum change, verified on real multi-pod data
docs.text:
The semantics change from sum by to max by is measurable against prod, which runs two pods for the same model_id. Read-only Prometheus queries, same instant:

raw gauge series for model_id f9a591e0 (GLM-5.3)
  pod litellm-proxy-5c46cf7f4c-79vdh -> 362
  pod litellm-proxy-5c46cf7f4c-vgnxz -> 354
sum by (model_id) -> 716    # old: double-counts a 2-pod deployment
max by (model_id) -> 362    # new: load on the busiest replica

On dev, with one replica, the field still tracks real in-flight work. A streaming request that outlives a 30s scrape made the Prometheus gauge read 1, and GET /api/v1/models/zai-org/GLM-5.3/endpoints with a cold reader cache returned live_concurrency: 1 while the request was still in flight, then 0 once it finished.

docs.title: Mapping: litellm usage data to latency/throughput endpoint fields
docs.text:
Answers the question: what usage/telemetry does litellm natively capture, how accurate is it, and what could populate latency_last_30m, throughput_last_30m, uptime_last_5m/30m/1d, and the reserved -1 load-based status.

Live verification: prod https://litellm.ecouncil.ae, 2026-10-07 14:41-15:15 UTC, key sk-05132025 (from docs/credentials.md). All findings below were observed on the actual deployment, not inferred.

Companion doc: MAPPING-litellm-to-endpoints.md (the field-by-field /endpoints mapping; its §4b describes the fields this doc sources).

docs.title: 0. What shipped, and where it diverged from this doc
docs.text:
This doc is the audit that fed the source decision. Two of its recommendations were not followed, deliberately, and one finding it recorded as blocking was fixed. Read this before §3.

Source: Prometheus, not the rollup table. §8h recommends the rollup table / SpendLogs. The implementation reads the cluster Prometheus instead (enrichment/telemetry.py), for two reasons: every relevant metric already carries a model_id label, so per-deployment grouping is a plain sum by (model_id) with no join, and the rollup does not carry a per-deployment key to join on (it is keyed by model_group). A 15s reader cache bounds the query load, so the extra Prometheus traffic is one query set per TTL per proxy process, not one per request.

Concurrency: the Prometheus gauge, now that the leak is fixed. §8e says the in-flight gauge is unusable. That finding was correct against the prod image at the time, and the leak was then fixed at the source (deployment_in_flight.py: a keyed registry with TTL eviction, plus a per-worker sweeper). On dev the gauge now reads 0 at idle and flips to 1 mid-request. The endpoints field is live_concurrency, sourced from that gauge. Prod ran the pre-fix bytes until 2026-10-08, so it kept showing the phantom values until it was rolled; it is now on the same digest as dev. See oicm-status/PROGRESS-AND-PAUSED-WORK.md, "Prod rollout: done".

Throughput: followed as recommended. §8g says to use per-request generation speed, not the counter rate. throughput_last_30m is the inverse of the litellm_deployment_latency_per_output_token histogram, which is the per-request definition.

Latency: followed as recommended, with the histogram rather than the rollup (as above). latency_last_30m is TTFT percentiles from litellm_llm_api_time_to_first_token_metric.

Uptime: counters, as §8h's alternative. §8h offered the health table or the success/failure counters. The counters shipped (success/(success+failure)*100), read as two separate queries so a zero-failure deployment still reports 100.

docs.title: 1. What litellm natively captures (the inventory)
docs.text:
Three tiers, all populated on every routed request:

Tier Store Fields Granularity Retention raw request log LiteLLM_SpendLogs startTime, endTime, request_duration_ms (int ms), completionStartTime (TTFT end; forced to endTime for non-streaming), completion_tokens, cache_hit, status, model_group, custom_llm_provider, entity columns (team/user/end_user/api_key/agent_id) per request janitor (60d floor) 1-minute rollup LiteLLM_ModelPerformanceRollup per model_group per minute: request_count, completion_tokens, throughput_tokens_sum, ttft_seconds_sum, 32-bin ttft histogram, starts/ends counters per minute same janitor Prometheus /metrics litellm_deployment_in_progress_requests (gauge), litellm_deployment_total_requests_total (counter), litellm_output_tokens_metric_total (counter), litellm_llm_api_time_to_first_token_metric (histogram), litellm_deployment_latency_per_output_token (histogram) 30s scrape 15d

The rollup's (starts, ends) counters exist specifically so peak concurrency can be recomputed at read time as a running sum (write path in model-performance-optimization-LOGIC-MAP.md, read path in model-performance-30d-read-fix-LOGIC-MAP.md).

Two read surfaces:

Endpoint Source Concurrency definition Throughput definition GET /model/metrics/per_model (realtime page) Prometheus, per deployment (model_id) max by (model_id) (max_over_time(gauge[window])) sum by (model_id) (rate(output_tokens[window])) GET /model/performance?window=5m/15m/1h Prometheus, merged to model group sum by (model_id, litellm_model_name) (max_over_time(gauge[step])) same counter rate, sum by (model_id, requested_model) GET /model/performance?window=24h/7d/30d/... (global) rollup table running sum of starts-ends, max per bucket (peak) per-request completion_tokens/request_duration_ms*1000, averaged per bucket then across buckets /model/performance entity-scoped or custom range raw SpendLogs SQL same running-sum peak same per-request average /spend/logs, /spend/logs/ui raw SpendLogs per-request request_duration_ms, TTFT —

docs.title: 2. The user's suspicion, verified on prod
docs.text: Claim checked: "realtime is not accurate, especially concurrency and throughput versus historical". Verdict: confirmed for concurrency, and the two surfaces disagree with each other; throughput is directionally right but defined differently per surface.

docs.title: 2.1 Realtime concurrency is a leaked gauge, not real load
docs.text:
Observed on prod (DB ground truth computed from the same window):

Deployment realtime gauge (per pod) /model/performance 1h DB truth hamsa/hamsa-stt 690 and 644 1334 flat 0 in flight; zero traffic since 2026-10-05 08:47 UTC; rollup starts=ends=677 over lifetime zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash 418 and 335 418+335 summed into group DB running-sum peak last 1h = 9 zai-org/GLM-5.3 362 and 353 ~713 peak last 1h = 5 Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 21 and 22 merged peak last 1h = 21 (this one looked real at 14:44 but drained to 0 by 15:05; the residual was transient overlap, not a leak)

Mechanism, traced in the code and confirmed by metric accounting on the pods:

  • The gauge is OICM-custom (deployment_in_flight.py). The ledger incs in async_pre_call_deployment_hook (fires inside the @client wrapper, before the provider call) and decs in set_llm_deployment_success_metrics / set_llm_deployment_failure_metrics.
  • On both prod pods, hamsa-stt has only the gauge series: zero deployment_total_requests, zero success/failure counters. 644 incs fired whose terminal logging event never ran. The STT path (atranscription via router _atranscription -> litellm.atranscription, also @client-wrapped) enters the inc, but its failures can terminate without a prometheus async_log_failure_event (e.g. exceptions raised after the wrapper's hook but before logging setup, client aborts, or failures in pre-call checks) so the dec never lands.
  • For chat models the same leak exists but smaller: GLM-5.3-Flash pod 79vdh counters show 71,359 total / 71,165 success / 194 failure since pod start, yet the gauge sits at 418 while DB peak concurrency is 9. The ratchet is event-correlated, not steady: the gauge climbed from ~50 to 442 during a 12:21-12:36 UTC window with 239 failed requests (ReadTimeouts / 4xx burst), then froze. Failures whose logging path skips the prometheus dec leave a permanent +1 each; retries re-enter the wrapped function and fire another inc while the failed attempt's dec never ran.
  • The Aug 24 fix (commit 0b0413b4f2) aligned model_id resolution between the inc and the success dec; it is deployed in prod. The remaining leak is inc-without-any-dec (terminal events that never reach prometheus at all), which that fix cannot address.

docs.title: 2.2 The two realtime surfaces contradict each other
docs.text:
For the same minute, same prod:

  • /model/metrics/per_model hamsa-stt concurrent = 690 (max over pods)
  • /model/performance 1h hamsa-stt concurrent = 1334 (sum across pods: _merge_series_into sums every series sharing the model name)

Both are wrong (truth is 0), and they disagree by construction. Even with a healthy gauge the two are different quantities: max-across-replicas (peak load on the busiest pod) vs sum-across-replicas (fleet-wide concurrency). The endpoints page must pick one definition; today it has two.

docs.title: 2.3 Historical (DB/rollup) concurrency is the accurate one
docs.text:
The rollup/DB running-sum matches ground truth: recomputing the running sum directly over SpendLogs for the last hour gives peaks of 9 (GLM-5.3- Flash), 24 (Kimi-K3), 34 (Qwen3-Embedding-4B), and the 24h endpoint's rollup numbers (GLM-5.3-Flash avg_concurrent 16.4, GLM-5.3 2.68) are consistent with the per-minute starts/ends counters. Known approximations, both benign:

  • 1-minute granularity (a sub-minute burst can peak higher than the bucket max reports).
  • Boundary-time approximation: concurrency is derived from request start/end timestamps, not true in-flight instants. A request whose logged end is delayed (flush queue) shifts its -1 late, inflating the tail of its minute. With 30s flushes and minute buckets this is noise.
  • endTime is never NULL in prod (18.9M rows checked), so there is no missing-end distortion today.

docs.title: 2.4 Throughput definitions differ per surface (all "true", none wrong)
docs.text:
Same prod hour, three views of GLM-5.3-Flash:

  • realtime per-model: rate(litellm_output_tokens_metric_total[1h]) last = 1126.9 tok/s (fleet instantaneous output rate)
  • /model/performance 1h: same counter aggregated, avg 1248 tok/s
  • 24h rollup: avg_throughput = 101.1 (per-request tokens/sec, averaged)

The realtime number is "how many tokens per second is the fleet producing right now"; the DB number is "what was the average per-request generation speed". A customer reading throughput_last_30m expects the OpenRouter definition (tokens/sec of generation speed per request, i.e. the DB definition). The counter-rate number also includes time when nobody is streaming, which drags it toward zero; it is a capacity metric, not a per-request speed metric.

docs.title: 2.5 TTFT is consistent where it exists
docs.text: Prometheus TTFT (litellm_llm_api_time_to_first_token_metric) and DB TTFT (completionStartTime - startTime) both exclude nothing/everything identically only for streaming; DB TTFT uses request start (includes preprocessing), the prometheus histogram also uses request start. The two definitions were aligned in the Aug 24 fix. Non-streaming requests are excluded from both (DB: completionStartTime != endTime guard; histogram: only observed for streams). Historical p50s from the rollup histogram are the right source for a latency-style field.

docs.title: 3. Findings (numbered, continuing the mapping doc series)
docs.text:
8e. Realtime concurrency is unusable as-is. The in-flight gauge leaks inc-without-dec events (terminal logging skipped: client aborts, pre-log exceptions, retry re-entry), producing frozen phantom values (690/644 on a zero-traffic deployment; 418/335 on a busy one whose true peak is 9). Both realtime surfaces read it. Until the leak is fixed at the source (or the gauge is periodically reconciled against DB truth), no endpoint field should be fed from it. The DB/rollup running-sum is the trustworthy concurrency source at all horizons.

Resolved 2026-10-07. The leak was fixed at the source: the gauge is now a keyed registry with TTL eviction plus a per-worker sweeper (litellm/integrations/prometheus_helpers/deployment_in_flight.py). Verified on dev: idle reads 0, a single in-flight request reads 1, three parallel read 3, and a killed client returns to 0. live_concurrency is therefore fed from the gauge. The historical note above described the prod image, which ran the old bytes until 2026-10-08; prod is now on the same digest as dev.

8f. The two concurrency read surfaces disagree by construction (max across pods in per_model vs sum across pods in /model/performance, 690 vs 1334 observed for the same model in the same minute). Whichever feeds the endpoints route must state its semantics; for a per-endpoint (deployment) field, per-pod max is the honest one; the "sum" merge only makes sense at model-group level.

Implemented 2026-10-07. The endpoints route follows this reading: live_concurrency is max by (model_id), the peak load on the busiest replica, not the fleet-wide sum. The sum-across-replicas behavior in /model/performance is a separate surface and is unchanged. Live proof on prod's two-pod GLM-5.3 deployment: the same model_id reads 716 summed and 362 with max.

8g. Throughput semantics must match OpenRouter's. throughput_last_30m should be per-request generation speed (completion_tokens / request duration), the DB/rollup definition. The prometheus counter rate is a fleet capacity metric and under-reports speed under low load.

Implemented 2026-10-07. throughput_last_30m is the inverse of the litellm_deployment_latency_per_output_token histogram, i.e. per-request generation speed in tokens/second, matching this finding.

8h. Best-fit sources for the telemetry fields (all already persisted; no new capture needed): - latency_last_30m: p50 TTFT from the rollup ttft histogram, last 30 minutes of buckets (streaming only; state that or fall back to p50 request_duration_ms for non-streaming models). - throughput_last_30m: rollup throughput_tokens_sum / active-time or per-request average from SpendLogs (same SQL the 24h path already runs, window shrunk to 30m; entity-scope filter not needed for the global field). - uptime_last_5m/30m/1d: not concurrency at all; derive from the health table history the gateway_status resolver already reads (share of healthy checks in the window), or from litellm_deployment_success/failure counters (success / (success + failure)) which prod shows are accurate (GLM-5.3-Flash: 71,165 success / 194 failure since pod start). - reserved -1 status (SGLang load telemetry): the DB concurrency running-sum over a short window is the only trustworthy input; do not gate it on the prometheus gauge.

As implemented 2026-10-07. The shape above held; the source is Prometheus rather than the rollup, for the per-deployment key reason in §0. Concretely: latency_last_30m is histogram_quantile over rate(TTFT_bucket[30m]), throughput_last_30m is the inverted per-token-latency histogram, uptime_last_* is the success/failure counters (the second option above), and the reserved -1 status is still unassigned. perf_last_30m_by_workload is not implemented.

docs.title: 4. Proof-of-verification commands (read-only, prod)
docs.text:
• GET /model/metrics/per_model?window=1h -> 27 deployments; hamsa-stt concurrent flat 690; GLM-5.3-Flash flat 424.
  • GET /model/performance?window=1h -> source=prometheus; hamsa-stt avg_concurrent 1334 flat; GLM-5.3-Flash group 752.
  • GET /model/performance?window=24h -> source=rollup; GLM-5.3-Flash avg_concurrent 16.4, avg_throughput 101.1, p50_ttft 13.8s.
  • PromQL range queries on the gauge: 7-day history for hamsa-stt shows a monotonic ratchet 10 -> 644 with zero traffic; GLM-5.3-Flash shows the ratchet coinciding with the 12:21-12:36 UTC failure burst.
  • SQL ground truth (prod postgres, read-only): running-sum peak per model for the last hour; rollup starts vs ends per model; per-pod deployment_* counter sums vs gauge via each pod's authenticated /metrics.

docs.title: Design and Implementation Instructions
docs.text: Status: Implementation design Target: Add an OpenRouter-compatible GET /api/v1/models capability-discovery surface to a LiteLLM Gateway Primary runtimes: SGLang and vLLM on internal Kubernetes services Design date: 2026-08-14

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text:
Implement a new, clearly separated OpenRouter-compatible model-discovery API in LiteLLM:

GET /api/v1/models

The endpoint must:

  1. Return the current OpenRouter Models API response shape.
  2. Discover live deployment information from the actual upstream inference runtime.
  3. Support SGLang and vLLM first.
  4. Be extensible to other runtimes and hosted providers later.
  5. Reuse LiteLLM's existing pricing/model registry logic rather than creating a second pricing database.
  6. Avoid persistent state in the first implementation.
  7. Keep runtime-specific parsing separate from OpenRouter serialization.
  8. Preserve LiteLLM authorization/model-access behavior.
  9. Remain resilient when an upstream model server is unavailable.
  10. Be maintainable as OpenRouter, vLLM, SGLang, and LiteLLM evolve.

The public API contract is OpenRouter-compatible. The internal implementation must not be coupled to OpenRouter's data model.

docs.title: 2.1 Keep /v1/models unchanged
docs.text:
Keep LiteLLM's existing OpenAI-compatible endpoint:

GET /v1/models

Add the richer compatibility surface separately:

GET /api/v1/models

Future OpenRouter-compatible routes should live under the same namespace:

/api/v1/models
/api/v1/models/{author}/{slug}/endpoints
/api/v1/models/{slug}/endpoints

This avoids breaking normal OpenAI-compatible clients and gives OpenRouter-specific behavior a clean boundary.

docs.title: 2.2 Runtime metadata is live and ephemeral
docs.text:
Do not initially persist runtime facts such as:

  • actual served model ID;
  • actual deployment context length;
  • runtime version;
  • runtime-supported task routes;
  • SGLang image/audio understanding;
  • OpenAPI-discovered API surface.

Initial flow:

request
  -> resolve caller-visible LiteLLM deployments
  -> query live upstream runtime
  -> normalize
  -> enrich from LiteLLM registry/pricing
  -> aggregate
  -> map into OpenRouter response
  -> discard

A cache can be added later, but it is an optimization, not the source of truth.

docs.title: 2.3 OpenRouter owns the output schema
docs.text:
Do not maintain a handwritten copy of OpenRouter's Model type.

Use the official generated Python SDK as the output-contract dependency:

from openrouter.components.model import Model as OpenRouterModel

OpenRouter's official generated source is marked Code generated by Speakeasy ... DO NOT EDIT.

Pin the SDK to a tested version in the image/build. Upgrade it through Renovate/Dependabot or an equivalent controlled dependency workflow.

Do not dynamically clone OpenRouter, install latest, or generate code at application startup.

docs.title: 2.4 Our code owns the mapper, not the OpenRouter schema
docs.text:
Ownership boundary:

OpenRouter owns:
  API schema
  generated SDK types

Our LiteLLM extension owns:
  discovery
  normalization
  aggregation
  pricing enrichment
  mapping
  failure policy
  caching

When OpenRouter adds an optional field, an SDK upgrade should usually remain compatible. When it adds a required field, contract tests should fail until the mapper has an explicit policy. That failure is desirable.

docs.title: 2.5 Never map runtime JSON directly into OpenRouter
docs.text:
Use four layers:

1. Raw runtime DTOs
2. DiscoveredDeploymentModel
3. AggregatedModel
4. OpenRouter generated output model

Dependency direction only:

raw DTO -> canonical deployment -> aggregation -> OpenRouter mapper

docs.title: 3.1 SGLang v0.5.16
docs.text:
/v1/models exposes:

id
object
created
owned_by
root
parent
max_model_len

/model_info exposes richer facts:

model_path
tokenizer_path
is_generation
preferred_sampling_params
weight_version
has_image_understanding
has_audio_understanding
model_type
architectures

/get_model_info remains a deprecated alias for /model_info.

Therefore SGLang discovery should use:

/v1/models
/model_info
/openapi.json       optional

docs.title: 3.2 vLLM v0.24.0
docs.text:
/v1/models exposes:

id
object
created
owned_by
root
parent
max_model_len
permission

vLLM does not expose a normal production /model_info endpoint equivalent to SGLang's richer endpoint.

Current vLLM builds parts of its FastAPI surface from supported_tasks; generation, speech-to-text/realtime, and pooling route groups are conditionally registered. Therefore /openapi.json can be useful for API/task capability discovery.

However, vLLM can disable OpenAPI/docs with:

--disable-fastapi-docs

so the OpenAPI probe must be optional.

docs.title: 4. Recommended package layout
docs.text:
Keep the route handler thin and isolate the implementation:

litellm/
└── proxy/
    └── openrouter_compat/
        ├── routes/
        │   ├── models.py
        │   └── model_endpoints.py
        │
        ├── domain/
        │   ├── identity.py
        │   ├── limits.py
        │   ├── architecture.py
        │   ├── capabilities.py
        │   ├── deployment.py
        │   ├── logical_model.py
        │   └── provenance.py
        │
        ├── discovery/
        │   ├── base.py
        │   ├── registry.py
        │   ├── resolver.py
        │   ├── adapters/
        │   │   ├── openai_compatible.py
        │   │   ├── vllm.py
        │   │   └── sglang.py
        │   └── probes/
        │       ├── base.py
        │       ├── openai_models.py
        │       ├── openapi.py
        │       └── sglang_model_info.py
        │
        ├── aggregation/
        │   ├── aggregator.py
        │   └── policies.py
        │
        ├── enrichment/
        │   ├── pricing.py
        │   ├── litellm_metadata.py
        │   └── capabilities.py
        │
        ├── mapping/
        │   └── openrouter.py
        │
        ├── transport/
        │   ├── client.py
        │   └── errors.py
        │
        ├── cache/
        │   └── memory.py
        │
        └── service.py

The exact route-registration file should follow the LiteLLM branch you are modifying, but business logic should not live in the main proxy handler.

docs.title: 5. Canonical internal domain model
docs.text: Use composition for capabilities. Use inheritance only for discovery protocol behavior.

docs.title: 5.1 Identity
docs.text:
class ModelIdentity(BaseModel):
    logical_model_name: str
    upstream_model_id: str | None = None

    root: str | None = None
    parent: str | None = None

    display_name: str | None = None
    canonical_id: str | None = None
    hugging_face_id: str | None = None
    created: int | None = None

Rules:

  • logical_model_name is the LiteLLM-facing routable name.
  • upstream_model_id is what vLLM/SGLang reports.
  • root is internal only. vLLM may expose a filesystem path there.
  • Never return PVC paths, tokenizer paths, ClusterIP addresses, or other internal identifiers publicly.

docs.title: 5.2 Limits
docs.text:
class ModelLimits(BaseModel):
    context_length: int | None = None
    max_input_tokens: int | None = None
    max_completion_tokens: int | None = None

Keep all three concepts separate.

For current vLLM/SGLang:

max_model_len -> context_length

Do not generically alias arbitrary fields such as max_tokens, max_input_tokens, and max_model_len because their semantics can differ.

docs.title: 5.3 Architecture
docs.text:
class ModelArchitecture(BaseModel):
    model_type: str | None = None
    architectures: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    tokenizer: str | None = None
    instruct_type: str | None = None

SGLang /model_info can populate model_type and architectures even though OpenRouter does not expose those exact internal fields.

docs.title: 5.4 Model capabilities
docs.text:
Do not create classes such as VisionModel, AudioModel, or VisionAudioModel.

class ModelCapabilities(BaseModel):
    input_modalities: set[str] | None = None
    output_modalities: set[str] | None = None

    tool_calling: bool | None = None
    parallel_tool_calling: bool | None = None
    reasoning: bool | None = None
    structured_outputs: bool | None = None
    logprobs: bool | None = None
    embeddings: bool | None = None
    rerank: bool | None = None

    is_moderated: bool | None = None
    supported_parameters: set[str] | None = None
    supported_voices: list[str] | None = None

Preserve tri-state semantics:

True  = explicitly supported
False = explicitly unsupported
None  = unknown

Never translate omission into False.

docs.title: 5.5 API capabilities
docs.text:
Keep server/API capability separate from model capability:

class ApiCapabilities(BaseModel):
    chat_completions: bool | None = None
    completions: bool | None = None
    responses: bool | None = None
    embeddings: bool | None = None
    transcription: bool | None = None
    speech: bool | None = None
    rerank: bool | None = None
    classification: bool | None = None
    routes: set[str] = Field(default_factory=set)

Meaning:

/openapi.json -> what the server API exposes
/model_info   -> what the loaded model can actually understand

Those are not equivalent.

docs.title: 5.6 Runtime information
docs.text:
class RuntimeInfo(BaseModel):
    kind: str
    version: str | None = None
    deployment_id: str
    api_base_fingerprint: str | None = None

Never expose the real private api_base in public output.

docs.title: 5.7 Provenance
docs.text:
Recommended:

class FactSource(BaseModel):
    probe: str
    field: str | None = None

class ModelProvenance(BaseModel):
    facts: dict[str, FactSource] = Field(default_factory=dict)

Examples:

limits.context_length
  <- OpenAIModelsProbe.max_model_len

capabilities.input_modalities.image
  <- SGLangModelInfoProbe.has_image_understanding

Keep provenance internal.

docs.title: 5.8 Canonical deployment object
docs.text:
class DiscoveredDeploymentModel(BaseModel):
    identity: ModelIdentity
    limits: ModelLimits
    architecture: ModelArchitecture
    capabilities: ModelCapabilities
    api_capabilities: ApiCapabilities
    runtime: RuntimeInfo
    provenance: ModelProvenance

Every runtime/provider adapter must eventually return this type.

docs.title: 6. Upstream transport DTOs
docs.text:
External runtime responses must be permissive because new versions may add fields.

class UpstreamDTO(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="allow")

Common OpenAI-compatible card:

class OpenAICompatibleModelCard(UpstreamDTO):
    id: str
    object: str | None = None
    created: int | None = None
    owned_by: str | None = None
    root: str | None = None
    parent: str | None = None

class RuntimeModelCard(OpenAICompatibleModelCard):
    max_model_len: int | None = None

vLLM:

class VLLMModelCard(RuntimeModelCard):
    permission: list[dict] = Field(default_factory=list)

SGLang:

class SGLangModelCard(RuntimeModelCard):
    pass

class SGLangModelInfo(UpstreamDTO):
    model_path: str | None = None
    tokenizer_path: str | None = None
    is_generation: bool | None = None
    preferred_sampling_params: dict | None = None
    weight_version: str | None = None
    has_image_understanding: bool | None = None
    has_audio_understanding: bool | None = None
    model_type: str | None = None
    architectures: list[str] | None = None

docs.title: 7. Discovery adapter hierarchy
docs.text:
Use inheritance for protocol behavior:

BaseDiscoveryAdapter
│
├── RuntimeDiscoveryAdapter
│   └── OpenAICompatibleRuntimeAdapter
│       ├── VLLMDiscoveryAdapter
│       ├── SGLangDiscoveryAdapter
│       ├── future TGIAdapter
│       ├── future TensorRTLLMAdapter
│       └── future LlamaCppAdapter
│
└── ProviderDiscoveryAdapter
    ├── OpenAICompatibleProviderAdapter
    │   └── future XAIAdapter
    ├── future AnthropicAdapter
    ├── future BedrockAdapter
    └── future VertexAdapter

Do not create adapters named after individual model families such as ClaudeAdapter or GrokAdapter. The adapter represents the discovery protocol/provider/runtime, not one model.

Template:

class BaseDiscoveryAdapter(ABC):

    async def discover(self, deployment):
        raw_models = await self.discover_models(deployment)

        models = [
            self.normalize_model(deployment, raw)
            for raw in raw_models
        ]

        return await self.enrich(deployment, models)

    @abstractmethod
    async def discover_models(self, deployment):
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def normalize_model(self, deployment, raw):
        ...

    async def enrich(self, deployment, models):
        return models

docs.title: 8. Reusable probes
docs.text:
Adapters should orchestrate reusable probes rather than duplicate HTTP behavior.

Implement:

OpenAIModelsProbe
  GET /v1/models

OpenAPISchemaProbe
  GET /openapi.json

SGLangModelInfoProbe
  GET /model_info
  fallback GET /get_model_info

Probe result should carry:

success/failure
data
source/probe name
latency
error category

An optional probe failure must not fail the complete model catalog.

docs.title: 9. vLLM adapter
docs.text:
Initial probe set:

/v1/models
/openapi.json optional

Map:

id             -> identity.upstream_model_id
created        -> identity.created
root           -> internal identity.root only
parent         -> identity.parent
max_model_len  -> limits.context_length
owned_by       -> runtime-detection hint only

Do not use permission as modality/capability metadata.

docs.title: 9.1 vLLM OpenAPI enrichment
docs.text:
If /openapi.json exists, inspect:

paths
HTTP methods
operationId
requestBody
components.schemas

Examples of useful API-surface evidence:

/v1/chat/completions      -> chat_completions API available
/v1/embeddings            -> embeddings API available
/v1/audio/transcriptions  -> transcription API available

Because vLLM conditionally registers some router groups from supported_tasks, route presence can be meaningful.

But:

/v1/chat/completions exists

is not proof that the loaded model is text-only. Vision/multimodal models can use the same endpoint.

Treat OpenAPI as API/task evidence, not universal model-modality truth.

docs.title: 10. SGLang adapter
docs.text:
Probe set:

/v1/models
/model_info
/openapi.json optional

Base mapping is the same as vLLM for id, created, root, parent, and max_model_len.

Enrich from /model_info:

has_image_understanding = true
  -> add image input modality

has_audio_understanding = true
  -> add audio input modality

model_type
  -> architecture.model_type

architectures
  -> architecture.architectures

For the current DeepSeek SGLang deployment, explicit false values for image/audio are meaningful negatives because SGLang derives them from the loaded model config.

Support /get_model_info only as a fallback for older SGLang versions.

docs.title: 11. Runtime detection
docs.text:
Prefer:

1. explicit deployment metadata override
2. known provider/runtime configuration
3. /v1/models owned_by hint
4. safe probing
5. generic OpenAI-compatible fallback

Optional LiteLLM metadata:

model_info:
  discovery_runtime: sglang

or:

model_info:
  discovery_runtime: vllm

Do not require this field, but allow it to avoid guessing.

Do not build the primary logic around version comparisons such as:

if sglang_version >= ...

Use capability probing:

try /model_info
fallback /get_model_info
otherwise continue without native enrichment

Capture runtime version for diagnostics only.

docs.title: 12. OpenAPI probe rules
docs.text:
Create one reusable inspector:

class OpenAPIInspector:
    def has_path(self, path: str) -> bool: ...
    def has_operation(self, path: str, method: str) -> bool: ...
    def request_schema_mentions(self, path: str, symbol: str) -> bool: ...
    def parameter_names(self, path: str, method: str) -> set[str]: ...

V1 does not need a complete OpenAPI engine. Resolve enough local $ref references to inspect known request schemas.

Useful schema signals may include:

tools
tool_choice
parallel_tool_calls
response_format
reasoning
logprobs

But remember:

schema supports field != loaded model supports field

docs.title: 13. Evidence precedence
docs.text:
Use deterministic source precedence.

For live runtime/model facts:

1. explicit runtime-native loaded-model metadata
2. live runtime /v1/models
3. runtime OpenAPI route/schema evidence
4. explicit LiteLLM deployment model_info override
5. LiteLLM model registry
6. unknown

For pricing:

1. explicit LiteLLM deployment pricing/config
2. existing LiteLLM cost/model registry lookup
3. explicit configured fallback/unknown policy

Never let theoretical registry context overwrite a smaller live deployment context.

Example:

LiteLLM registry: 262144
vLLM max_model_len: 65536

advertise deployment context: 65536

docs.title: 14. LiteLLM pricing integration
docs.text:
Reuse your existing LiteLLM pricing path. Do not create another model price database.

Introduce a thin resolver interface:

class PricingResolver:
    async def resolve(self, logical_model, deployment):
        ...

Reuse current LiteLLM logic backed by its continuously maintained model_prices_and_context_window.json data and explicit deployment overrides.

OpenRouter currently requires pricing.prompt and pricing.completion in the Model object.

Define explicit behavior if pricing is unknown. Do not silently report zero unless zero is truly the gateway's billing semantics.

docs.title: 15. LiteLLM deployment resolver and authorization
docs.text:
Create:

class LiteLLMDeploymentResolver:
    async def resolve_for_request(self, auth_context):
        ...

Return a minimal descriptor:

class DeploymentDescriptor(BaseModel):
    deployment_id: str
    logical_model_name: str
    provider: str | None = None
    model: str | None = None
    api_base: str | None = None
    auth_headers: dict[str, str] | None = None
    model_info: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)

The new endpoint must reuse LiteLLM's current authentication and model-access filtering.

Security invariant:

A model the caller cannot invoke must not appear in /api/v1/models.

Filter inaccessible logical models before discovery fan-out.

Do not independently reimplement all key/team/user/access-group rules; call the same current LiteLLM helpers used by the proxy branch you are modifying.

docs.title: 16. SSRF and upstream URL safety
docs.text:
Discovery performs server-side HTTP requests, therefore discovery targets must come only from trusted LiteLLM deployment configuration.

Never accept discovery targets from:

query parameters
request body
model ID
user headers

There must never be a feature like:

GET /api/v1/models?api_base=http://arbitrary-host

If untrusted tenants can create deployments, add a network/host allowlist policy before enabling live probes.

docs.title: 17. HTTP transport
docs.text:
Use a shared async HTTP client with connection pooling.

class DiscoveryHTTPClient:
    async def get_json(self, deployment, path, *, timeout):
        ...

Requirements:

  • shared connection pool;
  • short configurable connect/read timeouts;
  • upstream auth support;
  • bounded concurrency;
  • response-size cap, especially for OpenAPI;
  • JSON validation;
  • clear timeout/HTTP/parse error categories;
  • no secrets in logs.

Suggested starting timeout range: 1-3 seconds per probe, configurable.

docs.title: 18. Concurrency and deduplication
docs.text:
Do not discover deployments serially.

Use bounded async fan-out:

results = await asyncio.gather(
    *tasks,
    return_exceptions=True,
)

with a semaphore.

Deduplicate identical discovery targets. If several LiteLLM deployments point to the same api_base + runtime + auth identity, one /openapi.json fetch should be reusable during the request/cache lifetime.

docs.title: 19. Kubernetes ClusterIP invariant
docs.text:
For V1, all replicas behind one inference Service should expose equivalent identity/capabilities/limits.

Good:

qwen-service
  pod A 262144
  pod B 262144
  pod C 262144

Unsafe:

qwen-service
  pod A 262144
  pod B 65536
  pod C 32768

A heterogeneous Service makes ClusterIP discovery nondeterministic.

Document homogeneous replicas as a V1 requirement. If heterogeneous replicas are needed later, query EndpointSlices/pods and model them as distinct deployments.

docs.title: 20. Aggregation layer
docs.text:
Discovery returns deployments. /api/v1/models returns logical models.

Example:

LiteLLM model_name = qwen-coder

  deployment A: vLLM   context 262144
  deployment B: SGLang context 131072

Keep both deployment objects, then aggregate:

class ModelAggregator:
    def aggregate(self, logical_model_name, deployments):
        ...

Canonical logical object:

class AggregatedModel(BaseModel):
    logical_model_name: str
    deployments: list[DiscoveredDeploymentModel]
    identity: ModelIdentity
    limits: ModelLimits
    architecture: ModelArchitecture
    capabilities: ModelCapabilities
    pricing: object | None = None

docs.title: 21. Conservative aggregation policies
docs.text: Keep policies explicit in aggregation/policies.py.

docs.title: 21.1 Context length
docs.text:
Default policy:

guaranteed logical context = minimum known context across eligible routable deployments

Reason: advertising the maximum is unsafe if LiteLLM can route the request to a smaller-context deployment.

Allow a configurable alternative only if routing semantics justify it:

class ContextAggregationPolicy(str, Enum):
    GUARANTEED_MIN = "guaranteed_min"
    MAX_AVAILABLE = "max_available"

Default to GUARANTEED_MIN.

docs.title: 21.2 Completion limit
docs.text: Apply the same conservative principle when multiple explicit limits exist.

docs.title: 21.3 Modalities/capabilities
docs.text:
If LiteLLM may route any request to any deployment, the logical model should advertise capabilities guaranteed across all eligible deployments.

Example:

A = text+image
B = text only

Do not advertise image at the logical level unless routing is capability-aware and guarantees image requests reach A.

The per-deployment endpoint can expose richer deployment-specific capabilities.

docs.title: 22. Unknown vs unsupported at OpenRouter boundary
docs.text:
Keep None internally for unknown.

OpenRouter's architecture.input_modalities and output_modalities are required arrays, so define one explicit mapper policy.

Recommended resolution before mapping:

runtime-native metadata
  -> OpenAPI/task evidence
  -> LiteLLM exact-model registry fallback
  -> unknown

If still unknown, either:

  1. emit an empty list without making a false claim, or
  2. in strict mode, omit the model because required architecture semantics are insufficiently known.

Make this configurable. Do not silently invent text just because a field is missing.

docs.title: 23. Supported parameters
docs.text:
Build through a resolver rather than directly from OpenAPI.

Potential evidence:

LiteLLM supported OpenAI params/model registry
runtime OpenAPI request schema
runtime-native metadata

When both sides are known, prefer:

known model support INTERSECT known runtime/API support

Examples:

temperature
top_p
max_tokens
max_completion_tokens
tools
tool_choice
parallel_tool_calls
response_format
structured_outputs
reasoning
reasoning_effort
logprobs

docs.title: 24. OpenRouter SDK integration
docs.text:
Prefer normal package dependency installation rather than copying one generated file.

openrouter.components.model.Model depends on generated sibling classes and OpenRouter SDK helper types, so copying only model.py is not maintainable.

Recommended:

pin official openrouter Python SDK version
run contract tests
upgrade with automated dependency PRs

If the SDK creates an unavoidable dependency conflict with the LiteLLM branch, only then fall back to vendoring/generating the required OpenRouter schema subset.

docs.title: 25. OpenRouter mapper
docs.text:
Only this layer imports OpenRouter generated classes.

class OpenRouterModelMapper:
    def map_model(self, model: AggregatedModel) -> OpenRouterModel:
        ...

Discovery adapters must never import OpenRouter types.

Current required OpenRouter Model fields include:

id
canonical_slug
name
created
pricing
context_length
architecture
top_provider
per_request_limits
supported_parameters
default_parameters
supported_voices
links

Required-but-nullable fields include several fields such as context_length, per_request_limits, default_parameters, and supported_voices.

Use OpenRouter's generated serializer so nullable/optional behavior follows their contract.

docs.title: 26. Current /api/v1/models list shape
docs.text:
At the time of this design, OpenRouter's list response requires:

{
  "data": [],
  "total_count": 0,
  "links": {
    "next": null
  }
}

Implement pagination arguments if clients may request them. At minimum, data, total_count, and links.next must be correct.

docs.title: 27. Public ID and canonical slug
docs.text:
The public id should remain LiteLLM's routable logical model_name, because clients will use the discovered ID for inference.

OpenRouterModel.id = LiteLLM logical model_name

For a bare alias such as:

qwen-coder

use a stable canonical namespace such as:

canonical_slug = litellm/qwen-coder

If the existing logical ID is already provider-like (qwen/qwen3.5), it may be used directly if stable.

Do not rewrite id into a value that LiteLLM inference does not accept.

docs.title: 28. Display name and created timestamp
docs.text:
Name priority:

1. configured display name
2. registry display name
3. upstream model ID
4. logical LiteLLM model name

For created, use a deterministic known runtime/deployment timestamp. Do not claim it is the model's release date unless you have actual release metadata. Runtime ModelCard creation timestamps may reflect server/model-card creation.

docs.title: 29. top_provider policy
docs.text:
Treat top_provider as the gateway's representative/guaranteed serving capability:

top_provider.context_length
  = aggregated guaranteed context

top_provider.max_completion_tokens
  = aggregated guaranteed completion limit

OpenRouter requires top_provider.is_moderated as a boolean. Since internal state may be unknown, define an explicit gateway policy/config default rather than accidentally turning None into False inside arbitrary code.

docs.title: 30. architecture mapping
docs.text:
OpenRouter currently requires:

modality
input_modalities
output_modalities

Keep OpenRouter-specific formatting in the mapper.

Do not make runtime adapters know OpenRouter enum conventions.

Internal SGLang fields such as:

model_type = deepseek_v4
architectures = [DeepseekV4ForCausalLM]

remain useful internal data even if not emitted by OpenRouter's current schema.

docs.title: 31. Model endpoint-details route
docs.text:
OpenRouter's required links.details points to a per-model endpoints resource.

Implement immediately after the list route:

GET /api/v1/models/{author}/{slug}/endpoints
GET /api/v1/models/{slug}/endpoints

The second form serves a model whose id has no author segment, e.g. hamsa-tts. The mapper namespaces such ids under litellm, so hamsa-tts is canonically litellm/hamsa-tts and the first form serves that. The bare form is accepted too so a client that reads the id straight from /v1/models does not have to know about the namespace. Both forms return the same body, keyed by the canonical id.

This route should use AggregatedModel.deployments and expose deployment/provider-specific limits/pricing/capabilities according to the current OpenRouter endpoint schema.

Do not return a permanently dead links.details URL.

docs.title: The match key is the LiteLLM routing name, not the upstream served id
docs.text:
{author}/{slug} is matched against the registered model_name, the string a caller puts in the request body. Re-joining author and slug reproduces it exactly, so the URL round-trips into a working request. A model registered without an author segment is canonically namespaced under litellm.

This is deliberately not the upstream served id, which the runtime reports at /v1/models and which can differ. Live example:

litellm model_name (routing, request body)  Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1
upstream /v1/models id (served)             Qwen-Image-2.1

Matching on the routing name is the only workable choice, because LiteLLM rejects the served name outright:

POST /v1/images/generations {"model": "Qwen-Image-2.1"}
  -> 400 Invalid model name passed in model=Qwen-Image-2.1

Keying the URL on the served id would therefore make the URL reject the very string the request body needs. The served id is still surfaced, as the endpoint's model_name field.

Do not assume a runtime validates model. Verified on the dev cluster: sending a deliberately bogus name straight to the upstream still returns HTTP 200 for both image generation (vLLM omni) and chat completions (SGLang). The upstream serves whatever it has loaded and ignores the field, which is the only reason the routing-name/served-id mismatch is invisible today. If a runtime ever starts validating model, the image model above breaks at that layer, and nothing in this code reconciles the two names.

model_name is not unique: several deployments can share it when the same model is served from more than one cluster. Routing on it is correct, LiteLLM load-balances across those deployments, and one URL then returns one endpoint object per deployment.

Never expose ClusterIP addresses, local filesystem paths, credentials, or private service names unless deliberately part of your public API.

docs.title: 32. Upstream authentication
docs.text:
Discovery must support private model runtimes when needed.

Reuse LiteLLM's resolved deployment credentials/headers.

Do not put secrets in:

logs
client errors
public provenance
plain-text cache keys

Use a hash/fingerprint if auth identity must participate in deduplication/cache keys.

docs.title: 33. Failure behavior
docs.text:
Default behavior should be resilient:

fan out discovery
collect successful deployments
log/measure failed probes
aggregate remaining deployments
return partial catalog

If one of several deployments fails, use the healthy ones.

If all deployments for a logical model fail:

fallback to sufficient LiteLLM config/registry metadata
otherwise omit the model in strict mode

Do not fabricate a live context limit after total discovery failure.

Internal error categories:

DiscoveryTimeout
DiscoveryConnectionError
DiscoveryHTTPError
DiscoveryInvalidJSON
DiscoverySchemaError
UnsupportedRuntime
MissingRequiredOpenRouterField

docs.title: 34. Caching
docs.text:
V1 may begin uncached if deployment count is small, but code interfaces should allow cache insertion.

Recommended cache key dimensions:

deployment identity
runtime kind
api_base fingerprint
auth identity fingerprint

Good cache targets:

raw /v1/models
raw /model_info
parsed OpenAPI capabilities
final DiscoveredDeploymentModel

Initial TTL when enabled:

5-30 seconds

No Postgres is needed.

Prefer caching deployment discovery and applying caller authorization/aggregation afterward. Never globally cache one caller's filtered model list and serve it to another caller.

docs.title: 35. Security and information disclosure
docs.text:
Do not publicly expose raw upstream data.

Never leak:

root filesystem paths
tokenizer paths
model_path
ClusterIP/FQDN
API keys
Authorization headers
PVC paths
raw OpenAPI documents
raw SGLang server_info/model_info

Map only explicitly approved public fields.

docs.title: 38. Performance tests
docs.text:
Benchmark at least:

10 deployments
25 deployments
100 deployments

Measure:

upstream request count
event-loop blocking
OpenAPI memory/parse cost

All upstream network I/O must be async.

LiteLLM has already experienced expensive /v1/models model-info paths, so this new network-based endpoint should be designed with bounded concurrency and optional TTL caching from the beginning.

docs.title: 39. Docker/build and OpenRouter schema maintenance
docs.text:
Recommended build flow:

1. install pinned LiteLLM fork dependencies
2. install pinned official OpenRouter Python SDK
3. run unit/contract tests
4. build immutable image
5. deploy

Do not:

clone OpenRouter main at container startup
install latest at runtime
download openapi.json and generate Python at runtime

Update flow:

OpenRouter SDK release
  -> Renovate/Dependabot PR
  -> contract tests
  -> optional schema additions pass
  -> required schema changes fail visibly
  -> mapper updated
  -> merge/release

docs.title: 41. Service orchestration pseudocode
docs.text:
class OpenRouterModelsService:

    async def list_models(
        self,
        auth_context,
        *,
        offset: int = 0,
        limit: int = 500,
    ):
        deployments = await self.deployment_resolver.resolve_for_request(
            auth_context
        )

        discoveries = await self.discovery_service.discover_many(
            deployments
        )

        discoveries = await self.metadata_enricher.enrich(
            discoveries
        )

        discoveries = await self.pricing_enricher.enrich(
            discoveries
        )

        models = self.aggregator.aggregate_all(discoveries)

        output = [
            self.mapper.map_model(model)
            for model in models
        ]

        total_count = len(output)
        page = output[offset:offset + limit]

        return {
            "data": page,
            "total_count": total_count,
            "links": {
                "next": build_next_link(
                    offset=offset,
                    limit=limit,
                    total_count=total_count,
                )
            },
        }

docs.title: 42. Discovery orchestration pseudocode
docs.text:
class DiscoveryService:

    async def discover_many(self, deployments):
        targets = deduplicate_targets(deployments)

        results = await asyncio.gather(
            *[
                self._discover_target(target)
                for target in targets
            ],
            return_exceptions=True,
        )

        return merge_discovery_results(
            deployments,
            targets,
            results,
        )

    async def _discover_target(self, deployment):
        adapter = self.registry.resolve(deployment)
        return await adapter.discover(deployment)

docs.title: 43. Future extension rule
docs.text:
Adding a new runtime such as TensorRT-LLM should require only:

1. unique transport DTO(s), if needed
2. a discovery adapter
3. optional native probe(s)
4. registry entry
5. tests

It should not require changing:

/api/v1/models route
OpenRouter public contract
SGLang adapter
vLLM adapter
canonical domain model

unless the new runtime introduces a genuinely new capability dimension.

Hosted providers belong under ProviderDiscoveryAdapter, not under runtime adapters.

docs.title: 44. What not to do
docs.text:
• [ ] Do not turn LiteLLM /v1/models into OpenRouter's schema.
  • [ ] Do not persist live SGLang/vLLM limits as the initial source of truth.
  • [ ] Do not create a second pricing database.
  • [ ] Do not copy only OpenRouter's model.py.
  • [ ] Do not generate/install schema code at runtime.
  • [ ] Do not map SGLang/vLLM JSON directly into OpenRouter output.
  • [ ] Do not infer vision=False from a missing vLLM field.
  • [ ] Do not treat route presence as proof of every modality.
  • [ ] Do not expose root/model/tokenizer paths or ClusterIP details.
  • [ ] Do not query arbitrary caller-supplied URLs.
  • [ ] Do not perform serial discovery fan-out.
  • [ ] Do not fail the whole catalog because one optional probe failed.
  • [ ] Do not use runtime-version conditionals as the primary adapter mechanism.
  • [ ] Do not silently turn unknown into zero/false.
  • [ ] Do not globally cache caller-specific authorization results.

docs.title: 45. Definition of done
docs.text:
• [ ] GET /api/v1/models exists separately from /v1/models.
  • [ ] Output validates against the pinned official OpenRouter Python SDK.
  • [ ] SGLang v0.5.16 context length is discovered live.
  • [ ] SGLang /model_info enriches image/audio/model architecture facts.
  • [ ] vLLM v0.24.0 context length is discovered live.
  • [ ] vLLM OpenAPI probing is optional and works when available.
  • [ ] LiteLLM's existing pricing logic is reused.
  • [ ] No separate persistent discovery state is required.
  • [ ] Runtime responses pass through canonical internal objects.
  • [ ] Multiple deployments aggregate under documented conservative policies.
  • [ ] Caller model authorization is preserved.
  • [ ] One failed runtime does not normally break the complete catalog.
  • [ ] Internal URLs, paths, and secrets are not exposed.
  • [ ] Discovery uses bounded async I/O.
  • [ ] Contract tests protect against OpenRouter SDK/schema changes.
  • [ ] Runtime fixture tests protect against vLLM/SGLang shape changes.
  • [ ] links.details points to a working endpoint.
  • [ ] Cache can later be added/removed without changing the public API.

docs.title: 46. Recommended first coding order
docs.text:
1. Pin OpenRouter SDK + add contract import test

2. Create canonical internal domain classes

3. Create raw OpenAI-compatible/vLLM/SGLang DTOs

4. Create shared async discovery HTTP transport

5. Implement OpenAIModelsProbe

6. Implement vLLM adapter
   -> validate context length end-to-end

7. Implement SGLangModelInfoProbe

8. Implement SGLang adapter
   -> validate modality enrichment

9. Implement LiteLLM deployment resolver
   -> preserve auth/model visibility

10. Wire existing LiteLLM pricing resolution

11. Implement aggregation policies

12. Implement OpenRouter mapper
    -> validate official generated Model objects

13. Add thin /api/v1/models route

14. Add per-model endpoint-details route

15. Add OpenAPI capability probe

16. Add TTL cache only after profiling

This produces a useful vertical slice early while leaving optional enrichment and optimization until after correctness.

docs.title: OpenRouter
docs.text:
• Current OpenAPI specification: https://openrouter.ai/openapi.json

  • Official generated Python SDK: https://github.com/OpenRouterTeam/python-sdk

Verified at design time:

  • Model has required fields including id, canonical_slug, name, created, pricing, context_length, architecture, top_provider, per_request_limits, supported_parameters, default_parameters, supported_voices, and links.
  • ModelsListResponse requires data, total_count, and links.
  • links.next is nullable.
  • ModelArchitecture requires modality, input_modalities, and output_modalities.
  • The official Python model is generated and implements OpenRouter-specific nullable/optional serialization rules.
