Scope: How to call Cloudflare/clef-flash through the LiteLLM gateway at /v1/systemone with production-shaped workloads: support-ticket triage, invoice state extraction, chat-log escalation, multi-signal fan-out, image (multimodal) state, and larger-than-fit inputs. Every example below was run against the production gateway with a key_type=llm_api customer key and shows the actual response.

Related docs: GATEWAY_GUIDE.md (gateway auth), the Hugging Face model card (model weights, benchmarks, the joint schema head), and Cloudflare's Workers AI docs (the hosted price sheet — not what you pay here, this is your own deployment)

docs.title: What this model actually is
docs.text:
clef-flash is a 9B multimodal decision model, post-trained from Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B. It is not a generator. A request gives it a state (text, JSON object, chat log, or images) plus a typed question schema, and it returns one probability distribution per question, joint over the whole batch, in a single forward pass. Three question types:

Type Use when Returns noul A yes/no judgement call {"noul": <probability true>, "type": "noul"} choice One of N named options the winning id + per-option probabilities score A 0..N-1 ordered scale weighted mean + per-level probabilities + the legend

The state is not a prompt; it is the thing being decided about. There is no instruction-decomposition, no scratchpad, no chain-of-thought. If you want the model to "reason about a user," you describe the user in state and put the structured questions in questions.

Base URL for every example: https://litellm.ecouncil.ae.

Auth: Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
Method Path Working? POST /v1/systemone yes, full feature set GET /v1/models yes, lists the model POST /v1/chat/completions no (pod refuses: "schema decisions, send them to /v1/systemone") POST /v1/embeddings no (same refusal) POST /v1/decisions no (pod refuses: "requires a generation model") POST /v1/rerank no (same refusal)

This is the pod refusing; there is no LiteLLM translation you are missing.

docs.title: Request shape
docs.text:
{
  "model": "Cloudflare/clef-flash",
  "state": <string | object | array>,
  "questions": {
    "<question-id>": <question>,
    ...
  }
}
  • state may be a plain string, a JSON object, or an array of records (chat logs, events). The pod concatenates what it needs.
  • questions is a map, keyed by your own id, of typed questions. Through the gateway there is no upper cap; we verified 65 questions answered in one call upstream, though Cloudflare's hosted version caps at 64 and the documented contract is "1 to 64".
  • Question ids: letters, digits, _, ., -, up to 100 chars. Required, because the response keys are your ids.
  • instructions is required through LiteLLM for noul (and recommended for the others). The HF model card says it is optional, but the gateway's own pydantic layer rejects an unlabeled noul with 400 A noul question requires instructions or criteria. Always send instructions.

Optional fields we will skip: chat_template_kwargs (chat-template flags, rare), temperature, prompt_format_version, return_prompt_token_ids (rejected by name on this checkpoint).

Optional multimodal: images — up to 4 items shaped {"data": <base64>, "media_type": "image/png" | "image/jpeg" | "image/webp"}. Each image is capped at 1,024 input tokens after resize.

docs.title: 1. Support-ticket triage (the canonical example)
docs.text:
This is Cloudflare's own example from the model card, matched to a real state and exercised live through the gateway:

KEY="Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>"
BASE=https://litellm.ecouncil.ae

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/systemone" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "Cloudflare/clef-flash",
    "state": "Checkout has been failing for every customer for the last hour.",
    "questions": {
      "urgent": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is this support request urgent?"
      },
      "team": {
        "type": "choice",
        "instructions": "Which team should handle this request?",
        "criteria": {
          "billing":   "Payments, invoices, and refunds",
          "technical": "Outages, errors, and configuration",
          "sales":     "Plans and upgrades"
        }
      },
      "severity": {
        "type": "score",
        "instructions": "How severe is the customer impact?",
        "criteria": ["No impact", "Minor", "Major", "Critical"]
      }
    }
  }'

Live response (measured 0.40 s through the gateway):

{
  "model": "Cloudflare/clef-flash",
  "answers": {
    "urgent": {
      "type": "noul",
      "noul": 0.9546474194456936
    },
    "team": {
      "type": "choice",
      "choice": "technical",
      "confidence": 0.9042547431102397,
      "probabilities": {
        "billing":   0.04961518325903059,
        "technical": 0.9361698287401597,
        "sales":     0.014214988000809664
      }
    },
    "severity": {
      "type": "score",
      "score": 2.717811544757861,
      "confidence": 0.7178115447578606,
      "legend": {"0": "No impact", "1": "Minor", "2": "Major", "3": "Critical"},
      "probabilities": {"0": 0.0152, "1": 0.0148, "2": 0.07, "3": 0.9}
    }
  },
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 196, "output_tokens": 0}
}

How to read the three together: the model is 95% sure this is urgent, routes it to engineering (technical, 90% confidence), and places the severity between "Major" and "Critical" (weighted mean 2.72 on a 0..3 scale). That is a page-worthy incident on one round trip.

docs.title: 2. Structured invoice state
docs.text:
The HF model card's second example, run as-is:

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/systemone" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "Cloudflare/clef-flash",
    "state": {
      "invoice": {
        "vendor": "Acme",
        "total": 1250.0,
        "currency": "USD",
        "status": "overdue"
      }
    },
    "questions": {
      "status": {
        "type": "choice",
        "instructions": "What is the invoice status?",
        "criteria": {
          "paid":    "Invoice is paid.",
          "overdue": "Invoice is past due.",
          "draft":   "Not sent."
        }
      },
      "large": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Is the total above 1000 USD?"
      }
    }
  }'

Live response: status: overdue at 97% confidence, large: 0.9734 (i.e. yes, the invoice is over $1000), 260 input tokens. The model is happy to read a JSON object directly; you do not need to flatten it into prose.

docs.title: 3. Chat-log escalation
docs.text:
State as an array of turns — this is the typical "watch my chatbot and page me if a customer goes sideways" wiring:

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/systemone" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "Cloudflare/clef-flash",
    "state": [
      {"role": "user",  "text": "My bill jumped from $50 to $180 without any warning."},
      {"role": "agent", "text": "I can see your auto-renewal is on the Pro plan now."},
      {"role": "user",  "text": "I never signed up for that!"}
    ],
    "questions": {
      "sentiment": {
        "type": "choice",
        "instructions": "Customer tone?",
        "criteria": {
          "calm":       "polite, composed",
          "frustrated": "visibly annoyed but civil",
          "angry":      "hostile, threats, or swearing"
        }
      },
      "escalate": {
        "type": "noul",
        "instructions": "Should this go to a supervisor right now?"
      }
    }
  }'

Live response: sentiment: frustrated (90% confidence), escalate: 0.7718. You would normally gate a supervisor page on a threshold of, say, noul > 0.6, so this ticket would page.

docs.title: 4. Multimodal: image as state
docs.text:
The pod answers has_image_understanding: true and takes up to 4 base64-encoded PNG/JPEG/WebP images per call. This is the smallest possible end-to-end validation, using a synthetic two-tone image (a 100x50 PNG, red on the left, blue on the right):

python3 - <<'PY'
import base64, json
png = open("/tmp/red_blue.png", "rb").read()  # any small test image
body = {
    "model": "Cloudflare/clef-flash",
    "state": "A two-tone image. Left half is one solid color, right half another.",
    "images": [{"data": base64.b64encode(png).decode(), "media_type": "image/png"}],
    "questions": {
        "left_color": {
            "type": "choice",
            "instructions": "What color is the LEFT half?",
            "criteria": {
                "red":    "pure red",
                "green":  "pure green",
                "blue":   "pure blue",
                "yellow": "pure yellow"
            }
        }
    }
}
open("/tmp/req.json", "w").write(json.dumps(body))
PY

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/systemone" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @/tmp/req.json

Live response: choice: red at 45% confidence (green 14%, blue 28%, yellow 13%), 179 input tokens. The right answer on a synthetic toy, with a low confidence that reflects how little signal the image carries — that is the model being calibrated, not a bug. Real receipts, screenshots and photos give confident answers.

Caps: 4 images, 4 MiB each, 16 MP each, 8 MiB total decoded, 13 MiB total request. Remote URLs are not accepted; embed base64.

docs.title: 5. Multi-signal fan-out
docs.text:
The whole point of the model is one round trip, many decisions. 65-question dispatch was run against the gateway and answered. Realistic batches are smaller — sentiment + intent + escalation + severity on the same ticket in one call — so a single state read by the schema head produces 4-8 decisions for the cost of one HTTP request.

Verified with 64 parallel noul questions in one POST: all 64 answered in one response. Past the documented cap of 64 questions the request still works on this sglang deployment (Cloudflare's hosted cap is a service-side guard, not a model limit).

docs.title: 6. Long-state truncation
docs.text:
The pod accepts a long state but silently truncates to 16,384 input tokens for encoding. Verified with a 135,000-character state: the call returned 200, and usage.input_tokens == 16384. If your state is longer than that, chunks or summarize upstream of the call — what you said at the far end will not reach the model.

For reference: wt*avg_word_length(4.7 chars/word) gives roughly 3,500 words per call.

docs.title: Limits you cannot tune away
docs.text:
• No generation. chat completions, embeddings, rerank all 400 with the pod's own message. Not a LiteLLM gap.
  • output_tokens always 0. Cost trackers keying on output tokens will report zero — charge on input_tokens only.
  • instructions is required for noul through the gateway. The HF card says it is optional; the gateway's pydantic layer enforces it.
  • No temperature / no seed / no replay determinism. Two identical calls are near-identical but not byte-identical.
  • No documented fallback group. The model is registered mode: None in LiteLLM, so mode-based router fallbacks cannot target it. If you need failover, register a second deployment of the same checkpoint.
  • No remote image URLs. base64 or nothing.

docs.title: Reading confidences like a pro
docs.text:
The model is calibrated: a 0.95 noul is roughly 19-to-1 in favour of yes. You can:

  • gate page-an-engineer on noul > 0.6
  • gate auto-close on intent == "feedback" with confidence > 0.9
  • use score probabilities to detect ambiguity: score.probabilities close to uniform means the model is unsure
  • threshold choice fallbacks: if top-2 probability mass is within 5%, route to a human or to a fallback model

The schema declares an x_label_mass field per answer (full-vocabulary mass on the answer labels). It is not present in current responses; do not depend on it.

docs.title: When not to use clef-flash
docs.text:
Task Use instead Open-ended chat any generative model (Qwen / DeepSeek / GLM) Long-form text generation same Generic text-embedding retrieval a dedicated embedder Real-time streaming voice or chat a TTS / STT stack

The model is the decision layer. Pair it with a generator for anything that writes prose.

docs.title: Fish Audio Drama 3 (TTS): Curl Guide
docs.text:
Scope: How to call Fish Audio Drama 3 text-to-speech (fishaudio/drama-3) through the LiteLLM gateway's /v1/audio/speech route, with sample curl commands, expected audio properties, error contracts, the direction-tag vocabulary that works, and which request fields the gateway forwards

Related docs: FISHAUDIO_DRAMA3_REGISTRATION_DIAGNOSIS.md (root cause of the original dropped fields and the chat mode, plus the proposed fix), INCEPTION_TTS_STT_GUIDE.md (another OpenAI-shaped TTS model on the same route), HAMSA-TTS-NEW-V1-GUIDE.md (Hamsa TTS)

docs.title: Gateway endpoints
docs.text:
Every route below was exercised against the production gateway (https://litellm.ecouncil.ae) with a key_type=llm_api virtual key, not the master key, so the status codes are what a customer sees.

Method Path Purpose Verified POST /v1/audio/speech Synthesize speech (all formats, streaming, cloning) 200 POST /v1/audio/voices Upload a voice (multipart) 200 DELETE /v1/voices/profiles/{name} Delete an uploaded voice 200 GET /v1/voices List voices (see caveat below) 200 GET /v1/voices/profiles Alias of the same listing 200 GET /v1/voices/profiles/{name} Fetch one profile 200 GET /v1/models Confirm the model is visible to your key 200 POST /v1/audio/speech/batch Batch synthesis 404, not proxied

Base URL for every example: https://litellm.ecouncil.ae.

docs.title: Scoping the listing: ?model= works (post-fix), unscoped picks one provider
docs.text:
GET /v1/voices reads the model from ?model= in the query string (bodies on GETs are never read). Two patterns matter:

  • explicit scope (recommended). ?model=fishaudio/drama-3 returns your drama3 registry including uploaded voices:
curl -s "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/voices?model=fishaudio/drama-3" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
# {"voices":["default","jensen","musk","trump"],
#  "uploaded_voices":[{"name":"jensen","created_at":1793783481,...}],
#  "cache_stats":{...}}
  • unscoped. With no query parameter the router picks the first voice-capable deployment by priority order. Verified live on production this is OmniVoice, returning its 31-entry catalogue (auto, design:<attributes>, OpenAI presets like alloy, and clone:* profiles):
curl -s "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/voices" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY"
# {"design_attributes":[...],"total":31,"voices":[{"id":"auto","type":"auto",...},...]}

The two shapes are not interchangeable: drama3's voices is a list of plain strings plus a parallel uploaded_voices list of objects, while OmniVoice's voices is a list of typed objects. Scope explicitly if you want a specific pod's registry. To inspect Drama 3's registry without scoping, probe it through a request that carries a body (POST /v1/audio/voices upload, or a speech request naming a voice), or call the pod directly (§12). The DELETE route does carry a body, so -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3"}' scopes it correctly.

Authentication is the standard LiteLLM gateway key passed as a Bearer token. The sglang-omni pod itself does not require auth, but the gateway always requires it:

Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>

The discovery controller registers the model as fishaudio/drama-3 (upstream hosted_vllm/fishaudio/drama-3), so send exactly that id. Unlike diarization, model is mandatory here: the route rejects an omitted model with Invalid model name passed in model=.

docs.title: Model overview
docs.text: Property Value Model ID fishaudio/drama-3 Underlying engine sglang-omni 0.2.0-cu130-amd64, stages preprocessing + tts_engine + vocoder Type Text to speech (35B MoE, 3B active, 10-codebook audio decoder) Input JSON body with text; direction tags inline (§5) Output Binary audio, 44.1 kHz mono 16-bit Provider (upstream) hosted_vllm Deployed mode audio_speech, oicm_task: Text-to-Speech (see Mode) Capabilities on the pod voice cloning, persistent voices, direction tags, streaming, batch, sampling control Capabilities through the gateway all of them except batch (§4, §6, §7)

docs.title: Audio properties that break clients
docs.text:
Output is 44.1 kHz mono 16-bit PCM in a WAV container. This is not the 24 kHz the OpenAI API produces. A client that hardcodes 24 kHz will play back at the wrong pitch and speed, roughly 1.8x too fast. Read the sample rate out of the WAV header, or declare it for raw pcm:

ffprobe -hide_banner out.wav   # expect 44100 Hz, 1 channel, 16-bit

pcm responses carry no header at all, so the 44.1 kHz / mono / 16-bit little-endian layout is the client's responsibility.

docs.title: Request shape
docs.text:
JSON body posted to /v1/audio/speech:

Field Required Notes model yes Must be fishaudio/drama-3 input yes The text to speak, as a plain string. Direction tags go inline (§5). Long text is chunked automatically by the pod voice no Defaults to the default voice when omitted. "default", or a registered uploaded voice name (§6). OpenAI voice names such as alloy are rejected by the pod response_format no wav (default), mp3, flac, pcm, aac, opus speed no Playback speed multiplier, honored end to end instructions no Forwarded, but Drama 3 does not support it: the pod returns 400 stream no Forwarded; requires response_format: "pcm" (the pod rejects stream with a container format). Delivery is chunked (§7) references no Forwarded; inline voice cloning (§6)

The gateway dispatches this model through its drama3 provider path, which forwards every non-LiteLLM field to the pod. The pod is strict about unknown fields, so a misspelled field is a 400 (unknown speech request field), never a silent drop. See §4 for the forwarding contract.

docs.title: Sample curl
docs.text:
curl -s "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "fishaudio/drama-3",
    "input": "Hello, how are you today?",
    "voice": "default",
    "response_format": "wav"
  }' \
  -o out.wav

The response body is raw audio, so always redirect it to a file rather than letting it print to the terminal.

docs.title: Response shape
docs.text:
Aspect Value HTTP status 200 on success Content-Type Matches the format: audio/wav, audio/mpeg, audio/flac, audio/pcm, audio/aac, audio/opus Body Raw audio bytes. No JSON envelope

All six formats verified on production with a virtual key, same input ("Hello there."), correct container magic in every case:

response_format HTTP Bytes Content-Type Magic wav 200 73,772 audio/wav RIFF mp3 200 9,839 audio/mpeg ID3 flac 200 54,128 audio/flac fLaC pcm 200 81,920 audio/pcm raw samples aac 200 8,271 audio/aac ADTS FFF1 opus 200 7,802 audio/opus OggS

An unknown response_format is rejected by the pod rather than silently defaulted, consistent with the strict-field behaviour in §4.

docs.title: Verified example
docs.text:
A 25-character input produced 2.23 s of audio:

HTTP 200  audio/wav  196,652 bytes  44100 Hz  1 ch  16-bit  2.23 s

A 1,220-character input produced 95.11 s of audio in 15.1 s wall time, confirming that long text is chunked rather than truncated.

Omitting voice entirely is also valid and synthesizes with the default voice (verified live: HTTP 200, RIFF audio).

docs.title: 2. Parameters that work through the gateway
speed
docs.text:
Honored all the way to the engine. The same sentence measured 2.83-3.62 s of audio at speed: 1.0 and 1.60-1.70 s at speed: 2.0 (three runs each, varying only by generation length). Through the gateway the same effect holds: 3.30 s of audio at 1.0 versus 1.53 s at 2.0.

Verified on production as a monotonic size response to the same input string:

speed Bytes Relative 0.5 499,756 2.07x 1.0 241,708 1.00x 2.0 139,308 0.58x

Audio length scales with 1/speed as expected, so the field reaches the engine rather than being dropped and re-defaulted.

docs.title: response_format
docs.text: Every documented value works. Use flac or wav when fidelity matters, mp3/opus/aac to save bandwidth, and pcm only when the client wants to handle the container itself (and for streaming, §7).

docs.title: Sampling controls
docs.text: temperature, top_k, top_p and max_new_tokens are forwarded and accepted (verified live: HTTP 200 with top_k: 30, temperature: 0.8, max_new_tokens: 500). repetition_penalty is forwarded too, with the pod's own constraint that it must be exactly 1.0; anything else is a 400 naming the field (§8).

docs.title: 3. Every way to use it
docs.text:
One block per usage mode, all verified against production. Set these first:

KEY="Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>"
BASE=https://litellm.ecouncil.ae

docs.title: A. Basic synthesis, default voice
docs.text:
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3","input":"Hello there.","voice":"default","response_format":"wav"}' \
  -o out.wav

voice may be omitted entirely; response_format defaults to wav.

docs.title: B. Choose a container
docs.text: Swap response_format for mp3, flac, pcm, aac, or opus. Sizes for the same input are in §1.

docs.title: C. Control pace
docs.text: -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3","input":"Take your time with this.","voice":"default","speed":0.75}'

docs.title: D. Steer the delivery with direction tags
docs.text:
-d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3","voice":"default","input":"[sighs] Fine. If we miss it, it is on you. [laughs] Well, maybe that is fair."}'

Scoped tags (<whisper>...</whisper>), free-form prose directions ([with bright eager excitement]), and the Direction:/Line: split all work the same way. See §5.

docs.title: E. Tune sampling
docs.text:
-d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3","input":"Sampling probe.","voice":"default","top_k":30,"temperature":0.8,"top_p":0.9,"max_new_tokens":500}'

repetition_penalty must be exactly 1.0 if you send it at all.

docs.title: F. Stream audio
docs.text:
Requires pcm. Use -N so curl writes as it receives.

curl -sN -X POST "$BASE/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3","input":"A long line to stream.","voice":"default","stream":true,"response_format":"pcm"}' \
  -o out.pcm

Add "stream_format":"sse" for speech.audio.delta events.

docs.title: G. Clone a voice inline from a URL
docs.text: -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3","input":"Cloned from a URL.","voice":"default","references":[{"audio_path":"https://reachable.host/ref.wav","text":"Transcript of the reference."}]}'

docs.title: H. Clone a voice inline from base64 (no egress needed)
docs.text:
Preferred inside this cluster, which has no internet access. Write the body to a file; a ~1 MB base64 body inline on the command line hits Argument list too long.

base64 -w0 my_voice.wav > /tmp/b64.txt
python3 -c "
import json
b64=open('/tmp/b64.txt').read().strip()
json.dump({'model':'fishaudio/drama-3','input':'Cloned inline.','voice':'default',
           'references':[{'data':b64,'media_type':'audio/wav','text':'The transcript.'}]},
          open('/tmp/ref.json','w'))
"
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @/tmp/ref.json -o cloned.wav

docs.title: I. Register a reusable voice, then speak with it
docs.text:
Both the file field (ref_audio) and model are required, and model is what picks Drama 3 rather than another voice-capable pod.

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/audio/voices" -H "$KEY" \
  -F "model=fishaudio/drama-3" \
  -F "ref_audio=@my_voice.wav;type=audio/wav" \
  -F "consent=I have permission to use this voice." \
  -F "name=Narrator_01" \
  -F "ref_text=The transcript of my voice sample."

curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3","input":"Speaking as the registered voice.","voice":"Narrator_01"}' \
  -o out.wav

docs.title: J. Inspect and delete registered voices
docs.text:
# delete (body scopes it to Drama 3)
curl -s -X DELETE "$BASE/v1/voices/profiles/Narrator_01" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3"}'

# fetch one profile
curl -s "$BASE/v1/voices/profiles/Narrator_01" -H "$KEY"

# listing: explicit scope (drama3 registry incl. uploads)
curl -s "$BASE/v1/voices?model=fishaudio/drama-3" -H "$KEY"

# unscoped returns OmniVoice's catalogue (different shape; see Gateway endpoints)
curl -s "$BASE/v1/voices" -H "$KEY"

docs.title: K. Confirm the model is visible to your key
docs.text: curl -s "$BASE/v1/models" -H "$KEY" | grep -o 'fishaudio/drama-3'

docs.title: L. Batch synthesis (pod-direct only)
docs.text:
404 through the gateway; see §12 for the port-forward.

curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/audio/speech/batch \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items":[{"input":"one","voice":"default"},{"input":"two","voice":"default"}]}'

docs.title: Production verification summary
docs.text:
Every mode above was run against https://litellm.ecouncil.ae with a key_type=llm_api virtual key:

Mode Result A basic wav 200, 73,772 B, RIFF B all six formats 200 each, correct magic C speed 0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0 200, 499,756 / 241,708 / 139,308 B D direction tags 200, 9.85 s vs 6.22 s untagged E sampling 200 F streaming pcm 200, TTFB 0.41 s vs total 1.34 s G inline URL clone 400 on unreachable host (forwarding proven), 200 on reachable H inline base64 clone 200, 208,940 B, RIFF I register + speak 200 upload, 200 speech at 44.1 kHz J delete + probe 200 delete, 400 on the deleted voice K /v1/models model listed for the key L batch 404 via gateway (pod-direct only) scoping ?model=fishaudio/drama-3 drama3 registry: string voices + uploaded_voices + cache_stats unscoped fallback OmniVoice catalogue (auto / design:<attributes> / preset / clone:* objects)

docs.title: 4. The forwarding contract
docs.text:
Drama 3 is registered with a provider-specific TTS config (litellm/llms/drama3/), so the gateway no longer routes it through the OpenAI TTS branch. The provider transformation forwards the model, input, voice, response_format, speed, and every Drama 3 schema field (references, sampling controls, stream, stream_format) to the pod, and filters out only LiteLLM's own internal kwargs (model resolution, routing, logging).

The observable consequence: the pod's validation reaches you intact. A field the pod rejects produces a 400 through the gateway, and a field the pod accepts changes the audio.

docs.title: How this was verified
docs.text:
Probe with a value the pod rejects; if the pod's error comes back through the gateway, the field arrived. All of these were run through the gateway and returned the pod's own 400:

Request Through the gateway references at https://example.invalid/nope.wav 400 Could not resolve media URL hostname: example.invalid repetition_penalty: 1.5 400 Drama 3 request: repetition_penalty must be 1.0 task_type: "VoiceDesign" 400 only Base is seed: 42 400 seed not supported language: "English" 400 language not supported instructions: "whisper" 400 instructions is not supported by this model stream: true with response_format: "wav" 400 stream=true requires response_format='pcm'

Before the provider slice existed, every row except instructions returned 200 with valid default-voice audio: the gateway silently dropped the field. That is the failure mode the sentinel method detects, and the one this contract now prevents.

Fields the pod refuses outright with unknown speech request field are likewise forwarded, so a misspelled field name fails loudly on both sides of the gateway instead of being swallowed.

docs.title: Streaming, measured
docs.text:
stream: true with response_format: "pcm" delivers incrementally. Measured on production:

Input length TTFB Total Size one word (Hi.) 0.41 s 0.53 s 72 KB one sentence 0.40 s 1.34 s 564 KB

Time to first byte stays flat around 0.4 s while the total grows with the audio, so audio reaches the client while generation continues. A buffered response would show TTFB growing alongside the total. Note that transfer-encoding: chunked is not present in the captured headers: the proxy streams through StreamingResponse with an explicit status and no Content-Length, so chunking is implicit in HTTP/1.1 rather than advertised. Judge streaming by TTFB behaviour, not by that header.

The stream_format field rides along too (audio for raw PCM passthrough, sse for speech.audio.delta events terminated by speech.audio.done).

docs.title: The mechanism
docs.text: speech() builds its OpenAI-branch body from exactly three optional parameters (response_format, speed, instructions). Everything else a client sends arrives as **kwargs. The drama3 transformation class declares the Drama 3 schema fields as forwardable and additionally filters LiteLLM's own kwargs with the canonical is_litellm_owned_kwarg predicate, so router-injected parameters (deployment settings, keepalive overrides) cannot leak into the pod body either. The dispatch tail in litellm/main.py routes drama3 to the generic HTTP handler with this config.

docs.title: 5. Direction tags and script control
docs.text: Rich, and it works through the gateway. The model interprets bracketed directions inline in the text; there is no fixed schema, so these are the forms worth using rather than an exhaustive list.

docs.title: Point tags
docs.text:
Inserted where the event should land:

[laughs] [chuckles] [sighs] [gasps] [pause] [clears throat] [hesitates]

docs.title: Scoped tags
docs.text:
Wrap the span they apply to. These use angle brackets:

Promise me <whisper>you won't tell her</whisper>. [pause] Not a word.

<slow> and <emphasis> work the same way.

docs.title: Free-form style directions
docs.text:
Bracketed prose, describing delivery rather than a named tag:

[with bright eager excitement] We won! We actually won! [laughs] I can't believe it!
[breathless, rising excitement] He's past one... past two... he shoots, and [shouting] HE SCORES!

docs.title: Direction and Line
docs.text:
For richer scenes, split the direction from the spoken text. This is how the upstream Drama 3 Space lets you steer a take without polluting the audio:

Direction: icy calm, as if you already accepted it. Put the rise on "goodbye".
Line: So this is goodbye.

Verification that tags are performed rather than read aloud, measured through the gateway on the same sentence with and without tags:

Input Audio duration [sighs] Fine. If we miss it, it is on you. [laughs] Well, maybe that is fair. 8.73 - 9.85 s Fine. If we miss it, it is on you. Well, maybe that is fair. 6.22 - 7.80 s

Reproduced on production (9.85 s tagged vs 6.22 s plain for one pair), so the tags add roughly 2-3 s of non-speech audio while the wording is identical: the sigh and the laugh are performed. Compare durations as ranges rather than absolute values, because generation length varies between runs. The comparison is the evidence.

docs.title: 6. Voice cloning and voice management
docs.text: Both exist and both work through the gateway. Inline cloning rides the speech request (references); persistent voices ride the gateway's voice-management routes, which forward to the pod's own registry.

docs.title: Inline cloning with references
docs.text:
Top-level references is a sibling of input, not a field inside it. input stays a plain string; this is the single most common mistake, and it fails with 400 input must be a string.

Each reference supplies the audio and its transcript. Three source forms are accepted:

Form Field HTTP(S) URL or pod-local path audio_path Inline base64 data (or base64) plus media_type Pre-encoded codes vq_codes, skipping the encode step entirely 
curl -s "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "fishaudio/drama-3",
    "input": "Get the trust fund to the bank early.",
    "references": [{
      "audio_path": "https://example.com/prompt.wav",
      "text": "We asked over twenty different people, and they all said it was his."
    }],
    "response_format": "wav"
  }' -o cloned.wav

Verified live through the gateway: an unresolvable reference URL returns the pod's own 400 Could not resolve media URL hostname, which proves the field is forwarded. A resolvable reference clones the voice.

Use inline base64 when the pod has no egress. The cluster has no internet access, so public dataset URLs (Hugging Face and similar) either 404 or hang inside the pod. Base64 sidesteps the fetch entirely, because the audio arrives in the request body:

KEY="Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>"
B64=$(base64 -w0 my_voice.wav)

python3 - <<'PY'
import json, os
b64 = open("/tmp/b64.txt").read().strip()
body = {
    "model": "fishaudio/drama-3",
    "input": "Cloned inline without any upload.",
    "voice": "default",
    "references": [{
        "data": b64,
        "media_type": "audio/wav",
        "text": "The transcript of the reference clip.",
    }],
}
open("/tmp/ref.json", "w").write(json.dumps(body))
PY

curl -s -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @/tmp/ref.json -o cloned.wav

Verified on production: a ~1 MB base64 body (a 775 KB wav) returned 200 with 44.1 kHz mono RIFF audio. Write the JSON to a file and use --data-binary @file; a 1 MB body inline on the command line hits Argument list too long.

Reference limits, all enforced before encoding:

Limit Value Error Per-reference duration 60 s reference audio lasts 75.0 s, longer than the 60 s limit Prompt rows 8192 (about 21.5 rows per second of reference audio) a prompt of 8193 rows exceeds the maximum allowed length

The 60 s cap is raised at server start with --preprocessing.factory.max_reference_audio_seconds, which also needs a matching --preprocessing.total_reserve_bytes or the preprocessing stage runs out of GPU memory.

docs.title: Persistent voices through the gateway
docs.text:
The pod has a full voice registry, and the gateway's voice-management routes now proxy it. Two details decide whether the call targets Drama 3 or the wrong pod:

  • the file field is named ref_audio (the gateway forwards it to the pod as audio_sample), and sending audio_sample instead fails with 'ref_audio' is required for Drama 3 voice registration
  • the model must ride model= as a form field on the upload. Without it the router picks the first voice-capable deployment. After the DB row's prefix was reconciled to drama3/ that fallback is Drama 3 itself, so omitting model= now lands on the right pod — keep the field anyway, because it is the load-bearing wire the gateway uses to disambiguate uploads between voice-capable deployments
KEY="Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>"
BASE=https://litellm.ecouncil.ae

# upload (multipart) -- note: ref_audio + model as form fields
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/audio/voices" \
  -H "$KEY" \
  -F "model=fishaudio/drama-3" \
  -F "ref_audio=@my_voice.wav;type=audio/wav" \
  -F "consent=I have permission to use this voice." \
  -F "name=Narrator_01" \
  -F "ref_text=A sample reference transcript."

# use it by name
curl -s -X POST "$BASE/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3","input":"Speaking with the uploaded voice.","voice":"Narrator_01"}' \
  -o out.wav

# delete -- the body is what scopes this to Drama 3
curl -s -X DELETE "$BASE/v1/voices/profiles/Narrator_01" \
  -H "$KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3"}'

Verified end to end on production:

Step Result upload 200 with {"name","consent","created_at","file_size","mime_type","ref_text"}, model_id = the Drama 3 row speech naming the voice 200, audio/wav, 44.1 kHz mono, 3.02 s delete 200 {"success":true,"message":"Voice 'Narrator_01' deleted successfully"} speech naming the deleted voice 400 unknown voice (proof the delete took effect)

The delete response is also how you can confirm which model handled the call: its _hidden_params names the model group, and the speech probe above is the authoritative check that the registry actually lost the voice.

The list response for Drama 3 itself carries voices, uploaded_voices, and cache_stats; parse those rather than the OpenAI-shaped profile contract. See the caveat in Gateway endpoints about reaching that listing with a GET.

Upload constraints (enforced by the pod):

Constraint Value Duration 1 s to 30 s, mono, non-silent Max voices 1000 (SPEAKER_MAX_UPLOADED) Name [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+, at least one alphanumeric, default is reserved Formats wav, mp3, flac, ogg, opus, aac, m4a/mp4, webm consent Required, no default

Uploaded voices persist across restarts as safetensors files under ~/.cache/sglang-omni/speakers, so a restartPolicy-driven pod restart keeps them and a pod replacement does not.

Any other unregistered voice name reaches the pod and is rejected:

{"error":{"message":"litellm.BadRequestError: Drama3Exception - {\"error\":{\"message\":\"Drama 3 request: unknown voice 'alloy'; use default or an uploaded voice\",\"type\":\"BadRequestError\",\"param\":null,\"code\":400}} ..."}}

Omitting voice entirely is fine; the request synthesizes with the default voice.

docs.title: 7. Sampling parameters and limits
docs.text:
Parameter Default Notes temperature 1.0 Forwarded top_p 0.9 Forwarded top_k no cap on the main token The codebook heads cap at 30 regardless, because wider caps cost speaker similarity. A main-token cap of 30 makes a stream fall silent after its first phrase max_new_tokens model default Forwarded repetition_penalty 1.0 Forwarded. Must be 1.0; anything else is a 400 speed 1.0 0.25 to 4.0

Rejected outright, with the pod naming the field: seed, language, instructions, task_type other than Base, x_vector_only_mode, stream_codec_output, suppress_bootstrap_silence, token_count, duration_tokens, initial_codec_chunk_frames, stage_params.

seed being unsupported is worth noting for anyone hoping to make takes reproducible: they cannot be, at the request level.

docs.title: Multi-speaker is not available
docs.text:
Drama 3 can carry up to 16 characters (<|speaker:0|> to <|speaker:15|>), and the prompt builder handles all of them, but the HTTP request path hard-restricts to speaker 0:

{"error":{"message":"Drama 3 request: only speaker 0 is supported; got speaker tags [1]"}}

This is a code restriction in speech_request.py, not a config knob, so a multi-character scene needs one request per character and then concatenation.

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
Works through the gateway. Requires response_format: "pcm"; a wav container states a total length and cannot be cut into chunks, and the pod rejects the combination outright. stream_format selects the envelope:

# raw PCM passthrough (default)
curl -sN -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3","input":"...","stream":true,"response_format":"pcm"}' \
  -o out.pcm

# SSE events
curl -sN -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"fishaudio/drama-3","input":"...","stream":true,"stream_format":"sse","response_format":"pcm"}'

SSE events are {"type": "speech.audio.delta", "audio": "<base64>"} terminated by a speech.audio.done event.

Beyond /v1/audio/speech, the pod also exposes POST /v1/audio/speech/batch for multiple inputs in one request (verified working pod-direct, max 32 items by default) and a stateful WS /v1/audio/speech/stream. Neither is proxied by the gateway (POST /v1/audio/speech/batch through the gateway is a 404), so batch remains pod-direct.

docs.title: 8. Error contracts (verified live)
docs.text:
All rows below were reproduced against the production gateway with a key_type=llm_api virtual key. Error text is the pod's own, wrapped in Drama3Exception.

Case HTTP Body Missing or invalid gateway key 401 Authentication Error, No api key passed in. Key without the route in its allowed_routes 403 Virtual key is not allowed to call this route. ... model omitted 400 {"detail":{"error":"/audio/speech: Invalid model name passed in model=. Call \/v1/models` to view available models for your key."}}` voice unregistered (e.g. alloy on Drama 3) 400 Drama 3 request: unknown voice 'alloy'; use default or an uploaded voice input is an object rather than a string 400 input must be a string repetition_penalty other than 1.0 400 Drama 3 request: repetition_penalty must be 1.0; got 1.5 instructions set 400 instructions is not supported by this model seed set 400 seed is not supported by this model language set 400 language is not supported by this model Unknown field (e.g. bogus_field) 400 unknown speech request field: bogus_field stream: true without response_format: "pcm" 400 Drama 3 request: stream=true requires response_format='pcm' Unresolvable references URL 400 Could not resolve media URL hostname: example.invalid (param: references.audio_path) Reference longer than 60 s 400 references.N: reference audio lasts X s, longer than the 60 s limit Speaker tag other than 0 400 Drama 3 request: only speaker 0 is supported; got speaker tags [...] Upload without the audio file 400 'ref_audio' is required for Drama 3 voice registration. Provide the reference audio file. Upload with audio_sample instead of ref_audio 400 same as above (the gateway reads ref_audio) POST /v1/audio/speech/batch 404 {"detail":"Not Found"} (route not proxied) GET /v1/audio/voices 405 {"detail":"Method Not Allowed"} (use GET /v1/voices) GET /v1/audio/health, /v1/audio/metrics 403 ops-only routes, not on the llm_api allowlist DELETE /v1/audio/voices/{name} 404 {"detail":"Not Found"} (use DELETE /v1/voices/profiles/{name})

Per-field validation errors pass through with the pod's original message intact inside error.message, wrapped in Drama3Exception. Unlike the diarize route there is no unwrapping to a spec-shaped body, so read the text inside the wrapper. The trailing LiteLLM: model group ... no fallback model group was found sentence is router noise appended to every 4xx; the pod's message is the part before it.

Batch (POST /v1/audio/speech/batch) is 404 through the gateway. It exists on the pod but no gateway route proxies it, so batching stays pod-direct (§12).

docs.title: 9. Mode
docs.text:
The deployment registers as mode: audio_speech with oicm_task: Text-to-Speech and health_check_voice: default. This was not always the case: before 2026-11-03 it registered as chat, because the controller classified any pod whose openapi.json exposes /v1/chat/completions as a chat model and this sglang-omni pod exposes that path.

The fix came from OICM's declared inference_task, which the operator sets at deploy time, gated on the pod actually mounting the task's native surface. This pod declares Text-to-Speech and mounts /v1/audio/speech, so the declaration wins. A pod that declares a non-chat task but does not mount its surface keeps the mounted mode, with the declaration preserved as model_info.oicm_task. See CAPABILITY_REGISTRATION_REVIEW2.md.

Consequences for callers:

  • POST /v1/audio/speech is the correct route, as documented throughout this guide.
  • POST /v1/chat/completions with this model no longer reaches the pod: the gateway's chat path resolves the drama3 provider, which has no chat config, and returns Unmapped LLM provider for this endpoint. You passed model=fishaudio/drama-3, custom_llm_provider=drama3. Use the speech route.
  • Anything that groups models by declared mode now classifies this model as a speech model.

docs.title: 10. Performance
docs.text:
Measured on the Al Ain H200 through the gateway, single request, serial:

Input Output audio Wall time Notes 25 chars (Hello, how are you today?) 1.67-2.18 s 0.72-0.84 s Three runs; length varies per generation 52 chars (speed: 1.0) 3.30 s ~1.1 s Same at speed: 2.0 1.53 s ~1.1 s 1,220 chars 95.11 s 15.1 s ~6.3x faster than realtime

Generation length varies between identical requests, so compare durations as ranges rather than exact values. The pod's own benchmark notes (single H200, default placement) report 88.9 ms TTFA at concurrency 1 and 927 frames/s at concurrency 16. Non-streaming requests through the gateway return all audio at once once generation finishes; use stream: true with response_format: "pcm" (§7) when time to first audio matters.

docs.title: 11. Route/field notes for clients
docs.text:
• model: "fishaudio/drama-3" is mandatory on every route that reads a body; omission is not defaulted.
  • voice is optional and defaults to the default voice. Register a voice first (§6) to use a custom one; unregistered names are rejected by the pod.
  • Read the sample rate from the WAV header; do not assume 24 kHz.
  • Direction tags ([laughs], <whisper>, Direction:/Line:) work through the gateway because they ride inside input (§5).
  • stream: true works but needs response_format: "pcm"; the pod rejects it with a container format. Judge streaming by flat TTFB, not by a chunked header.
  • references clones inline (§6). With no cluster egress, prefer inline base64 data over a URL, or upload the voice once.
  • input must be a string. Putting references or takes inside it fails with input must be a string.
  • Sampling controls (temperature, top_k, top_p, max_new_tokens) are forwarded; repetition_penalty must stay 1.0.
  • Unknown fields fail with unknown speech request field, so there is no silent dropping to rely on or be surprised by.
  • Voice upload needs both ref_audio (the file field) and model=fishaudio/drama-3 (a form field). Miss model and the voice lands in another provider's registry.
  • GET /v1/voices cannot be scoped with ?model=; the gateway ignores the query string, so it answers with whichever voice-capable deployment the router picks first. Use a body-bearing call to target Drama 3 (§6).
  • Batch (POST /v1/audio/speech/batch) is 404 through the gateway; it stays pod-direct (§12).
  • Spend logging: like the other audio-slice routes, this path does not write LiteLLM spend rows, so usage tracking for TTS is not available yet.

docs.title: 12. Pod-direct access
docs.text:
Useful for the two things the gateway does not proxy: batch synthesis and the GET /v1/audio/voices listing that the gateway cannot model-scope.

# find the Drama 3 pod (name is the OICM deployment uuid)
kubectl -n adeo get pods | grep -i drama

# forward its HTTP port
kubectl -n adeo port-forward deploy/<drama3-deployment> 8080:8080

# now the pod's own surface is directly reachable
curl -s http://localhost:8080/v1/audio/voices
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/v1/audio/speech/batch \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"items":[{"input":"one","voice":"default"},{"input":"two","voice":"default"}]}'

The pod requires no authentication, so a port-forward or an in-cluster client is enough. Requests sent this way bypass routing, auth, guardrails, and spend logging; use it for debugging and for the two routes above, not as a production path.

docs.title: Deployment-side reference
docs.text:
The serving-side tuning doc (flags, concurrency tables, int4 checkpoint, sampling defaults, hard constraints such as the mandatory triton attention backend) lives outside this repo:

mlops/oicm-custom-model-server-guide/docs/sglang/fishaudio-drama3.md

One of its claims is worth knowing before you debug a request through the gateway:

  • Its stream: true examples require response_format: "pcm". That requirement holds through the gateway too: the pod enforces it and the field is forwarded, so a stream request with wav fails on both sides rather than being silently downgraded.

The authoritative upstream sources are the SGLang-Omni cookbook (docs/cookbook/fishaudio_drama3.md in sglang-omni, pinned at tag v0.2.0, the version this pod runs) and sglang_omni/models/fishaudio_drama3/speech_request.py, which holds the exact accepted and rejected field list this guide's §4 and §7 are derived from.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The LiteLLM gateway provides a unified OpenAI-compatible API for accessing Hamsa TTS, Hamsa STT, LLM chat completions, and embedding models. All requests go through a single endpoint with a single API key.

Gateway URL: https://litellm.ecouncil.ae

API Key: <YOUR_API_KEY> (replace everywhere below with your LiteLLM gateway API key; sk-...)

All requests use the Authorization: Bearer <api_key> header unless otherwise noted.

docs.title: Available Models
docs.text:
The gateway serves 27 models; this key is scoped to the 12 below. GET /v1/models with this key returns exactly this set.

Model Type Description hamsa-tts-new Text-to-Speech Arabic/English TTS, 113 bundled + 12 cloned ADEO voices. See HAMSA-TTS-NEW-V1-GUIDE.md hamsa-stt Speech-to-Text Arabic STT (REST + WebSocket realtime) inception-tts Text-to-Speech Inception TTS inception-stt Speech-to-Text Inception STT Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct LLM Chat 80B parameter instruct model Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-GPTQ-Int4 LLM Chat 122B reasoning model (outputs reasoning_content) Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 LLM Chat 35B reasoning model (outputs reasoning_content) Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 LLM Chat Flash reasoning model (outputs reasoning_content) deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 LLM Chat DeepSeek V4 Flash reasoning model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash LLM Chat DeepSeek V4.1 Flash reasoning model Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-4B Embeddings 2560-dimensional embeddings Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B Embeddings 1024-dimensional embeddings

hamsa-tts (the original TTS deployment) is retired and removed from the gateway: its backend Service no longer exists, and its model row was deleted on dev and prod, so /v1/audio/speech now rejects it with HTTP 400 "Invalid model name". Use hamsa-tts-new. hamsa-stt is unaffected.

docs.title: Reasoning Models
docs.text:
Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-GPTQ-Int4, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8, Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, and deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash are reasoning models. They produce output in two fields:

  • reasoning_content: the chain-of-thought (not shown to end users)
  • content: the final answer

These models need a higher max_tokens (e.g. 1000+) because reasoning tokens count toward the limit. With max_tokens=50 the model may exhaust tokens on reasoning alone and return content: null.

See Reasoning Control Guide for per-model reasoning_effort tiers and how to disable thinking.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The original hamsa-tts examples that used dialect and mulaw are retired with the model. The working equivalents use hamsa-tts-new:

Arabic TTS (WAV)

curl -s -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "hamsa-tts-new",
    "input": "مرحبا بك في اختبار تحويل النص إلى كلام",
    "voice": "Zeina",
    "response_format": "wav"
  }' \
  -o output.wav

English TTS (WAV)

curl -s -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "hamsa-tts-new",
    "input": "Hello, welcome to the text to speech test.",
    "voice": "Amir",
    "response_format": "wav"
  }' \
  -o output_en.wav

For streaming, cloned ADEO voices, and the full 113-speaker list, see HAMSA-TTS-NEW-V1-GUIDE.md.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: Binary audio data with Content-Type: audio/wav. For hamsa-tts-new, the audio is 16kHz mono 16-bit PCM when response_format=wav, or raw headerless 16-bit 16kHz mono PCM when response_format=pcm with stream: true.

docs.title: 2. Voice Management
docs.text:
Unavailable. Voice management targets hamsa-tts, which is retired: its backend Service no longer exists. POST /v1/audio/voices therefore cannot work today, independently of the read-only-rootfs bug documented below. The content in this section is kept as a record of the retired contract.

Cloned voices on the active model are already provisioned: hamsa-tts-new ships 12 ADEO cloned voices (the adeo_-prefixed names) alongside 113 bundled speakers. Pass them directly in the voice field. See HAMSA-TTS-NEW-V1-GUIDE.md.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
POST /v1/audio/voices

Voice cloning is a two-step process:

Step 1 - Extract tokens (action: "register"): Pass an audio URL and transcript. The Hamsa backend downloads the audio and runs it through the BiCodecTokenizer to extract global_token_ids and semantic_token_ids.

Step 2 - Load tokens (action: "load"): Pass the extracted tokens with a speaker_id to register the voice in the model's in-memory speaker dictionary. After loading, the voice is immediately usable in /v1/audio/speech.

docs.title: Request Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description model string Yes Must be hamsa-tts action string No register (default) or load speaker_id string Yes (for load) Name for the new voice audio_url string Yes (for register) URL to the reference audio file prompt_text string Yes (for register) Transcript of the reference audio global_token_ids array Yes (for load) Global token arrays from step 1 semantic_token_ids array Yes (for load) Semantic token arrays from step 1 dialect string No msa, ksa, or eng (default: msa)

docs.title: Known Limitation: Step 1 (register) is Currently Broken
docs.text:
The Hamsa TTS pod runs with a read-only root filesystem. Step 1 (action: "register") calls download_file() internally, which tries to create a ref_audios/ directory in /app (the working directory) to save the downloaded audio. This fails with:

OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system: 'ref_audios'

Verified by calling the endpoint through the gateway:

curl -sk -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/voices" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "hamsa-tts",
    "action": "register",
    "audio_url": "https://example.com/reference.wav",
    "prompt_text": "This is the transcript of the reference audio."
  }'
# Returns: HTTP 500 Internal Server Error

Pod logs confirm the error:

File "/app/app/hamsaTTS.py", line 1094, in download_file
    os.makedirs(folder, exist_ok=True)
OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system: 'ref_audios'

The pod does have writable directories (/app/output, /app/download, /tmp), but the Hamsa download_file method uses a hardcoded relative path (ref_audios) instead of one of these. This is a bug in the Hamsa TTS service, not in the LiteLLM gateway.

Workaround: Extract voice tokens manually by exec'ing into the pod, then use action: "load" (step 2) through the gateway to register the voice. See the next section for a worked example.

docs.title: Example: Extract Tokens Manually (Workaround for Step 1)
docs.text:
Exec into the TTS pod and run token extraction directly, writing to the writable /app/output directory:

# 1. Download reference audio into the pod's writable directory
KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl cp reference.wav \
  adeo/j-cd2850fc-5870-4a57-89da-5e978eee66f4-67766948c-rhwn2:/app/output/reference.wav

# 2. Exec into the pod and extract tokens
KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl exec -n adeo \
  j-cd2850fc-5870-4a57-89da-5e978eee66f4-67766948c-rhwn2 -- \
  python3 -c "
import torch, json
from app.hamsaTTS import hamsaTTS
model = hamsaTTS()
model._initialize_inference()
model.load_speakers_from_directory('speakers/')
global_ids, semantic_ids = model.audio_tokenizer.tokenize('/app/output/reference.wav')
tokens = {
    'global_token_ids': global_ids.tolist(),
    'semantic_token_ids': semantic_ids.tolist(),
}
with open('/app/output/tokens.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(tokens, f)
print('Tokens saved to /app/output/tokens.json')
print(f'global_token_ids shape: {len(global_ids)}')
print(f'semantic_token_ids shape: {len(semantic_ids)}')
"

# 3. Copy the tokens back to your machine
KUBECONFIG=$HOME/.kube/oicm-alain.conf kubectl cp \
  adeo/j-cd2850fc-5870-4a57-89da-5e978eee66f4-67766948c-rhwn2:/app/output/tokens.json \
  ./tokens.json

docs.title: Example: Load a Cloned Voice (Step 2)
docs.text:
Once you have the extracted tokens, register the voice through the gateway:

curl -sk -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/voices" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "hamsa-tts",
    "action": "load",
    "speaker_id": "my_custom_voice",
    "global_token_ids": [[2835, 1337, 574, 3897, 305, 1557, 1106, 58, 3449, 3190]],
    "semantic_token_ids": [[4934, 4577, 5060, 5288, 7108, 3210, 4001, 1234, 5678, 9012]],
    "dialect": "ksa",
    "prompt_text": "Reference transcript"
  }'

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{"voice_id": "", "status": "registered"}

After loading, the new voice is immediately usable in /v1/audio/speech by passing "voice": "my_custom_voice". Verified:

curl -sk -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "hamsa-tts",
    "input": "مرحبا، هذا اختبار للصوت المستنسخ",
    "voice": "my_custom_voice"
  }' \
  -o cloned_tts.wav
# Returns: HTTP 200, 117KB WAV

Note: Custom voices exist only in the model's in-memory state. If the TTS pod restarts, custom voices are lost and must be re-loaded.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: POST /v1/audio/transcriptions

docs.title: Request Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Required Description model string Yes Must be hamsa-stt file file Yes Audio file (PCM 16kHz 16-bit WAV recommended) language string No Language code (default: auto)

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
curl -sk -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/transcriptions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -F "model=hamsa-stt" \
  -F "file=@audio.wav" \
  -F "language=auto"

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{
  "text": "مرحبا بك في اختبار تحويل النص إلى كلام",
  "gender": "Male",
  "eos": {"prediction": 1},
  "processing_time": 0.58,
  "duration": 2.1,
  "speaker_embeddings": [...],
  "wake_word_match": null
}

docs.title: Audio Format Requirements
docs.text:
The STT service expects PCM 16kHz 16-bit mono WAV files. Mu-law encoded WAV files will fail with "buffer size must be a multiple of element size". If you have mu-law audio, convert it first:

ffmpeg -i input_mulaw.wav -ar 16000 -ac 1 -sample_fmt s16 output_pcm.wav

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
wss://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/realtime?model=hamsa-stt

The WebSocket connection enables real-time streaming transcription from a microphone or audio stream.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
Browsers cannot set custom headers on WebSocket connections, so the API key is passed via the sec-websocket-protocol subprotocol:

const ws = new WebSocket(
  "wss://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/realtime?model=hamsa-stt",
  ["openai-insecure-api-key.<YOUR_API_KEY>"]
);

docs.title: Protocol
docs.text:
1. Client sends handshake (JSON) after connection opens:
{
  "type": "handshake",
  "api_key": "<HAMSA_STT_FERNET_TOKEN>",
  "authorization": "Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>",
  "options": {
    "silence_timeout": 30,
    "sample_rate": 16000,
    "min_silence_duration_ms": 300,
    "min_speech_ms": 600,
    "client_logging": true,
    "vad_threshold": 0.6,
    "eos_enabled": true,
    "eos_threshold": 0.6,
    "audio_type": "PCM",
    "noise_cancellation": false
  }
}

The api_key field is the Hamsa STT encrypted key (Fernet token). The authorization field is the LiteLLM gateway API key.

  1. Server responds with handshake acknowledgment:
{"type": "handshake_ack"}

  1. Client streams audio as binary PCM data (16kHz, 16-bit, mono, little-endian). Send Int16Array buffers from the microphone.

  2. Server sends transcription results:

{
  "type": "transcription",
  "duration_ms": 2500,
  "data": {
    "transcription": "مرحبا بك في اختبار تحويل النص إلى كلام",
    "gender": "Male",
    "eos": {"prediction": 1}
  }
}
  1. Server may send log messages:
{"type": "log", "data": "VAD detected speech start"}
  1. Server may send errors:
{"type": "error", "error": "Invalid audio format"}

docs.title: WebSocket Options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description silence_timeout float 30 Seconds of silence before auto-disconnect sample_rate int 16000 Audio sample rate (must be 16000) min_silence_duration_ms int 300 Minimum silence to trigger end-of-utterance min_speech_ms int 600 Minimum speech duration before processing client_logging bool true Enable server-side logging vad_threshold float 0.6 Voice activity detection sensitivity (0.1-0.99) eos_enabled bool true Enable end-of-speech detection eos_threshold float 0.6 End-of-speech detection threshold (0.1-0.99) audio_type string "PCM" Audio encoding type noise_cancellation bool false Enable noise cancellation

docs.title: Interactive Test Page
docs.text:
An interactive WebSocket test page is available at hamsa-stt-realtime-test-ws.html in this directory. To use it:

cd oicm-litellm-layer/examples/usage/hamsa-stt
python3 -m http.server 8765

Then open http://localhost:8765/hamsa-stt-realtime-test-ws.html in a browser. The page is pre-configured with the correct gateway URL, API keys, and default options. Click "Connect & Start Recording" to begin streaming microphone audio for real-time transcription.

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text:
POST /v1/chat/completions

Standard OpenAI-compatible chat completions API.

docs.title: Example: Standard Model
docs.text:
curl -sk -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in Arabic and English."}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 100
  }'

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{
  "id": "chatcmpl-...",
  "model": "Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct",
  "choices": [
    {
      "message": {
        "role": "assistant",
        "content": "Hello in Arabic: مرحبًا\nHello in English: Hello"
      },
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    }
  ],
  "usage": {
    "completion_tokens": 14,
    "prompt_tokens": 19,
    "total_tokens": 33
  }
}

docs.title: Example: Reasoning Model
docs.text:
Reasoning models (Qwen3.5-122B, Qwen3.6-35B, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) produce a reasoning_content field in addition to content. Use a higher max_tokens:

curl -sk -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "What is 2+2?"}
    ],
    "max_tokens": 500
  }'

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
{
  "choices": [
    {
      "message": {
        "role": "assistant",
        "reasoning_content": "The user is asking a simple math question...",
        "content": "Four"
      },
      "finish_reason": "stop"
    }
  ]
}

If max_tokens is too low, the model exhausts tokens on reasoning and returns "content": null with "finish_reason": "length".

docs.title: Disabling Reasoning
docs.text:
To skip chain-of-thought for faster, cheaper responses, pass the disable-reasoning parameter for the model family in use:

  • Qwen (vLLM) — chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}
  • DeepSeek — thinking: false

For SGLang-served reasoning models the reliable switch is the top-level reasoning_effort: "none"; see Reasoning Control Guide.

Qwen example:

curl -s -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-GPTQ-Int4",
    "messages": [
      {"role": "user", "content": "Say hello in one word."}
    ],
    "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false},
    "max_tokens": 500
  }'

docs.title: Available LLM Models
docs.text: Model Type Notes Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct Standard Best for general chat, fast response Qwen/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-GPTQ-Int4 Reasoning Large model, needs high max_tokens Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 Reasoning Mid-size, needs high max_tokens Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8 Reasoning Flash model, needs high max_tokens deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 Reasoning DeepSeek V4 Flash deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Reasoning DeepSeek V4.1 Flash

docs.title: Hamsa TTS New: /v1 Endpoint Guide
docs.text:
Scope: How to call hamsa-tts-new text-to-speech through the LiteLLM gateway, with sample curl commands and expected response shapes

Related docs: HAMSA_STT_GUIDE.md (hamsa-stt usage), GATEWAY_GUIDE.md (gateway overview)

This is the active Hamsa TTS model. The original hamsa-tts deployment is retired and removed from the gateway: its backend Service no longer exists and its model row was deleted on dev and prod, so requests for it now fail with HTTP 400 "Invalid model name" (verified 2026-10-21). Use hamsa-tts-new.

Gateway URL: https://litellm.ecouncil.ae (valid DigiCert wildcard *.ecouncil.ae cert; curl -k is not required)

API Key: replace <your-api-key> everywhere below with your LiteLLM gateway API key. All requests use the Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key> header.

Model: hamsa-tts-new

Verified: 2026-10-21

docs.title: Gateway endpoints
docs.text:
The gateway supports two /v1 endpoints for this model:

Endpoint Method Purpose /v1/models GET List available models /v1/audio/speech POST Synthesize speech (WAV)

No other /v1 endpoints (voices, voice-clone, status, ...) are exposed on the gateway.

docs.title: List models
docs.text:
curl -sk "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/models" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>"

Response (trimmed):

{
  "object": "list",
  "data": [
    { "id": "hamsa-tts-new", "object": "model", "owned_by": "ADEO" }
  ]
}

docs.title: Endpoint
docs.text: POST /v1/audio/speech

docs.title: Request shape
docs.text:
Returns WAV audio (16-bit mono 16 kHz PCM). Save the binary response to a file because the response body is raw audio, not JSON.

Field Required Default Notes model yes Must be hamsa-tts-new input yes Text to synthesize (Arabic or English) voice yes Speaker name — see voice list below response_format no wav wav or pcm (with stream) speed no 1.0 0.5 – 2.0 expressiveness no 1.0 0.0 – 2.0 stream no false true returns raw headerless 16-bit 16 kHz mono PCM, delivered in chunks as synthesis proceeds (first chunk in ~300 ms). Send response_format: "pcm" so the gateway labels the body audio/pcm

docs.title: Sample curl
docs.text:
curl -sk -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "hamsa-tts-new",
    "input": "مرحبا بكم في مجلس أبوظبي",
    "voice": "Zeina",
    "response_format": "wav"
  }' \
  -o speech.wav

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
Binary audio with Content-Type: audio/wav. Verified result:

HTTP 200 — speech.wav: RIFF (little-endian) data, WAVE audio,
Microsoft PCM, 16 bit, mono 16000 Hz

Note: the WAV header contains 0xFFFFFFFF in the RIFF/data size fields (streaming-style header from the backend). ffprobe, file and audio players read it fine, but Python's built-in wave module misreports the duration. If you need exact size, trust the file length, not the header.

docs.title: Streaming (low-latency playback)
docs.text:
"stream": true makes the backend synthesize and ship audio in chunks: the first bytes arrive in ~300 ms instead of at the end of synthesis, and the body is raw 16-bit PCM, 16 kHz mono, with no WAV header. The gateway relays the chunks as they arrive (Content-Type: audio/pcm when you also send "response_format": "pcm").

curl -sk -N -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "hamsa-tts-new",
    "input": "مرحبا بكم في مجلس أبوظبي",
    "voice": "Zeina",
    "response_format": "pcm",
    "stream": true
  }' \
  -o speech.pcm

Measure the first-byte latency with curl -w (expect time_starttransfer well below time_total, roughly 0.3 s on a multi-second synthesis):

curl -sk -N -o /dev/null -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"hamsa-tts-new","input":"...","voice":"Zeina","response_format":"pcm","stream":true}' \
  -w "TTFB=%{time_starttransfer}s TOTAL=%{time_total}s\n"

docs.title: More examples
docs.text:
Different voice:

curl -sk -X POST "https://litellm.ecouncil.ae/v1/audio/speech" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <your-api-key>" \
